Crop speed) * Sunshower (2x Crop speed) ## Calendar An in-game calendar is provided to help you keep track of which season is currently active, and which are coming up next. The game follows the natural progression of the seasons: spring, summer, autumn, winter. If you are a new player, however, your island will be perpetually stuck in spring until you upgrade to Petal Paradise. Even after that, the powerful magic that held your farm in temporal stasis takes another two weeks to wear off, after which you will finally be caught up with the rest of the world. Most delivery NPCs ask for crops and fruits that are in season, though not all do. Because deliveries will only update when you complete or skip them, it's possible to have an NPC asking for something you can't currently produce. The goblin NPCs that reward FLOWER are so ravenous that they ignore the seasons altogether, asking you for foods made with out-of-season produce, and fish that can't be caught for another week or two. Initially you will want to skip these until you have a good stock of resources built up. You can also use the calendar to find out when special events are happening. The three event types that are visible are Unknown Events, Double Delivery Day, and the Full Moon. The calendar will also display the current time in UTC, labeled as the Sunflower Clock. When this reaches midnight, the game will reset, so use it to find out when that will happen in your local area. If you live in an area that observes daylight savings time, note that UTC does not, so reset time will be different for part of your year. ### Unknown Event “A mysterious force approaches… Will it bring fortune or destruction? Only time will tell…" The most common calendar event, this day will bring a challenge or blessing depending on the season. Tap on the day and Read More to see what events might be possible. The Fish Frenzy can occur in any season.  The developers have stated that there will only be three unknown events per week, and at least one of them will be negative. The Full Moon counts as one of those events, despite it being known, so a week with a Full Moon will only have two other events in it. ### Double Delivery Day The generosity of the residents of Sunflorea overflows on this day, and every delivery you make will have double the rewards, whether that be Coins, Chapter Tickets, or FLOWER. Note that only tasks visible in the Deliveries tab of your Codex are eligible for this bonus, not Weekly Chores or the Mega Bounty Board. The first delivery you make to an NPC will be doubled, but it doesn't have to be the one that is visible. If you are able to skip a delivery for a character, the new delivery you get will be doubled instead. If you complete an old delivery for double value and a new one appears, it will **not** be doubled. Skills and items that increase the value of deliveries are factored in before the doubling, so you can stand to make quite a profit on this day. It's a good strategy to hold off on making deliveries the day before a DDD, so you can ensure you will be able to complete them the next day.  ### Full Moon “A rare event where exotic creatures and crops appear.” The game follows the Chinese lunar calendar, so you may not see a perfectly full moon if you look outside on the night of this event. Regardless, this brings some important bonuses to your game. For one, you can buy one seed for each of the three “moon berries” from the market on your farm on this day. You can plant and harvest them anytime, and there are rumors of ways to get more through a system of Telegrams… The chances of obtaining Marine Marvel map pieces also increases by 100%. The chance is still very small, but if you're determined to find them all, waiting until this day is a good strategy. Finally, if you have Eggplants actively growing when this event begins at game reset, all of them will instantly mature. They aren't affected in any other way for the remainder of the day. The usefulness of this bonus is limited, however, since Eggplant only grows in the summer, so the full moon must happen during that season.  ## Weather Events For the four negative events, an item is available that will prevent it if it's placed on your farm when the game resets and the event begins. The item will be consumed, however, requiring you to buy a new one. Visit Bailey in the Plaza for the costs of each item. **All of the events that affect numbers like output boosts and growing times will only affect actions on that day.** Output is determined upon harvest, and growing time upon planting. So, you can plant a crop during the Sunshower and the time remaining won't change at game reset, but the boost provided by the Bountiful Harvest will only be included if you harvest on the same day. ### Tornado/Tsunami The Tornado and Tsunami events are functionally the same, though they require different protection items; the Tornado Pinwheel and Mangrove, respectively. Roughly half of your crops and buildings will be damaged if they are not protected. Crop damage means that anything growing in the affected plot is lost and cannot be harvested, even after the event ends. The affected plot also cannot have any new seeds planted in it. Fruit and flower plots are currently unaffected by this event. Damage to buildings means something different depending on the building. Buildings currently include the five cooking stations, the barn, chicken coop, greenhouse, pet house, aging shack, crafting table, and crop machine. Anything that was being produced in those buildings will continue to do so, including queued items. You cannot collect any finished foods, crops, or items, and cannot start new ones. If the barn or coop is affected, animals cannot be fed or collected from.  These are arguably the worst events, as there is no way to control which of your buildings or crops will be damaged. The best solution is to simply pay for the protection items. ### Insect Plague All crop plots harvested on this day will have their output halved. All bonuses and boosts are factored in accordingly before the halving. Fruit, flowers, and the greenhouse are currently unaffected.  Of all the events, this one is possibly the least bad, as you can simply wait to harvest your crops until the next day. If you are concerned about the resource cost of the protective items, the Pesticide is likely the best one to skip. ### Great Freeze The growing speed of your crops is doubled, meaning it takes twice as long for them to mature. Depending on the crop, this can be an annoyance or a major issue. Potatoes maturing in 10 minutes instead of 5 isn't that much of an issue, but Kale taking 3 days to grow is a big problem.  If you choose to skip the Heat Stone this winter, make sure you have Rapid Root available, and any harvest-time boosting items.  ### Sunshower The opposite of the Great Freeze, all of your crops growing speeds will be halved! This event only occurs in winter and autumn, when most of the longest-growing advanced crops are active, so it can be a great boon. ### Bountiful Harvest All of your crops and fruits, including the greenhouse plants and crop machine outputs, have a flat +1 bonus when harvesting them on this day. Take advantage of this event to grow basic and medium crops with short growing times! ### Fish Frenzy Every time you catch a fish, you will get +1 extra. This is in addition to any other boosts you have to fish output. It's important to note that it only applies to fish, not other treasures you can catch like sea cucumbers, starfish, seaweed, and the rest. ## Predicting the Weather Because of some rules that have been observed with the weather/event system, it is sometimes possible to guess an upcoming event with a reasonable probability of success. 1. Every week has **exactly three** unknown events, unless one of them is the Full Moon, in which case there will be **two**. 2. **Exactly one** of those unknown events will be a disaster event, no more. 3. The other two positive events will be the Fish Frenzy and the seasonal event (Bountiful Harvest in Spring and Summer, Sunshower in Autumn and Winter). 4. The Full Moon event replaces the Fish Frenzy; no Frenzy will occur during a week with a Full Moon. By applying these rules, the events later in the week can be guessed fairly reliably. The third and fourth rules have not been expressly stated by the developers, only observed through repeated weather watching. So, if the first event of the week is a disaster, the other two will be positive. Conversely, if two positive events happen, the third is guaranteed to be a disaster. The third event of the week can be predicted most of the time: if a disaster hasn't occurred yet, it will be that. If it has, the positive event will be the other one that happens during that season.  Full Moon weeks are slightly different, since they are effectively positive events for the purposes of the calendar, but are known beforehand, unlike the others. So if the first event of the week is a disaster, then the Full Moon rises, the third event will be positive, but could be either of the two that can happen that season. Double Delivery Days don't factor into this prediction, since they are always known beforehand and (nearly) always occur once a week. ## Guardians & Shields There are a series of items that directly affect the seasonal and weather events in the game, though they are all rare and require thousands of FLOWER to obtain just one. If a player is willing to invest in the game, though, they will provide huge benefits. The Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter Guardians are a set of elemental spirits, that when placed on your farm, protect against all negative events regardless of what weather items you have. In fact, you no longer need to buy protective items at all. In addition, the Sunshower and Bountiful Harvest events will be boosted, giving you even faster growing times and +2 harvest bonus, respectively. Fish Frenzies are even more intense, with the base bonus rising to +2. If a Full Moon rises during a season that you have a Guardian for, the chance to get a Marine Marvel map piece will also be double what it usually is. The Seasonal Shields are another quartet of secondary items that you equip on your Bumpkin or Farmhands. The Solflare Aegis and Autumn's Embrace reduce the growing time of all crop plots by 50% in summer and autumn, respectively. The Blossom Ward and the Frozen Heart will add +1 to your crop output in either spring or winter. While these items debuted in the Winds of Change chapter that introduced seasons, they have appeared in the auction lineup of subsequent chapters, so you may still have a chance to obtain one if you have the resources… > Contributors to this page > > [librophagus](/en/user-pages/librophagus)\- primary content > > [iSPANK](/en/user-pages/iSPANK) - tagging

title: Skills

# Skills

## Skills in General

Specialization is the key to a healthy economy and community, and Sunflower Land is no different. There are so many activities available to players, from farming to animal rearing, to fishing and cooking, that it can be overwhelming to think you have to do it all. But because of the marketplace and skills, you don't. In fact, you will probably benefit more from picking one thing and leaning into it than trying to be a generalist.

Skills are accessible from your Bumpkin's portrait menu, under the Skills tab. You will earn 1 Skill Point for every level of experience, so start those kitchens cooking to climb to the top!

There are seven categories of skills you have access to at the beginning of the game, and five more that unlock at the Petal Paradise and Desert Islands. 

Every group of skills is broken up into three Tiers, like so many other things in the game. All of the skills in Tier 1 cost 1 point to unlock. Those in Tier 2 cost 2 points, but you must have unlocked a certain amount of points in the lower Tier to be able to take any at all. The requirements differ by category, so check in-game to see the current numbers. Tier 3 skills cost 3 points each and also require prior skills to be unlocked.

You can see a full list of every skill in the game and their uses at [https://sfl.world/info/skills](https://sfl.world/info/skills). There is also a [skill trainer](https://sfl.world/tools/skills/) that will load your farm's data and let you pick and choose skills freely with your available points, and even increase the amount of points to plan your next levels.

This guide will not attempt to explain every single skill, as they are described in sufficient detail through the above resources, and are subject to change for balancing purposes. Instead, an overview of each category and some strategies and synergies will be discussed.

## Power Skills

Most skills provide boosts in the form of resource output or time deductions, but some provide actions that you take at specific times. These are known as Power Skills, and will be labeled as such in the window. After you claim one, you can access it with the Power Skills button (lightning bolt) in the lower-left of your screen. 

The fertilizer Power Skills can be used as often as you need, but the others have cooldowns that require you to wait several days between uses. The benefits of each are usually well worth the wait, though.

## Crops Skills

The most straightforward category, and the one you will likely take the most points in right away. Crops are one of the basic components of the game, and should not be neglected. Some of the most useful skills include the three scarecrow boosters, as you will outgrow a 3x3 area very quickly. 

The Acre and Hectare Farm skills are also worth considering, especially when planning an overall strategy. For example, if you plan on raising animals, Acre Farm is a good choice, since all three crops required for animal feed are Advanced.

## Trees Skills

One of the smallest categories, these skills boost growth time, output, and help make Axes more affordable through cost reduction and stock increase. Tough Tree is a very valuable skill, as it can multiply your wood output substantially. It's possible to get up to 4 units of wood per tree with this skill.

Tree Turnaround means that after chopping a tree, there's a 15% chance of it immediately growing back and letting you chop it down a second time.

There are no tree skills that provide benefits at the cost of something else, but increased wood output is very useful if you plan on leaning into either of the next two categories.

## Fishing Skills

With the advent of the Aging Shed in the Salt Awakening chapter, fish have become more valuable than ever. Corale's Fishy Fortune skill doubles the amount of coins you earn from her deliveries, which can be very beneficial. Many of the other skills increase your daily limit for fishing, which sounds great until you consider that your stock of Fishing Rods is limited, and you may end up restocking more often than you want to.

The three Fishy skills (Chance, Roll, Gamble) increase your chances of getting +1 fish for the respective tiers. By coupling that with Frenzied Fish and waiting for a Fish Frenzy day, you can potentially get 5 fish with a single catch (+1 Fishy skill, +1 Fish Frenzy base, +1 Frenzied skill base, 50% additional chance of +1), which will leave you with more fish than you know what to do with.

Fishy Feast is very useful if you plan on creating Aged Fish or any of the fish product-based foods in your cooking buildings, as it applies to all of them.

## Mining Skills

Mining is a very lucrative trade, as all of the minerals you dig up can be sold on the marketplace directly. Most of the skills in this category just boost output or recovery time, but some allow you to lean into a specific mineral. Rocky Favor increases Stone by +1 at the cost of -0.5 Iron, while Ferrous Favor does the opposite. Stone is slightly more versatile if you plan on doing a lot of fishing or digging, while Iron is the way to go if you are drilling for oil or continuing on the chain for gold.

For any mining operation, consider taking as many wood-boosting Trees skills as you can, since wood is required for every kind of pickaxe.

## Cooking Skills

More food means more experience, which means more levels and more skill points! Cooking is always a valuable endeavor, as food will always be in demand for deliveries, chores, the faction pet, and personal pets too. Most of the skills in this category increase experience from eaten foods or decrease cooking time, so you can take them all safely.

The only cooking skill that has a detriment, if you could call it that, is Double Nom, which effectively cooks two recipes simultaneously. You will need to provide twice as many ingredients per cooking action, but you will get two dishes instead of one upon completion. Once you have a large amount of resources as your disposal, this will expedite your food production substantially.

## Composting Skills

Composters are so useful they have a category unto themselves. Most of these skills boost the fertilizer output for a specific unit or decrease their processing time, and the Power Skills are worth considering because of their lack of cooldown. 

Feathery Business is worth considering if you plan on specializing in Chickens, as you will have many extra Feathers.

The penalty from Composting Revamp was actually reduced to -2 from its original amount of -3, but either way it is very easy to mitigate this downside by purchasing fermented bait from the marketplace.

## Aging Skills

All of these new skills involve Salt harvesting and the products of the Aging Shed. Each are fairly self-explanatory, and don't involve any kind of specialization at this time. 

Wide Rakes is a good investment, as the more Salt you get from each rake, the better.

If you want to take up the noble profession of bait merchant, Speedy Aging, Bacalhau and Fish Smoking are all the skills to take, along with enough skills from the Fishing category to keep your output as high as possible. When looking at the hard numbers, bait manufacture isn't “profitable” if the cost of one fishing rod and chum yield one fish. But during a Fishing Frenzy, the cost of each fish is reduced significantly, making bait worth your while.

## Fruit Patch Skills (Petal Paradise)

The first category to provide real specialization choices, the Tier 3 skills allow you to choose two fruits to focus on and either decrease growing time or boost output, at the cost of penalizing the others. 

Choosing Short Pickings will make spring your time to shine, as Blueberries and Oranges will be quickened by 25%. 

Or, make autumn your oyster with Long Pickings, when the normally ponderous Apples and Bananas will mature 25% faster.

You could also ensure a year-round harvest with Zesty Vibes and Crime Fruit, as one of the two acidic fruits are viable in every season. If you choose to focus on Lemons and Tomatoes, also consider the Trees skill No Axe No Worries, along with Fruity Woody, as you will be clearing your fruit patches out more frequently than ever.

## Animals Skills (Petal Paradise)

Animal raising has a very high amount of specialization, and seems designed from the start to encourage players to pick one animal and focus on them. Milk and Leather are definitely the top sellers, but with the introduction of doll crafting, Wool is more important than ever, and Eggs are in high demand for cooking and deliveries. 

The Featherweight, Merino Whisperer, and Leathercraft Mastery skills boost the output of those three secondary animal products, at the cost of reducing the others. Some detrimental skills can be canceled out by taking another, but not these. Claiming all three would only provide you with a paltry +0.15 bonus to each product and a waste of skill points.

Clucky Grazing, Sheepwise Diet, and Cow-Smart Nutrition all decrease the feed required for their respective animals, while increasing the cost for the other two. Taking two of these would mean a 25% increase to both animals, and no benefit. The cost of feed will make or break any animal operation, so this is one of the most important things to consider when planning.

As mentioned above, Acre Farm is an excellent choice for animal enthusiasts, as any feed you grow yourself is feed you don't have to buy.

## Bees & Flowers Skills (Petal Paradise)

The only real specialization you can choose with flowers is Flowery Abode, which boosts your honey output by a large amount, in exchange for a longer flower growing time. Since flowers already take a very long time to grow, and you can reduce the penalty to only 20% through two other skills, this is a possible contender for an apiarist specialization.

Another important synergy to consider is Buzzworthy Treats, which boosts the experience earned for foods made with Honey. Couple that with the Cooking skill Drive-Through Deli, and the Honey Cheddar is suddenly worth 25% more. 

## Greenhouse Skills (Desert)

There are two main paths you can take with the Greenhouse. You can choose Seeded Bounty to increase produce by +0.5, at the cost of using two seeds per planting. Since Greenhouse seeds are expensive, even with the Seedy Business skill that decreases seed cost by 15%, this is a hard one to justify.

Or, you can pick Greasy Plants, which will increase produce by +1, at the cost of double the Oil consumption for every plot. It's important to note that picking Slick Saver will decrease the **doubled** amount by -1, resulting in costs of 5 (Grape), 7 (Rice) and 11 (Olive).

## Machinery Skills (Desert)

There are many useful skills here once you reach the Desert Island, most of them involving the Crop Machine, but some that boost Oil extraction, which in turn helps the Greenhouse and even Cooking. 

The Tier 2 skill Rapid Rig decreases growth time in the Crop Machine by 20%, while increasing Oil consumption by 40%. The skills Oil Gadget and Efficiency Extension Module will cancel that penalty out altogether.

Oil Rig is an important skill to consider if you are a Sheep specialist, as it will allow you to craft Oil Drills with the Wool that you will have in abundance.

Due to a quirk in the math, taking Oil Rig (-10% Oil consumption), Efficiency Extension Module (-30%) AND Rapid Rig (+40% consumption, and -20% speed boost), does not result in a net gain of -20% speed and -0% increased consumption. It actually gives you -16% reduced consumption and the speed boost at the same time.  

## Skill Upgrades

Almost every skill in the game comes with three ranks. The first one is the same as taking the skill directly in the previous skill system. Ranks 2 and 3 are upgrades to the skill's effects, each of which require [Ascension Shards](/en/mechanics/ascension) and additional skill points. Pay close attention to the bonuses for the upper ranks before taking them. Green Thumb I reduces plot crop time by 5%, while Green Thumb III reduces it by 7.5%. There are better and cheaper ways to reduce your crop time than spending all of those skill points and shards.

Some Rank 2 and 3 skills require you to unlock the higher tiers in the skill tree first before upgrading.

The skills that do not have ranks are ones that would not benefit from additional upgrades, such as Insta-Chop (harvest trees with one tap instead of three), or Sprout Surge (Apply Sprout Mix to all crop plots).

Power Skill upgrades reduce their cooldown time, some by as much as half.

## Skill Reset

If you decide that your current build just isn't working for you, there is a way to re-spec your Bumpkin and try something different. The first time you choose to reset your skills, you will pay nothing, getting all of your skill points and ascension chards back at once and losing any boosts you may have had. You will be able to reset again for free in six months, and can check the time remaining at the link at the bottom of the skills screen.

Did you make an error and you're using up too much oil? You can reset again ahead of time, but it will cost you. The full list of withering penalties is available here: [https://sfl.world/info/const/#SKILL\_RESET\_COST](https://sfl.world/info/const/#SKILL_RESET_COST)  
Resetting your skills with Gems will also not change the time until your next free skill reset.

markdown:
# Reputation

## Introduction

Reputation is a system that was implemented by the devs to try and combat “bad actors”, “multi accounters” and “bots”. The system aims itself to allow only REAL people to play the game and benefit from certain features that the game has to offer. This system has been successful overall, as bot activity which used to be rampant has largely subsided.

## How to get reputation points?

Reputation points can be gained a number of ways

*   Reach Petal Paradise - 100 points
*   Reach lvl 15 - 50 points
*   Reach Desert Island - 50 points
*   Reach Volcano Island - 50 points
*   Connect & verify Discord - 50 points
*   Complete proof of Humanity - 100 points
*   Reach lvl 100 - 150 points
*   Own a bud - 300 points
*   VIP Access - 600 points (If your VIP status lapses you will lose the points)

## What do I gain by having reputation points?

At certain “milestones” of rep points you will gain the ability to do more things in the game.

###   
Seedling - 250 points

*   2 Marketplace Listings Per Day
*   Withdraw NFTs (decorations and wearables)
*   Ability to Mint Your Farm (This provides you with an NFT token that represents access to your farm. It also allows you to “Store on Chain," a process required to exceed the storage limits for some items)

### Grower - 350 points

*   3 Marketplace Listings Per Day
*   Auction Access

### Cropkeeper - 600 Points

*   Make & Accept Offers
*   Unlimited Listings & Offers
*   Unlock all $FLOWER Deliveries

### Grand Harvester- 1000 Points

*   Withdraw FLOWER

## How can I find how many reputation points I have?

1.  Click your profile Icon at the top left corner of the screen. (image 1)
2.  Click the “reputation button" (image 2)
3.  Click “Earn Points” in the top tab to view your points, and what you still need to do to get more (image 3)

title: Marketplace
markdown:
# P2P Marketplace The in-game marketplace is the very heart of Sunflower Land, as it allows players from all over the world to trade resources with one another and ultimately help everyone succeed in their game. With so much to do and see, it can be overwhelming to try and do everything at once. Fortunately, you don't have to grow it yourself, you can buy it! Give some food to those hungry goblins and get a few FLOWER, or deposit some from outside the game, and let's get trading. **This article assumes you have reached the Cropkeeper** [**reputation level**](/en/mechanics/reputation) **and unlocked full access to the Marketplace. Otherwise, you may have restrictions or limits in place.** ![](/game-mechanics/marketplace.png) ## Overview The marketplace is easy to access, just tap the icon with left and right arrows in the lower-left corner of your screen. There are lots of buttons and links, so lets go through each one. ### Trending The first tab, shown in the screenshot, displays some stats about recent activity and high-value items sold in the last few days. From there you can search or browse the listings directly. ### Resources This is the directory of everything you can grow, mine, and ranch on your farm. An individual listing contains the item's price and how many you have. ### Power ups A directory of every item, whether wearable or decorative, that will provide you with a boost of some kind in the game. You can narrow it down to one of those two categories with the links that appear in the left-hand menu. ### Cosmetics Everything you can wear or place on your farm that doesn't have a boost of any kind. These are just for fun and style, and are usually much cheaper than boost items. But some rare ones can still be worth quite a bit… ### Pet NFTs If the common pets are just too boring for you, visit this section to find a unique creature to call your own! ### Bud NFTs Visit this page if you've got resources to invest in your game journey, or just want to look at their adorable little faces! Buds are a rare item that are worth several thousand FLOWER at the least, but can provide some major boosts to your gameplay. ### My Profile Some stats about the last few things you've bought, and your active trades. You can also see your whole farm's inventory and, if possible, sell something you don't need. There are many non-tradeable items listed here, like your house and firepit. ### Reward Shop Under My Profile, this is where you'll spend all of those Trade Points you'll eventually earn. ### Flower Dashboard Look here for some fun stats and numbers about the economy. ![](/game-mechanics/trading2.png) ## Making a Deal Once you find something that strikes your fancy, you will see several options on the screen. If you're looking to Buy something, find a row under Listings that fits your budget and click the button to trade. You'll get the items instantly and pay the FLOWER. ### Bulk Buy What if you need a LOT of something, or want to pick up several smaller listings to get everything you need? Just use the Bulk Buy button, which will let you select multiple listings and purchase them all at once. You can also specify the amount of resource you need and the game will automatically select listings that come as close as possible to your desired number without going over. You'll be able to verify which ones you want before purchasing, too. ### Offers But what if you don't want to buy 50 Leather, especially at those prices? What if you only need 5 to craft that doll? Then scroll down to the bottom of the Offers section that isn't visible in the screenshot and click Make Offer. Enter in how many you need, and the game will tell you if you go under the minimum that every item has. The total price for the sale is prefilled to the right, but you can click the Price button to change it to Price Per Unit, if that way of thinking makes more sense to you. You can leave the price as it is, but to make your offer more enticing to sellers, you should generally price it slightly **higher** so it appears at the top of the Offers list. But it's really up to you. After you make an offer, you will have to wait for someone to accept it and sell to you. It may take a while, but if you priced it right, it should be fairly quick. You'll get a popup when you first load the game, or if you try to do other actions. Congratulations on your successful trade! ### Listings After your latest bountiful harvest, you're looking to sell some of that Kale. You have two options when selling something, either accepting someone else's Offer, or making a new Listing. First scroll through the Offers list and see if any look good. Offers are usually always lower than the official price at the top of the screen, but the advantage is that you will get your money instantly, instead of waiting for a Listing. Use the List for Sale button at the top to make that happen. The Listing screen looks almost the same as the Offers screen, except for the trading fee. The marketplace taxes every transaction, with the fees paid by the seller. When you made your offer earlier, you weren't selling, so you didn't pay the fee. You can see your current resource fee on the right side of the screen, and like it suggests, advancing in the game will lower this fee substantially. Draw up your Listing with quantities and price, then submit it and wait for a buyer. When selling, you want your prices to be **lower** than the other farmers, so even just reducing it by 0.0001 FLOWER is enough to put you at the top of the queue. Or, hold your position and hope for a better deal. Again, it's up to you. Quantity is also important for Listings, since if you sell 500 Kale at once, it might take a while for someone with that kind of budget to come along. It's generally better to split up a large amount of a resource across several Listings with smaller quantities. This is very easy to do, just change the # field at the right of the screen to the number of listings you want to create simultaneously, all for the same quantity. You can create up to 20 in one go with this method. Like with Offers, Listings depend on another player to transact, so you might have to wait a while, especially if the demand for a resource or item is low. If your Kale isn't moving, cancel the Listing and try for a different price until you get it. ### Obsidian Obsidian is a rare and powerful resource, and used to be available on the Limited tab of the marketplace before it was removed. Despite being shown in the standard Resources list now, it still retains some of its old limitations. **Currently, each player can only list 1 piece of Obsidian for sale per week, and buy a total of 5.** Despite Obsidian being divisible into decimal units through instantly growing flowers and giant fruits, you can only buy and sell a single unit at a time. This means if you want more than one you must buy each individually. You also earn Trade Points when buying or selling Obsidian. ### Item Trading The process to trade NFT collectibles or wearables is slightly different than it is for resources. You can only list one copy of an item for sale at a time, even if you have more than one. The tax for trading items is fixed at 10%, regardless of your progression in the game. When buying a collectible item, you don't get to choose which listing you want to purchase. The Buy Now button will let you buy the first item in the list, which is the lowest-priced. If you're selling and choose to Accept an offer, you will sell to the first player in the list, which will be the highest-priced. This requires a little more strategy than when selling resources, where your listings can be bought up even if someone else creates a listing at a lower price. If you want to make sure your item is chosen by a buyer, you have to watch it periodically and re-list it if someone undercuts you. Or, if you want to make sure your offer is accepted by a seller, bid a little more than the next farmer. ## Searching If you're looking for something to help a specific aspect of your game, you can search for the kind of boost you want in addition to the name of the item. Searching for “tomato” not only gives you the Tomato Clown and the Tomato Bombard, but also Cannonball, all of which boost your Tomato plants in some way. ## Reward Shop After you've bought or sold some NFT items, you may notice a few things in your inventory called Trade Points. These are earned at a rate of 0.25 for each 1 FLOWER of the item's list price (pre-tax). Visit the Rewards tab under My Profile to see what you can redeem all those points for. [Treasure Keys](/en/mechanics/chests) are a good investment, or you can try your luck in the Bud Raffle with the rare [Prize Ticket](/en/chapter-race/raffles). The Trade Cake is worth a decent amount of XP, if you don't feel like gambling. There are also several valuable packs available. These items are given to you directly, not added to your shops [stock amounts](/en/beginners/stock-limits), as they seem to indicate. The Tools Pack claims to have a full Stock's worth of tools, which it would if you didn't have any other items or skills that boost your tool stock amounts. It also only contains pickaxes of every variety and regular Axes. The [Digging](/en/mechanics/digging) Pack contains 50 Sand Shovels and 10 Drills, naturally. The [Seeds](/en/mechanics/harvesting) Pack contains _most_ of a un-boosted stock's worth of seeds, except it is missing several. All of the single-season crops added in the Winds of Change Chapter are absent, as are flower and greenhouse seeds. It will warn you if you have so many seeds that you will go over your inventory limit with at least one of them, but given its limited nature this isn't really worth your hard-earned TP. The [Fishing](/en/mechanics/fishing) Pack contains those missing rods from the Tools Pack, along with a good assortment of baits. If you don't have the higher level composters, this is a decent choice. The [Animal](/en/mechanics/animals) Feed Pack contains the four major food groups for any of your animals, except Omnifeed. Given the price of Mixed Grains, this is worth considering if you are an animal expert. Here is the trading tax table in English: ## Trading Commission | Island Type | Base Tax | With VIP
(-50%) | With VIP
+Trading Shrine (-2.5%) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **Basic** | No trades available | No trades available | No trades available | | **Spring** | 55% | 27.5% | 25% | | **Desert** | 25% | 12.5% | 10% | | **Volcano** | 15% | 7.5% | 5% | ### Notes: 1. **Basic** islands do not offer trading 2. **VIP status** reduces the tax by half (divides by 2) 3. **Trading Shrine** further reduces the tax by 2.5 percentage points 4. **VIP** and **Trading Shrine** effects stack # External Marketplaces It is still possible to buy and sell resources and items on other NFT marketplaces such as [OpenSea](https://opensea.io/collection/sunflower-land-collectibles). However, as the in-game marketplace has evolved, other marketplaces have become less relevant, as they are less accessible to new players unfamiliar with blockchain concepts. You must pay for your resource or item in crypto, and transfer it from your wallet to your game account, every step of which requires a gas fee and the POL token. The game used to provide a Polygon wallet address tied to your farm, which allowed you to skip a step and have the marketplace send the NFT directly to the farm. That has been removed, so you must receive it in your personal wallet. Resource withdrawal has been removed from the game, so any Sunflowers that you find for sale somewhere else were extracted before the change. It is only possible to Deposit resources that you may still have in your wallet. All other items are still withdrawable and tradeable, including powerups, cosmetics, Buds, and NFT Pets. # History The marketplace used to be only accessible from the Plaza, at a large notice board that stood where [Bailey](/en/npcs/bailey) currently has his shop set up. You had to travel to the Plaza to be able to create listings or make offers, and your goods or money would be delivered to you wherever you were as it happens today. The button in the UI that lets you access it anywhere was added before Bailey set up shop, so you could still get to it from the Plaza or the button. ### Limited Section A rotating list of items that were requested on the [Mega Bounty Board](/en/chapter-race/bounty-board) for the week. The Limited tab was removed at the beginning of Chapter 13. For every item on this page, you could buy 3 of them and sell 1 in a week, excepting Obsidian, which you could buy 9 of. Even at Cropkeeper with “unlimited access” this restriction was still in place. ### Resource Withdrawal Previously, resources could be withdrawn from a player's account and stored as SFTs in their crypto wallet, then sold on external marketplaces. To make the game less attractive to players who only wanted to make money, this option was removed in March of 2026. Only certain resources were withdrawable, and even then the game charged a 30% tax when doing so. | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Sunflowers | Potatoes | Pumpkins | Carrots | | Cabbage | Beetroots | Cauliflower | Parsnips | | Radishes | Wheat | Kale | Apples | | Blueberries | Oranges | Eggplants | Corn | | Bananas | Soybeans | Wood | Stone | | Iron | Gold | Eggs | | > Contributors to this page > > [librophagus](/en/user-pages/librophagus)\- primary content

# How to Complete In-Game Verification via Discord or Telegram

This guide provides step-by-step instructions for verifying your identity in-game using your linked Discord or Telegram account.

* * *

## Discord Verification

Follow the steps below to complete verification through Discord:

### Step 1 – Agree to Terms

*   Go to the **⁠╭📙・rules** channel in the server.
*   Read and agree to the game's **Terms and Conditions**.

### Step 2 – Request Verification

*   Navigate to the **⁠｜🔓・verify** channel.
*   Type `/verify` exactly, including the slash (`/`).
*   Submit the command.

### Step 3 – Complete In-Game Verification

*   Return to the game on your device.
*   Follow the prompts to complete the **face verification** step.

### Platform-Specific Notes

#### On Mobile:

1.  Tap the **game icon** in Discord.
2.  Select **Flower Rewards Bot**.
3.  Press the **Send button** next to the **Verify** option.

![01.png](/faq/verification/01.png)  
![02.png](/faq/verification/02.png)

#### On Desktop:

1.  Click the **Plus (+)** icon in the message box.
2.  Select **Use Apps** (or **Apps**).
3.  Choose the **`/verify`** command.
4.  Press **Enter** to send.

![04.png](/faq/verification/04.png)  
![03.png](/faq/verification/03.png)

* * *

## Telegram Verification

### Step 1 – Open the Bot

*   Go to: [https://t.me/pumpkin\_pete\_bot](https://t.me/pumpkin_pete_bot)
*   Start the bot if you haven’t already.

### Step 2 – Send Verification Command

*   In the chat, type: **`/verify`** (including the slash).
*   Send the message.

### Step 3 – Finalize In-Game

*   Switch back to the game.
*   Proceed with **face verification** as prompted.

* * *

## Troubleshooting

If you encounter any issues during verification, the most common reason is:

> You are using a **Discord or Telegram account that is NOT linked** to the game account you’re trying to verify.

### How to fix:

*   Log out of Discord/Telegram on your device.
*   Log in with the **correct account** that you used when registering for the game.
*   Repeat the verification steps above.

If the problem persists, contact the game’s support team through official channels for further assistance.

title: Deliveries
markdown:
# Deliveries

![](/game-mechanics/deliveries.png)

## Overview

“Travel and deliver goods to earn rewards."

The delivery system is the backbone of earning resources in the game, and will provide you with great benefits in the future. Open the Codex near your Bumpkin's portrait and see what's currently being asked for. 

The first tab of the window is Deliveries, and is split up into three categories: Coins, Chapter Tickets (Bracelet in the above screenshot) and FLOWER. Not all NPCs will be available to you at the beginning of the game, so level up and get them all! 

The items requested by each NPC are different for every player, except for the Chapter Tickets, which are the same for everyone for balancing purposes. You can see the current deliveries for your farm in every category at [https://sfl.world/land](https://sfl.world/land) (enter your Farm ID to see yours). Or, go to the main sfl.world page to see the current day's Ticket deliveries and decide if skipping that tough one is worth it or not.

You can also see every possible delivery for every NPC at [https://sfl.world/info/deliveries](https://sfl.world/info/deliveries)

## Delivery Types

There are currently three categories for deliveries, based on the token or resource the NPC gives as a reward.

### Coins

Coins are the primary resource used to purchase seeds, tools, and for many crafting projects. While you can sell crops and fruits for Coins directly, deliveries to these NPCs are usually a better choice. The value of a Coin delivery is **always** higher than the sell price of the component resources when sold at the farmer's market or the digging store, so don't worry about whether or not you're getting a good deal, because you are. Even if you have earned the Treasure Map from digging (sell price +20%), Old Salty will still give you a better deal on diggable items. Coin deliveries also provide 10 Chapter Points, regardless of the amount of coins awarded.

### Chapter Tickets/Points

These NPCs will trade your resources and food for the active Chapter Ticket, as well as points toward the current Chapter Pass, at a rate of 5 Points per 1 Ticket.. The chapter race is designed for late-game players, so if you're new, focus on Coins and possibly FLOWER for now. These NPCs will go “on holiday” and refuse deliveries during the first few weeks of each new Chapter, to help with fairness for new players. Those who reside in the Plaza will all congregate inside the auction house, while those in other zones will remain where they are. You can still gift them with flowers to boost delivery points, though, and trade Finn for Fishing Lures if you need them.

### FLOWER

The ever-hungry goblins will pay for food, fish, and flowers with the highly coveted FLOWER token. Some pay only a little, while others can pay a lot. Take some time to do the math with sfl.world, though, as oftentimes the value of the delivery will be less than if you had sold the component items on the marketplace individually. Furthermore, some goblins will request the same items but pay differing prices. Once you have a good handle on the game and can build up some food, it is definitely worth your while to visit these ravenous creatures. FLOWER deliveries also reward 10 Chapter Points, regardless of the amount of FLOWER earned.

![](/game-mechanics/make_delivery.png)

## Making Deliveries

Once you've collected everything a character wants, a board icon will appear in their window. This icon also appears next to their name when you approach them in the Plaza. Use these indicators to see at a glance what you have ready to go out and what you're still missing.

In order to deliver something to an NPC, **you must travel to wherever they live**. You cannot deliver something from your farm. Each NPC in the window displays their location underneath their quote, and the background of their portrait also reflects this. There's also a Travel to button which will take you to the zone where they reside, but **not** directly to them. You must still walk up to and interact with them to finish the delivery. You will begin to learn the locations of every character as you play and develop a path to reach all of them as you travel through each area.

If you are playing on a desktop or laptop, you can take advantage of a fun trick. Enter the Plaza or another zone where you can move around. Open your Codex, and when you find the next NPC in your area that needs a delivery, you can actually walk towards them with the WASD or arrow keys while your Codex is open. That way, you can easily keep track of who needs what without having to constantly open and close the window.

## Relationship Points

After you successfully make your delivery, you will notice the green bar at the top of the window increase. This is the amount of relationship points you earned for that order. By clicking on the present icon, you will be able to see your progress to the next reward, and what that reward will be. Once the bar is full, the present icon will start blinking. Any points earned beyond the amount needed to trigger a gift are still added to the total. You can see all of the possible rewards for each NPC at [https://sfl.world/info/flowers](https://sfl.world/info/flowers)

Note that some NPCs do not have a point bar and will not provide any rewards for successive deliveries. This includes all of the goblins and some others such as Peggy and the Pharaoh.

## Skip Order?

If you can't complete the delivery for whatever reason, or just don't want to, you can skip one delivery per day, per NPC. You can only do this, though, if the delivery has been active for at least 24 hours. A timer will tell you how much longer before an order can be skipped, but it is the same for every order as it is just a countdown until the game reset at 00:00 UTC. Note that you can skip an order from anywhere, including while standing near the NPC.

Delivery orders will remain in the queue until you complete or skip them. This allows you to time to complete orders that might require food or flowers that take time to prepare. Every day brings new deliveries, though, so you can think of it as another delivery card underneath the one you are working on. If you complete the order from a previous day, the current day's delivery will become active, allowing you to make up to two deliveries to one character per day. Or, if you skip the order, the card on top is discarded and the current day is shown instead.

Don't worry about needing to skip orders that are too expensive or impossible to craft yet. NPCs are forgiving and don't keep track of how many times you dismiss their requests. Also don't feel bad if you can't clear the board and complete 24 deliveries in a single day. There is no bonus for doing so. Just work within your means and play style and do your best. 

## Double Delivery Day

This special event **usually** happens once per week, though it may not depending on the events of the game. For the duration of this day, the **first** delivery you make to an NPC will give double the reward. This means if you have an older delivery active, it will be doubled and the new delivery that will appear immediately afterward will not be doubled. Or, if you skip a delivery, the new one will be doubled, if you can make it before the day ends.

Chapter Ticket amounts are doubled, after any other boosts that you might have from items and wearables. The amount of Chapter Points will be increased accordingly.

Coin and FLOWER deliveries will be doubled, which makes many requests exceed the value of their component ingredients. Each delivery still awards 10 Chapter points, though.

This event is visible on the in-game calendar, and if you are subscribed to the Pumpkin Pete Telegram bot for quest rewards, it will notify you when DDD arrives. It was not always so easy to predict, though. Previously, when you made a delivery to Pumpkin' Pete in the Plaza, he would whisper to you when the date of the next Double Delivery Day would be. You could see it again by talking to him a second time, but if you forgot, you would have to wait until the next day and make a delivery to him again.

title: Flowers & Gifts
markdown:
# Flowers & Gifts

_Not to be confused with_ [_$FLOWER_](/en/home/tokens#flower)_, the primary utility token for the game_

## Flower Gardening

After you upgrade your island to Petal Paradise, you will be given a flower bed and beehive, and your gardening journey will begin! 

Flower growing begins by purchasing a seed from the farmer's market on your island. There are seven types of seeds, three of which can be grown in any season, and four which rotate with every season.

After buying the seed, you will also need another resource to cross-pollinate your new sprout. You will primarily use fruits and crops, but you can also use other flowers that you've already grown. When you start out, each combination will be listed as unknown, and revealed after you collect the grown flower. Many flowers have more than one recipe, but you will only see the result of a combination if you have specifically bred that seed with that other plant before, even if you've already grown the result of the combination elsewhere (for example, you plant a Sunpetal Seed with Sunflowers, which gives you a Yellow Pansy. You then grow a Sunpetal Seed with Apples, which also results in a Yellow Pansy, but since you haven't bred Sunpetal+Apples before, it will display as Unknown combination). 

After you plant a new unknown combination that results in a flower you've already seen, you can tap or mouse over the flower bed to see what it will be. Of course, the full list of possible combinations is available at [https://sfl.world/info/flowers](https://sfl.world/info/flowers), but we recommend experimenting for a while to preserve that sense of wonder. There is also a tab in your Codex that will show all of the flowers you have discovered, how many of them you have, and what combination is required to breed them. 

## Instant-Grow

While you can't cancel or destroy a flower that is currently growing, you can speed it along with Obsidian. Harvest some from your Lava Pit or buy it on the Marketplace, and apply it (?) to the flower bed to make a flower instantly ready to harvest. The amount of Obsidian needed is proportional to the amount of time remaining, roughly 0.1 units per 24 hours of time, rounded up or down as necessary.

## +1 Flower Boosts

By now you've probably learned that 2 copies of the same item won't give you the same bonus twice. Skills and NFTs that provide you a chance of +1 flower will stack, but a little differently than you might think. Instead of the game adding each chance percentage together into a single cumulative number, each bonus actually resolves individually. For example, if you have the Petalled Perk skill (10%) and the Butterfly craftable (20%) on your farm, you do not end up with a 30% chance to get +1 flower on harvest. Instead, the chance for each boost is resolved separately, meaning if you're lucky and they both succeed, you would end up with 3 total flowers from one bed. There are several NFT items in the marketplace that provide +1 flower chance and are surprisingly affordable, so check them out!

## Beehives

Once a flower is planted, the bees start to work. Honey will be produced in the hive for as long as a flower is growing, or until the hive is full. Each flower bed is paired to a beehive, and while there is no icon or indicator showing this relationship, you can tell by looking closely. Every so often, a bee sprite will leave the hive and hover over the flower bed it is tied to, then return. Beds and hives can be placed anywhere on your farm that you like, but it is usually useful to place them adjacent to one another so you can easily manage your honey output. The distance between the bed and the hive has no bearing on honey speed or yield. 

One beehive takes 24 hours to produce 1 unit of honey. This is actual time, not tied to the game reset. The skill Sweet Bonus increases the amount of honey from a full hive by 0.1, while Hyper Bees increases production by 0.1. This seems a little confusing, but it results in “1.1 full hive / day”. The base rate of production is 1 per 24 hours, or 0.042 honey per hour (rounded). The skill increases that rate to 0.046 honey per hour (rounded), which means you will have a full hive in 21.6 hours instead. That doesn't seem like much, but will add up more quickly than you think, especially when you have multiple hives.

Bees are finicky, though, and will only produce honey in certain conditions. For one, the hive must not be full. When it is, honey production will stop and the excess that would have been produced when you eventually clear it out will be wasted. For this reason, you can harvest honey at any time. The window for a hive will tell you when the hive will be full, so you can estimate if you will be asleep or away when the cap is reached, and harvest it beforehand to ensure it is always producing.

The other important factor is that a flower must be actively growing in the bed tied to the hive. Once it reaches maturity, honey stops, and won't start again until you harvest the flower **and** replant it with a new one.

From those warnings, you may think it wise to always be harvesting your honey every time you visit your farm. That isn't necessarily a good idea, though. If you look closely at the hive window, you will see the progress bar has a fractional percentage, i.e. 22.45%. If you harvest it at that time, you will get 0.22 units of honey, and that .45% will be lost. 

The other reason is that when the hive is 100% full, there is a chance of a [Bee Swarm](/en/mechanics/harvesting#bee-swarm), which will boost your crop plots. There is no indication in the game as to when you get a Bee Swarm until it happens, but if you don't like being surprised you can check your hive status at [https://sfl.world/land](https://sfl.world/land), under Resources on the right side. 

## Mutant Flowers

Every so often you will discover a special, mutant flower upon harvesting a flowerbed. These are randomly determined based on the current Chapter, and you can obtain more than one per Chapter. All mutant flowers can be placed on your farm as decorations, and some even provide rare boosts. You can also sell them on the marketplace when the current chapter concludes.

## Deliveries & Gifts

As you start to make deliveries, you will see many NPCs request flowers as part of their delivery package. While you're fulfilling the order, you may also see a Gift button in the NPCs window. Many NPCs will accept flowers as gifts, complementary to their normal delivery requirements. You can gift an NPC one flower per game day, and earn delivery points which will get you closer to the next reward.

The language of flowers is complicated, and each NPC has certain flowers that they prefer over others. They will accept any flower that you give them, but their preferred flowers will earn more delivery points than others. The character will tell you what they like in their window, and you will see a lightning bolt icon when you select one of those bonus flowers. 

It can be easy to forget about flower gifts when there is so much else going on in the game, but they are the key to earning bonus rewards much faster than you will with just deliveries alone. Also, for Valentine's Day 2025, a special gift was airdropped to all players who had given at least one flower to an NPC in the previous week, with a rare bonus for the top gift givers. So, try to give whenever you can!

## Flower Bounties

Every week, the [Mega Bounty Board](/en/chapter-race/bounty-board) is headlined by a selection of five different flowers, all of which can be redeemed for an amount of Chapter Tickets. Quickly-grown, common flowers are worth less than rare ones, but all are worth your attention if you want to take part in the Chapter Race. Visit [Poppy](/en/chapter-race/bounty-board) in the Plaza to turn in the ones you have collected, and make sure to do the math on whether growing a more advanced specimen is even possible before the week ends (unless you are willing to use some Obsidian).

## Flower Decorations

All flowers can be placed as Decorations on your land, anywhere you would like them to go. Keep in mind that placed flowers do not count as being in your inventory, so cannot be gifted ordelivered to NPCs or used for anything else.

# Infernos/Sunstones ![](/game-mechanics/infernos-sunstones/map.jpg) ## Infernos Infernos can be accessed from the map, using the globe icon in the bottom left of the screen. You must be level 30 to travel there. Infernos is the home of 3 Infernal Goblins: [Gunter](/en/npcs/gunter), [Gilda](/en/npcs/gilda), and [Gorga](/en/npcs/gorga). It is also the place where you can exchanges Obsidian for Sunstones, and Sunstones for more ‘nodes’ or ‘node forging’. | ![](/npcs/gunter.jpg)
Gunter | ![](/npcs/gilda.jpg)
Gilda | ![](/npcs/gorga.jpg)
Gorga | | --- | --- | --- | ## Sunstones Sunstones are a ‘Finite’ resource that, unlike the other resources, does NOT refresh once fully mined. When you mine a Sunstone node 10 times, it disappears from your island. Sunstones require a Gold Pickaxe to mine. If you're curious about how much Sunstone is remaining in your nodes, you can check [https://sfl.world/land/](https://sfl.world/land/) (enter your farm ID). Each individual node displays its remaining value visually, getting smaller and smaller as you continue to mine it. You will gain new Sunstone rocks as you expand your island, though, so eventually more will come. If you just can't wait, though, visit **Gorga** on Infernos island, who will trade you 1 Sunstone for 3 Obsidian. Obsidian is obtained from the Lava Pits available after you upgrade to the Volcano island. ![](/game-mechanics/infernos-sunstones/exchange-sunstone.jpg) ## Node Purchase and Forging By visiting **Gunter** at the left side of the island you can exchange your Sunstones for various resource nodes to add to your home island. The price of each node increases as you craft them, and as always the amounts are listed at [https://sfl.world/info/const/#RESOURCE\_NODE\_PRICES](https://sfl.world/info/const/#RESOURCE_NODE_PRICES) ![](/game-mechanics/infernos-sunstones/buy-nodes.jpg) The Upgrade tab in Gunter's window allows you to combine, forge, or fuse resource nodes together, which will increase your resource output tremendously. Trees, Stones, Iron, and Gold rocks can all go through this process, with two tiers per node type. The cost to do this may be high, but the benefits will soon outweigh the price. Each Tier 2 node takes up the same amount of space as the standard node, but contains 4 nodes worth of resource, that is, you will extract four times more resources from the node per harvest. You do, however, need 4 tools to actually harvest it (4 Axes, Pickaxes, etc). Tier 3 nodes require 4 Tier 2 nodes to forge, which results in a total of 16 tools worth of resource in one harvest! In addition to saving space, each higher-tier node provides an **additional** boost to resource output. Every node you want to use in this process must be ready/fresh, that is, it must not have a cooldown timer after having been harvested. Remove them from your farm before visiting Infernos to make sure you only use the ones you want. With the new [Ascension](/en/mechanics/ascension) system, eventually you will gain more resource nodes than you have space for on your farm.
