title: Harvesting
markdown:
# Harvesting

The foundation of every farming game should be just that, farming! Sunflower Land provides with a dynamic and interesting way to grow crops, fruits, and other produce. Nearly everything starts in the ground, and many game mechanics work together to maximize the fertility of your land.

## Crops

The term “crops” refers to plants that are grown in Crop Plots. You will have several of these on your farm when you begin the game, and will earn more as you expand. Any crop plot can grow any kind of seed, provided it is currently in season. All crops start out as seeds, which you can buy from the Farmer's Market on your home island. 

When you select a seed from the Market or from your inventory Basket, it will appear at the top of the quick-select bar at the right of the screen. These are your three most recently selected items, and you can choose one of the other two to become the active selection at the top. There is no confirmation when you plant a seed, so make sure you are putting the right one in the right place! There is also no way to destroy or remove a seed from a plot once it has been planted. Even if you use the farm designer (hand) tool to remove the plot from your farm, it will retain the growing seed inside your inventory and continue to mature once you replace it. 

Once you've planted a seed, a number will appear over the plot with the rounded time remaining until harvest, and a green bar to represent it another way. These timers can be disabled via Game Options → General Settings → Preferences → Timers, if you want. You can also tap or mouse over the plot to see the specific amount of time down to the minutes or seconds.

### Harvest Security

Sometimes when you harvest a crop, you won't get the product right away, a blue bar appears underneath it and you will need to click on the crop a second time. A window pops up asking you to do a simple CAPTCHA-like challenge, either tapping the chest on the field or choosing the goblins among the other green things. Don't worry, this is perfectly normal, and is part of the game's ongoing effort to combat bots and other bad actors.

After solving the puzzle, you'll get an extra 1-3 seeds for the crop you just harvested, which is useful for the more expensive seeds.

If you fail to solve the puzzle by clicking on the wrong elements, you will be locked out of the game for 5 minutes. Take a break before getting back to farming!

If these harvest pop-ups start to become annoying, don't worry. Once you fulfill all of the following criteria, they will stop appearing (and you will still get bonus seeds periodically!):

*   Reach Bumpkin level 60
*   Have active VIP status
*   Complete face verification at the Retreat

### Crop Type

Crops are divided into three types: Basic, Medium, and Advanced. 

Basic crops grow quickly, between 1-30 minutes. They are designed for a more active play style of constantly harvesting and replanting, and can actually yield a higher profit than the slower growing crops. The skill Young Farmer increases their output by +0.1.

Medium crops are predictably in the middle, taking between 1-12 hours per harvest. They play an important role in many recipes and products. The skill Experienced Farmer increases medium yield by +0.1.

Advanced crops take the longest, ranging from 16-48 hours before maturity. These are best to plant overnight, or if you will be away from the game for a while. The skill Old Farmer increases advanced yield by +0.1 also. The skill Strong Roots decreases their long growth times by 10%.

There are two specialization skills, Acre Farm and Hectare Farm. Acre Farm increases the yield of Advanced crops by +1, while decreasing Basic and Medium by -0.5. Conversely, Hectare Farm boosts Basic and Medium by +1 and decreases Advanced by -0.5. Taking both of these skills does even out to +0.5 for all crop types, but choosing one over the other can lead to some serious boosts in output and profit.

You can see the type of a crop in the Farmer's Market either by selecting it in the Buy tab or in the Guide tab. Seeds are organized in your inventory by type order.

### Plot Fertility (Water Well)

As you expand your farm and gain more crop plots, you will find some to be grayed out and unusable. It's time to build a Water Well! Find in the workbench and place it somewhere on your farm. It does not have to be anywhere near the plots themselves. As you continue to expand, you will need to upgrade the well, to a maximum level of 4. You can see the requirements for the well upgrades at [https://sfl.world/info/const/#BUILDINGS](https://sfl.world/info/const/#BUILDINGS)

The well was not always upgradeable, instead you had to place multiple wells on your farm to handle more crops. If you still happen to have an extra well, visit Garbo so he can take it off your hands.

### Fertilizers

Crops do better with some love and attention, and you can help your plant along before it's ready. Fertilizers can be applied while a crop is growing. Sprout Mix will increase the yield by a flat +0.2, while Rapid Root will decrease the **remaining** growing time by 50%. For that reason it's almost always best to use Rapid Root as soon as you plant a crop, or on an empty plot that you're about to plant into.

You can only apply one fertilizer to a plot, and only once per harvest. You can apply fertilizer to a plot while it is empty, and it will boost the next crop grown in it. You can't apply any fertilizer to a fully grown crop.

You can combine the effects of the two crop fertilizers at the [Aging Shed](/en/mechanics/fermentation); Sproutroot Surprise will decrease growing time by 50% and add +0.2 to yield at the same time.

While you cannot harvest all of your plots at once without a [special item](https://sfl.world/info/pets), there is a way to mass-apply fertilizer. The Sprout Surge power skill adds Sprout Mix to all crop plots on your farm that don't already have a fertilizer added to them, while Root Rocket does the same for Rapid Root. 

### Bee Swarm

If you're lucky enough to get a pollination celebration from your beehive, the bonus will be applied on top of any other fertilizer you have already added, **and** it will stack with subsequent bee swarms. Take the skill Pollen Power Up to increase the boost to +0.3, and Bee Collective to increase the chance of a swarm by another 20%

### Scarecrows

There are three items you can craft which will directly boost your crop outputs, and are well worth the investment. Each scarecrow will only affect the crops planted in a 3x3 grid directly below it, as shown by the glowing square when placing it. This range can be increased to 7x7 with a skill specific to each scarecrow.

The Basic Scarecrow reduces the growing time of the already quick Basic crops by another 20%. The Chonky Scarecrow skill increases the range and reduces growth time by an additional 10%.

Scary Mike frightens your Medium crops into producing another +0.2 yield boost. The Horror Mike skill increases the range of effect and increases the boost to +0.3.

Laurie the Chuckle Crow stands watchful over your Advanced crops, increasing the yield by +0.2. Spending skill points on Laurie's Gains increases the range and boost to +0.3 as well.

It's important to note that the area of effect for the scarecrows can overlap, meaning the boost will be applied to multiple types of crops planted in their range. Even if all are lined up in a row and their range increased, however, you cannot have all three affect the exact same area.

## Fruit

Fruit Patches are unlocked once you advance your island to Petal Paradise, and they are worth your time. Fruit seeds are available in the market alongside crop seeds, according to the current season. They cost a bit more than crop seeds, but as you can see from their description, you will get multiple harvests from each one.

After you plant a fruit seed, it will take the listed time to produce one harvest. After harvesting, the timer will restart and grow another (replenishing). You **must** harvest the fruit before another one will start growing, so keep an eye on them. 

Once the number of harvests has been reached, the fruit plant will die and turn into a stick or stump. You need to have an Axe to cut it down and return the plot to an empty state before you can plant another seed. In return, you will get 1 Wood. Take the skill No Axe No Worries to be able to clear dead plots without an Axe, at the cost of receiving no Wood. Or, take Fruity Woody to boost the Wood return by +1. Taking both gives you +1 Wood with no Axe usage.

The game does not indicate to you how many harvests remain on each of your fruits. If you really want to know, however, you can find out at [https://sfl.world/map/](https://sfl.world/map/) (Enter your Farm ID)

### Quick Select

When you click or tap on a fruit patch and do not have a fruit seed in your quick-select bar, you will be shown a popup of the currently available seeds for that plot. Selecting one will plant it in that patch, and make it be your currently selected item (even if you take the skill No Axe No Worries). You can turn this off if you choose in Game Options → General Settings → Preferences → Quick Select. Clearing a spent plot will cause the Axe to be your current item, so you will need to quick-select again to continue planting.

### Fruit “Type”

The game does not divide each fruit up into types like it does for crops, but clear groupings can be seen.

Tomatoes and Lemons can be considered Basic fruit, as they take 2-4 hours to produce one harvest. The skill Zesty Vibes will increase their yield by +1, while decreasing the other four by -0.25. The skill Crime Fruit also increases the amount of stock at the market for both by +10.

Blueberries and Oranges are Medium fruit, clocking in at 6-8 hours each. The skill Short Pickings decreases their growth time by 25%, while adding 10% to the growth time of all others.

Apples and Bananas make up Advanced fruit, taking 12 hours between each harvest. The skill Long Pickings does the same for these two, decreasing by 25% at the cost of all other fruit taking 10% longer.

Three of the six fruits can be planted per season, and one of them is always valid for the season following the current one. For example, Oranges grow from spring through summer, while Apples are viable from autumn all the way to the end of winter. Use this fact when planning your orchard to ensure maximum output.

In addition, the monthly “[moon berries](/en/mechanics/seasons#full-moon)” of Celestine (Basic), Lunara (Medium), and Duskberry (Advanced) fall into a category of their own. Many fruit boosts and bonuses apply to these three as well.

### Fertilizer

The primary fruit fertilizer is Fruitful Blend, created at the Turbo Composter. It will increase the output of every harvest on a plant by +0.1. It does not need to be reapplied until the plant dies and a new one is planted. The Fruitful Bounty skill doubles the effect of this fertilizer, making a total boost of +0.2 to every harvest. The Blend-Tastic skill allows you to apply Fruitful Blend fertilizer to every fruit patch at once, which can be very useful to ensure every one has been treated.

At the [Aging Shed](/en/mechanics/fermentation), you can combine Fruitful Blend with Rapid Root to make Turbofruit Mix, which increases yield by +0.1 and decreases the growth time of every harvest in the fruit's lifecycle by 20%. The skills for Fruitful Bounty don't affect Turbofruit Mix.

### Pear and Macaw

You can craft an item at your workbench called the Immortal Pear, which when placed on your farm will increase the number of harvests per plot by +2. This will only happen for fruits you plant after you place it, not for fruits that are already growing. The skill Pear Turbocharge doubles the effect of this item, giving a total of +4 harvests per plot. The Pear's bonus does not affect the three Moon Berries, they are fixed at 6 harvests per seed.

You can also “craft” the Macaw, which increases the yield of all fruit patches by +0.2. The skill Loyal Macaw increases this boost to +0.4. Both items can be placed anywhere, including in your house, to take effect.

## Composters

The fertilizers that you need to improve your farm come from Composters, a set of three items that you can build from your workbench. What goes into these wonderful devices? Crops and fruit, of course! (And sometimes Eggs) Each composter requires a different set of items that changes each season. As appropriate for a three-tier system, each one requires a higher grade of resources as you step up. You can see the full list of requirements broken down by season at [https://sfl.world/info/const/#SEASON\_COMPOST\_REQUIREMENTS](https://sfl.world/info/const/#SEASON_COMPOST_REQUIREMENTS)

After you start it cooking, a composter can be sped up by adding Eggs, which will decrease the time remaining by 2 hours. If it has less than 2 hours remaining, it will complete immediately. The Feathery Business skill will change the boost to require Feathers rather than Eggs, but it will take twice as many. The Composting Bonanza skill will increase the boost time to 3 hours, but increase the resource requirement by another factor of two. If you're using Feathers already, this could make it too expensive to continue boosting.

If you don't fish that much, you can take the Composting Revamp skill, which will increase the fertilizer output of each unit by +5, while decreasing the worm output by -2. This may result in you getting no worms at all unless you boost them another way. Conversely, the Composting Overhaul skill will boost worm production by +2, while leaving fertilizer output unchanged. 

### Compost Bin

The first composter you will build, this one is the smallest and requires the simplest crops, mostly Basic and some Medium. In return, you will get the humble Sprout Mix, along with a few Earthworms for fishing. The Efficient Bin skill increases the fertilizer amount by +5.

### Turbo Composter

Despite its name, this composter actually produces Fruitful Blend, but takes only Medium and Advanced crops. You'll also end up with fishing Grubs. The Turbo Charged skill increases the output of Fruitful Blend by +5.

### Premium Composter

This composter is so high-end, it requires a mountain of Gold to build, not to mention the expensive fruits and Eggs needed to make it work. It will give you not only the coveted Rapid Root, but also Red Wigglers, the highest-tier fishing bait. The Premium Worms skill boosts Rapid Root output by +10, not worm output, but there is another skill to increase that.

## Greenhouse

The Greenhouse is an advanced building that is only available for players on the Desert Island, and requires a large amount of resources to build and use. Once it is ready, though, it provides unique crops that you can't grow anywhere else.

Greenhouse crops grow from seeds bought from the market. The greenhouse only has four plots, and cannot currently be expanded. Composter fertilizers cannot be applied to greenhouse plots, but there are two which can be created at the [Aging Shed](/en/mechanics/fermentation). In addition, the output and growth time of each crop can be increased or decreased by various skills. The quick-select system used in fruit patches also works on greenhouse seeds. 

All three crops require Oil, which must be added to the greenhouse's machine before you can plant a seed in a plot. Oil can only be added in multiples of 5, or you can empty your entire inventory into it at once (up to 100 units maximum). The requirements for each seed are displayed on the screen where you add Oil, and can be affected through various skills.

Greenhouse crops can be grown in any season, since it is a protected environment. The consensus among most players is that the greenhouse is too expensive to run until much later in the game, but if you want to ensure you will always be a contributing member for your [Faction Pet](/en/factions/pet), or be able to handle any [delivery](/en/mechanics/deliveries) from any NPC, you may choose to use it despite the cost.

For some reason, boosts that affect the growth time of crops will speed up Rice and Olives, but not Grapes. Boosts that reduce the growth time of fruits will also not affect Grapes. The only real way to reduce Grape time is the Rice and Shine skill.

## **Crop Machine**

The Crop Machine is your automated farming station, unlocked on Desert Island. It runs on oil, consuming it for every batch it processes. Once powered, it grows crops automatically and keeps working even while you’re offline.

You can queue up to five batches, though only one runs at a time. Each crop has its own seed capacity and growth time inside the machine, separate from regular plots. Crops grown here ignore seasons, so you can produce them at anytime. You can also buy seeds for every crop your machine supports at any time, regardless of season (they will also be included in your daily Free Restock). Finished batches can be collected at any point with no risk of decay or penalty. Because of the way crop yield bonuses work, though, it can be worthwhile to wait until a Bountiful Harvest event occurs before emptying the machine. Fertilizers cannot be applied to the Crop Machine in any way.

Adding seeds is done in batches of 10, so if you have less than 10 seeds for a crop you cannot add them. The All button in the add seeds dialog allows you to add every seed in your inventory, provided you have at least 10. Each set of 10 seeds take the base growth time of the crop to grow, but they are harvested and replanted automatically. You can remove a pack of seeds if it is not actively being processed.

Any boosts you have to decrease crop growth time do not affect the Crop Machine, except for those that specifically state that they reduce the production time of the Crop Machine. All boosts that affect the yield of a crop, whether flat or percentage-based, **will** work when harvesting a completed pack.

Oil is added at a base rate of 1 unit per 1 hour, to a maximum of 2 days of runtime (however much Oil that requires). Decreasing oil usage with skills or items makes it require less oil per hour added. If you add seed packs that will take longer than the machine has oil runtime to produce, it will not warn you or prompt you to add more oil, it will simply stop working when the time runs out. Since you cannot extract a partially-finished set of seeds, it is usually better to process smaller batches than larger ones, unless you know you will be away from the game for a long period of time and want to keep it growing while you are gone.

Through skill upgrades, you can expand queue capacity, reduce oil costs, increase efficiency and more. However, the general player consensus is that the Crop Machine is expensive to operate and not very profitable unless you’ve invested multiple skill points into its related upgrades. Having SFTs that boost supported crop yields can also make a big difference, turning what’s normally a costly system into a steady source of resources. Even items that provide chance-based boosts like the Peeled Potato (20% chance of +1 potato on harvest) work with the machine; the game simply calculates these boosts as though you had grown each potato seed manually and increases your yield accordingly.

Because of the rough nature of the Crop Machine, you will never get bonus seeds after harvesting anything in it. While the power of a Bountiful Harvest adds +1 to your machine yields, the quickening effects of a Sunshower do not affect the speed of processing.

# Mining

_This page discusses node forging (grouping), an upcoming feature that may change before final release_

# Mining

Mining is essential for obtaining valuable minerals, which allow you to do multiple things:

*   Create fishing rods.
*   Craft pickaxes to mine minerals.
*   Build oil drills to extract oil.
*   Use minerals to expand your land.
*   Use minerals to construct or upgrade buildings.
*   Use minerals to acquire SFTs from the blacksmith.
*   Craft shovels and drills to find treasures on the beach.
*   Complete deliveries.

In short, we need to mine (or buy minerals from the market) to progress in the land or simply enjoy the various activities mentioned above.

The basic flow of mining is: chop trees → use the wood for pickaxes to get stone → make stone pickaxes to get iron → make iron pickaxes to get gold → make gold pickaxes to get Crimstone or Sunstone.

## Stone

To obtain **stone**, we need to craft a pickaxe, which will allow us to mine the **Stone Rock**.

![](/pickaxe.png)

Cost and restock of pickaxes

As we progress through the game, we’ll be able to obtain **Sunstone**, which can be used to unlock additional **Stone Rock** nodes. The initial cost for the first Stone Rock node is **4 Sunstone**, and it increases by **+3 Sunstone** for each subsequent node.

![](/stone_rock.png)

Stone Rock

Soon, it will be possible to **group Stone Rocks together** to obtain more stone and make mining more convenient.

![](/fused_stone_rock.png)

Fused and Reinforced Stone Rock cost

💡 **Tip:** If you’re new to the game, I recommend getting the **Stone Beetle** from the blacksmith as soon as possible.

![](/stone_beetle.png)

Stone Beetle from Blacksmith

## Iron

To obtain **iron**, we need to craft a stone pickaxe, which will allow us to mine the **Iron Rock**.

![](/stone_pickaxe.png)

Cost and restock of stone pickaxes

As we progress through the game, we’ll be able to obtain **Sunstone**, which can be used to unlock additional **Iron Rock** nodes. The initial cost for the first Iron Rock node is **7 Sunstone**, and it increases by **+5 Sunstone** for each subsequent node.

![](/iron_rock.png)

Iron Rock

Soon, it will be possible to **group Iron Rocks together** to obtain more iron and make mining more convenient.

![](/fused_iron_rock.png)

Refined and Tempered Iron Rock cost

💡 **Tip:** If you’re new to the game, I recommend getting the **Iron Beetle** from the blacksmith as soon as possible.

![](/iron_beetle.png)

Iron Beetle from Blacksmith

## Gold

To obtain **gold**, we need to craft a iron pickaxe, which will allow us to mine the **Gold Rock**.

![](/iron_pickaxe.png)

Cost and restock of iron pickaxes

As we progress through the game, we’ll be able to obtain **Sunstone**, which can be used to unlock additional **Gold Rock** nodes. The initial cost for the first Gold Rock node is **10 Sunstone**, and it increases by **+6 Sunstone** for each subsequent node.

![](/gold_rock.png)

Gold Rock

Soon, it will be possible to **group Gold Rocks together** to obtain more gold and make mining more convenient.

![](/fused_gold_rock.png)

Pure and Prime Gold  Rock cost

💡 **Tip:** If you’re new to the game, I recommend getting the **Gold Beetle** from the blacksmith as soon as possible.

![](/gold_beetle.png)

Gold Beetle from Blacksmith

## Crimstone

To obtain **Crimstone**, we need to craft a gold pickaxe, which will allow us to mine the **Crimstone Rock**. 

![](/gold_pickaxe.png)

Cost and restock of gold pickaxes

As we progress through the game, we’ll be able to obtain **Sunstone**, which can be used to unlock additional **Crimstone Rock** nodes. The initial cost for the first Crimstone Rock node is **20 Sunstone**, and it increases by **+20 Sunstone** for each subsequent node.

![](/crimstone_rock.png)

Crimstone Rock

## Mining skills

![](/mining_skills.png)

Mining skills

Having a **mining skill tree** allows us to create a strategy to optimize it.

Here are several examples:

*   **Stone Specialist:** **Rock’N’Roll, Speed Miner, Forge-Ward Profits, Frugal Miner, Rocky Favor**
*   **Iron Specialist:** **Rock’N’Roll, Iron Bumpkin, Forge-Ward Profits, Frugal Miner, Iron Hustle, Ferrous Favor**
*   **Gold Specialist:** You can use the Stone or Iron specialist setup (or even combine both if you want to be a complete player) and add **Golden Touch, Midas Sprint, Midas Rush**.
*   **Crimstone Specialist:** You can use the Stone or Iron specialist setup (or combine both if you want to be a complete player) and add **Fire Kissed, Fireside Alchemist**.

title: Cooking
markdown:
# Cooking

All of that farming makes a Bumpkin hungry, so sit down for a meal! In Sunflower Land, unlike in other farming games, experience is not earned by actions taken like harvesting crops or making deliveries, only from eating food. If you don't eat, you don't level, and leveling up has a host of benefits. So, order up and let's dig in!

There are five different cooking buildings that you will encounter in your journey, all of which exist on your home island. The process of cooking itself is fairly straightforward, just choose a building, pick your recipe, and start it cooking. While a recipe is in progress, you can speed it up by spending a number of Gems, which will decrease the closer the recipe is to completion.

Only one recipe can be cooking per building at a time, but if you have an active VIP status, you can queue up an additional three recipes that will start when the current recipe is done. Adding a recipe to the queue will take the ingredients from your inventory, but if you cancel it before it begins, the ingredients are returned. This feature is valuable enough to justify paying the VIP cost almost by itself.

If you don't recognize the icon for an ingredient in a recipe, tap or click on it to display its name. A full list of every recipe in every building along with their cost is available at [https://sfl.world/info/cooking](https://sfl.world/info/cooking)

Once you've cooked up some tasty treats, tap on wherever your primary Bumpkin has been placed on your farm, or use the upper-left portrait menu and select the Feed Bumpkin tab.

## Firepit

“Roast your Sunflowers, feed and level up your Bumpkin”

Run by a chef named Bruce, the Firepit is the first cooking building you will get as a new player (for free) and will serve you long into your farming career. The Firepit provides a number of simple recipes with relatively short cooking times, which means you will need to make quite a few to fulfill most deliveries. 

The skill Fast Feasts reduces the cooking time of all recipes in the Firepit by 10%, and the skill Fiery Jackpot provides a 20% chance that a meal collected from it will be doubled.

## Kitchen

“Step up your cooking game”

The next building you will add to your cooking arsenal, and the most versatile. The Kitchen has the largest number of recipes, and the most complex, including exotic ingredients like fish and greenhouse produce. Some even require other cooked foods for true culinary mastery.

The skill Fast Feasts reduces the cooking time of all recipes in the Kitchen by 10% (and the Firepit). 

## Smoothie Shack

“Freshly squeezed!”

This building makes exclusively juices and other blended drinks out of the fruits and vegetables you can grow on your farm. Some blends also need Eggs to make the consistency just right. 

The skill Juicy Boost increases the experience from drinks made at the shack by 10%.

## Deli

“Satisfy your appetite with these delicatessen foods!”

An advanced building and one of the most expensive to build, the Deli produces fermented products and other foods that require long cooking times. It is also the building that produces Cheese, which is an ingredient in many high-level foods.

The skill Drive-Through Deli increases the experience from deli foods by 10%.

## Bakery

“Bake your favorite cakes”

Eggs, wheat, and nearly every vegetable can be combined to make a tasty pastry of excellence. Cakes are used for many deliveries, and are among the foods asked for by Farm Pets and the Faction Pet too. You won't generally find yourself eating cakes unless there is a weekly chore asking you to, since they are better used elsewhere.

Cakes may take longer than any other food to bake, but the skill Frosted Cakes decreases the cooking time of the Bakery by 10%, and the Boar Shrine cuts that by another 25% (along with all other cooking buildings).

## Cooking with Oil

“Now we're cooking with gas!”

After you unlock the Desert Island and Oil Wells, you can add Oil to any of your cooking buildings to further reduce cooking time. The sub-window will tell you by how much cooking time will be reduced, and allow you to add as much as you choose to each building.

The total runtime will be displayed before you confirm your selection. After adding Oil, the next recipe cooked will benefit from the reduced time. Currently cooking recipes are unaffected. 

As dishes cook with the Oil boost, the time taken to cook them (before the boost) is deducted from the total runtime, until it reaches zero. If nothing is cooking, no time is used, so you don't need to worry about wasting precious oil if you have nothing to cook. That recipe that you had cooking when you added oil also doesn't affect the runtime, only those started afterwards. If a recipe would use up all the remaining runtime before its completion, the game will factor that into the cooking time accordingly. For maximum benefit, you will want to ensure enough runtime to cover the full cooking time of the recipe.

When you add a recipe to the VIP queue, the runtime is deducted, and if you cancel it, the time is added back to the building's total. There is currently no way to check the total time for a specific queued recipe, since it may be different than the stated value in the recipe list.

The amount of runtime added for 1 unit of oil is different for every building. The maximum amount of Oil a single building can hold is 5 days (120 hours) of runtime.

*   Firepit: 24 hours per unit
    *   Time is reduced by 20%, with skill Swift Sizzle, 40%
*   Kitchen: 4 hours, 48 minutes
    *   25% base reduction, 50% with skill Turbo Fry
*   Smoothie Shack: 3 hours
    *   30% reduction. No skill affects Smoothie Shack Oil time.
*   Deli: 2 hours
    *   40% base reduction, 60% with skill Fry Frenzy
*   Bakery (35% reduction): 2 hours, 24 minutes
    *   35% reduction. No skill affects Bakery Oil time.

Since oil is somewhat expensive, it is usually recommended to avoid using it to cook with unless there is a competition or other reason to decrease cooking time. The Firepit, though, with its very generous runtime, is usually worth adding a unit or two to keep those Mashed Potatoes coming.

title: Fishing
markdown:
# Fishing

![](/game-mechanics/fishing.png)

Need some anchovies…

# Fishing

The oceans are full of aquatic treasures, and fishing is how you'll claim them for yourself! Grab a rod, some bait and chum, and get your feet wet for some satisfying rewards.

Fish are important for a wide range of applications, from cooking and eating, to deliveries, chores, and bounties. Nearly every fish is useful in some way, and you might find some other valuable things at the end of your line…

There are multiple pages for fishing on sfl.world. The landing page is at [https://sfl.world/info/fishing/info](https://sfl.world/info/fishing/info), while the list of  fish and suggestions on how to catch them are available here: [https://sfl.world/info/fishing/type](https://sfl.world/info/fishing/type)

## Fishing Rods

To get any fishing done, first you need a Rod. Visit the Workbench on your Home Island to make one out of some Wood and Stone, with a small fee of Coins as well. You can decrease the fee by 50% with the skill Reel Deal, but it reduces it from 20 to 10, which will only be a savings in the long run.

Unfortunately the craftsmanship on Rods is rather shoddy, and they will break after a single use. Rods have a stock limit like any other tool, but some are included in the free daily restock.

## Bait

The second component is bait. There are three tiers of bait, corresponding with the three tiers of fish.

*   Basic Bait
    *   Earthworm- Produced from the Compost Bin
    *   Capsule Bait- Made at the [Aging Shed](/en/mechanics/fermentation) from aged basic fish and pickled zucchini/tomatoes.
*   Advanced Bait
    *   Grub- Produced from the Turbo Composter
    *   Umbrella Bait- Made at the Aging Shed from aged advanced fish and pickled broccoli/peppers.
*   Expert Bait
    *   Red Wiggler- Produced from the Premium Composter
    *   Crimson Baitfish- Made at the Aging Shed from aged expert fish and pickled radishes/onions.

Each of the three fermented baits can also be purchased from the Marketplace when you need some more right away.  

You will also get some of the three composter worms from the daily rewards chest, once per week. Bait can be found in some other places, too, so keep exploring!

The Fishing Lure is a special kind of bait that can be obtained by trading with [Finn](/en/npcs/finn) at the Beach, or as a reward from several types of chests. It is used to catch some special fish, so use them sparingly.

## Chum

You can fish with just bait, but you have a much better haul if you add some chum also. Technically chum is optional, and many fish can be caught without it, but most fish have a preferred chum that will increase your chances of catching it substantially. Once you choose a chum, it will remain selected until you change it, so pay attention if you're trying with something rare or valuable. 

## Cast your line

Once you have all of your equipment together, visit the fisher at the bottom-left corner of your Home Island and Cast away! Wait a moment and click or tap on the Reel icon, then see what you've caught.

 There is a limit on the amount of fishing you can do in a day, shown in the window as “# reels left". This can be increased with the skills Fisherman's 5 Fold (+5), Fisherman's 10 Fold (+10), and More with Less (+15). There are also many items and decorations which increase fishing limit, some of which you'll earn just through fishing. If you find yourself completely out of reels, you can buy 5 more for 5 Gems.

The fish you get is determined by a random roll, influenced by your bait, chum, and the current season. There are some fish that can be caught 100% of the time, regardless of season, with the right combination.

*   Anchovy
    *   Basic Bait + 10x Carrot (cheapest)
    *   Basic Bait + 5x Egg
*   Tuna
    *   Advanced Bait + 3x Orange
    *   Advanced Bait + 1x Wild Mushroom (technically cheapest, since mushrooms are free, but can't be bought in bulk like Oranges)
*   Red Snapper
    *   Expert Bait + 3x Apple (cheapest)
    *   Expert Bait + 1x Honey

Since these three are the most commonly requested fish for deliveries and are used in the fish market and [aging shed](/en/mechanics/fermentation), they are worth memorizing, especially during the Fish Frenzy.

## Multi cast

If you have VIP status, you can work your fisherperson extra hard and spend multiple rods and reels at the same time. Just select the number you want to use at once, ensure you have all the resources you need, and cast a wide net. You will use the same bait and chum for every cast, and unless you choose one of the guaranteed catch combinations, you will get a wide variety of fish in return. All bonuses and buffs will resolve automatically.

If you do choose to use a fish product for a guaranteed catch, you must choose the same fish for every cast.

## Fish Types

Fish are categorized into types, just like many other things in the game. You can see each of the basic, advanced, and expert fish in your Codex, along with which you've caught, the season to find them in, and some suggestions on how to catch them again. There are several skills (the Fishy group) that will increase the chances of you getting another fish when you catch one in a specific category.

Marine Marvels are a rare type of fish that require special circumstances, but are so valuable that you can place them on your farm in a tank for all to see.

Chapter Fish are even rarer Marvels that are only available during the current Chapter and provide different boosts. But, you can trade some of them on the marketplace if you missed out.

The Codex also shows you the rewards you can earn from certain fishing achievements. There's no indication in the game as to when you unlock one, so check back often!

## Cooking & Preparing (Fish Market)

Fish can be eaten for XP, but it is almost never a good idea to do so. Foods prepared from fish are **always** worth more XP, and some are even used for deliveries. The only time you would want to eat fish raw is when a Weekly Chore requests you to do so. Even then, consider whether the tickets and points are worth the value of the fish in products or recipes.

The skill Fishy Feast increases the XP of raw fish, aged fish, **and** foods made with fish products. All other boosts that increase the XP value “of fish” affect eating fish directly and foods prepared with them.

You'll notice that your cooking buildings don't take raw fish as ingredients. First you must prepare your catches at the Fish Market, another building that you need to place on your farm. There, you can produce four different items with the fish and crustaceans you have caught, and then cook them at your Kitchen and Firepit. It may take a while to prepare the fish product, but the edible recipes are cooked instantly, to save you time! What's more, if you are a VIP player you can cook an instant recipe right away, even if all of your queue slots are full.

The Fish Market is not considered a cooking building, so boosts that affect cooking time or output do not apply to fish preparation. There are other NFT items that can boost your fish processing times, though.

There are only four fish products, but the ingredients that go into them change every in-game Season. As always, you can see the complete schedule at [https://sfl.world/info/fishing/info#FISH\_MARKET\_RECIPES](https://sfl.world/info/fishing/info#FISH_MARKET_RECIPES)

## Guaranteed Catch

Products prepared at the Fish Market are not only tasty for your Bumpkin, they are irresistible to fish too. Sometimes you just can't afford to spend all your rods and reels on pot luck, and need a specific fish for a delivery or recipe. Fortunately, you can use the power of fish products to ensure that you always get the fish you need instead of a lot of Seaweed (unless you want Seaweed, of course).

Choose a fish product as your Bait when fishing. Then, you can pick exactly which fish you want to pluck out of the ocean. You can't use Chum when doing a guaranteed catch. 

The complete list of guaranteed catches with fish products is at [https://sfl.world/info/fishing/info#FISH\_MARKET\_GUARANTEED](https://sfl.world/info/fishing/info#FISH_MARKET_GUARANTEED)

You may notice that there is no mention of Season in the guaranteed list. This is because with products, you can catch **any** fish during **any** Season. This will help make your fishing empire grow much more smoothly, and allow you to make deliveries more easily and get the category rewards much more easily.

You can use VIP multi-cast with products, but you will get the same fish on every cast.

## Crustaceans

While fish are definitely valuable, there are other aquatic creatures that just can't be caught with a rod and reel. Next to your pier will be several posts in the water, some of which will have crabs at the bottom, others will have a gull on top. These are where you can place your water traps. You will gain more automatically as you upgrade your island.

Visit your Workbench on your farm to have the Blacksmith put together some Crab Pots or Mariner Pots. Both have their own stock that is replenished with the paid Workbench Restock, not the free daily Restock. Once you have at least one, set it out on a pier and wait. Crab Pots take 4 hours to finish, and Mariner Pots take 8. Make sure to select a chum to go with it, though.

If you have at least one of the resources that can be used as a chum, it will appear in the window, but you may not have enough of that resource to actually use it. As always, you can see the complete list of chums and what they catch here [https://sfl.world/info/fishing/info#CRUSTACEANS](https://sfl.world/info/fishing/info#CRUSTACEANS)

Another major difference from fishing is that each chum will **always** catch the corresponding crustacean. There is no RNG involved. Using no chum in a Crab Pot will always get you an Isopod, never any other kind of creature.

Bonuses that affect the number of fish caught do not work for water traps, including the Fishing Frenzy event. There are other NFT items that will boost your pot readiness time and the yield from each one.

Crustaceans are used to complete requests on the Mega Bounty Board, and for deliveries to a certain NPC. You can also use them to create a Crab Stick at your Fish Market, which is then used to catch some very valuable fish. You can also cook the Crab Stick into an edible meal on its own.

## Treasures

There are other things you can catch other than fish, such as Seaweed, Sea Cucumbers, and Old Bottles. These are valuable on their own, but do not count as fish for the purposes of boosts that increase the number of fish you get per catch. Some are used for deliveries and crafting, others can be sold at [Jafar's shop](/en/mechanics/digging) at the Beach for Coins, and a few can be processed into Salt at the [Aging Shed](/en/mechanics/fermentation).

## Marine Marvel Maps

Marine Marvels are rare fish that take some work to find and catch, and are so valuable that you can place them as decorations on your farm! There are five permanent Marvels that can be caught at any time, and between 1-3 Chapter Marvels that are only obtainable during the current Chapter, but can usually be bought from the Marketplace later on.

Finding one isn't just up to a random number roll like it used to be, either. When catching certain fish, you may see a sparkle in the water and get an opportunity to score a Map Piece for a specific Marvel. Complete the minigame and it will be yours!

### Marvel Minigame

You will be shown a series of squares and need to click on one per row, starting at the bottom. If you find the correct path (arrow), you can then click on the next higher row. If you click on a crab, you will briefly be shown a few steps ahead and then all squares will flip back over. Remember the path as you uncover it and you'll be at the top in no time. If you choose incorrectly too many times, don't worry, just pay 1000 coins and get 4 more attempts. The Anemone Flower obtainable on the marketplace will give you an extra chance when map-finding.

Once you complete the minigame, you will get a map piece corresponding to one Marvel. Once you get all 9, the Marvel is yours! You can see how many map pieces you've discovered on the Fishing tab of your Codex.

### Map Piece Chances

Only certain fish have a chance of dropping map pieces, and some more than others. The table below lists the five “permanent” marvels, that are obtainable at any time regardless of in-game season or chapter. For the current chapter marvels, check out [https://sfl.world/info/fishing/info#MAP\_PIECES](https://sfl.world/info/fishing/info#MAP_PIECES) 

If you catch multiple fish using VIP multi cast, you can obtain multiple map pieces as well.

The Deep Sea Helm increases the chances of a piece dropping by +100%. Note this does not make a map piece guaranteed, it just adds the base chance to the total (i.e. if the base chance to get a map piece is 5%, the DSH increases the chance to 10%). This helmet is obtainable by catching at least 5 of every Basic, Advanced, and Expert Fish. Using fish products for a guaranteed catch on a Fish Frenzy day is an excellent way to accomplish this quickly.

The Full Moon monthly Event doubles the chances of a piece dropping again (+100%). For some Marvels this makes the chance over 100%, guaranteeing you will get a piece if you catch the required fish. For others, it makes a miniscule chance slightly less so.

The seasonal Guardians obtainable through the marketplace or at auction also affect the Full Moon Event, giving you a +200% increase for the day.

The Navigation Table item introduced in the Salt Awakening Chapter increases the chances by yet another +100%.

## Fish Frenzy

Every so often, the waters around your island will teem with life and a Fish Frenzy will begin. You will earn an additional fish every time you make a successful catch. This is on top of any other boosts you have that increase fish quantity, such as the Fishy skills. If those skills trigger you will get 3 fish, with the possibility for more.

The skill Frenzied Fish is considered the ultimate during the Fish Frenzy, as the event bonus increases to +2, and you have a 50% chance to get +3. Once again, every other chance for an additional fish still applies. 

The seasonal Guardian items increase the bonus of a Fish Frenzy to +2 when it occurs in their season.

## History

With the addition of the Fish Market and prepared products, many fish recipes were removed from the various cooking stations. All cooking recipes now use prepared fish products instead of raw fish. This caused some confusion during the first week of the new Chapter, when the Faction Pet for some factions didn't get the news and still asked for foods that couldn't be cooked any longer! Fortunately the issue was fixed quickly, and the Pets now content themselves with the new foods instead.

Previously there was another fisher NPC at the Beach, near the entrance to the Plaza. Fishing from there was functionally the same as fishing from your home island, but it meant there were two separate chance tables for each fishing location: Ocean fishing from the Beach, and Wharf fishing from the home island. Ultimately this was determined to be too complicated, so Corale chased off the Beach fisher and he hasn't been seen since.

In Chapters past, there was a time of day mechanic that affected fishing. Dawntide and Dusktide were the two halves of the day, and the chances for certain fish changed along with those tides. This was removed with Seasons, which now govern which fish can be caught and when.

title: Dig Site
markdown:
# Dig Site

![](/game-mechanics/digsite.png)

What will you dig up?

# Digging

Untold treasures await beneath the shifting sands at the upper end of the Beach. Grab some shovels and get to excavating, then enjoy the substantial rewards!

The Dig Site is located at the uppermost section of the Beach area. You can get there very quickly from your Home by first traveling to the Beach, which will put you at the lower exit by Corale. Then, teleport to the Kingdom, where you will be at the exit by the Mark Shop. Just walk to the left and you will be at Jafar's doorstep!

There are two NPCs who manage the Dig Site. Jafar crafts Sand Shovels and Sand Drills at his shop, and buys back any treasures you find for Coins. Digby monitors the site itself, and gives you tips on how to best excavate. Get yourself a tool, then enter the grid to begin digging. 

## Digging Tools

The primary tool you will use is the Sand Shovel, which uncovers a single square in the grid. It is slightly cheaper than a Fishing Rod, at 2 Wood and 1 Stone each, but has a lower stock of 50 pieces. The Toolshed building you can add to your Home Island does **not** increase the number of shovels per restock, and the Workbench Restock option does not replenish digging tools. To make up for that, the free daily restock includes 5 shovels, and the cost to restock only shovels and drills is a paltry 5 Gems. This will let you keep excavating without affecting the rest of your farm stock.

The other tool you can craft is the Sand Drill, which digs up a 2x2 area in the grid. It is useful, but rather expensive, requiring Oil, Crimstone, Wood, and Leather. There are also only 10 in a restock, but you may find some through rewards or chests, so use them when you have them.

## Dig Site

The digging area itself is a 10x10 grid of squares, which you can enter through a gap in the fence on the left or right sides, near Old Salty or Digby, respectively. While you may see other farmers trying their luck at digging also, don't worry about them getting in your way, as Pharaoh cast an ancient spell that gives you exclusive access to the sands. All other players will move to the edges of the fence as soon as you enter, and reappear where they actually are as soon as you leave. Powerful magic indeed, but very useful!

Every space in the grid contains something valuable in some way. Even Sand, which you will get a lot of, can be sold for Coins or saved up to unlock rare treasures at the shop. Like with Fishing, there is no real junk or any useless items.

The basic rule when digging is that if you find a Crab, there is another treasure orthogonally adjacent to it. That's a fancy way of saying that there is something else above, below, or to the left or right of the Crab. If you find Sand, there is nothing orthogonally adjacent other than more sand. 

So, if you find a Crab, dig around it. If you find Sand, dig somewhere else.

The magic that gives every player their own unrestricted access to the dig site also means that the location of the treasures is unique to each digger. If you're lucky enough to find a Pearl or other great item, you can't tell your friends about it because it (probably) won't be there for them if they dig in the same spot.

## Treasures

Everything that you can see under the Sell tab at Jafar's shop is something you can potentially dig up at the site. Some items you may recognize as fishing treasures also. Just because you can sell it, though, doesn't mean that you should. Many items are needed for deliveries, so you'll want to hang on to a few of each. Seaweed can be cooked into a useful food in your Firepit. You can also convert several treasures to Salt at the Aging Shed. Or, you can just sell them for Coins.

An important type of treasure is the Chapter Artifact, which changes at the beginning of each Chapter. You'll see past Artifacts in the shop list, and may see the next Chapter's when the current one nears its end. Keep as many of these as you can, and turn them in at the Megastore. Only sell them when their Chapter ends, or if you have bought all the items you can with them.

## Digby's Clues

Digby surveys the site each day and can provide some clues as to where to find different treasures, but he has an eye out for the Chapter Artifacts specifically. By talking to him, clicking the “New Dig Site!” button on the bottom of the screen, or visiting the Treasures tab of [https://sfl.world/land/](https://sfl.world/land/) (enter your Farm ID), you'll get some clues as to what to look for. Once you find all of the items in a pattern, it will be checked off the list. 

The patterns are consistent and recurring, for example you'll always find two vases with a hieroglyph underneath the left vase, three sea cucumbers in a row with a pipi at the far right, and so on. This will make digging easier as you learn the patterns and can recognize them as you go. You may also find other items that are not shown in the patterns, so keep digging!

If you can unearth all three of the Artifacts in a single day, Digby will give you a bonus prize (you don't have to find the camel bones also). This will include a fourth Artifact, as well as another item, randomly determined. By building up a daily streak, you can get even better rewards. Find all of the Desert Streaks at [https://sfl.world/info/chests](https://sfl.world/info/chests)

## Dig Limit

Like with many tasks in the game, there is a limit as to how many times you can dig in a day. This can be increased through several different items, one of which you can trade with Jafar for, and the rest you can find on the marketplace. There are currently no skills that affect digging in any way. Dig chances reset at midnight UTC along with many other things.

If you're really desperate, you can also convince Digby to give you a few extra chances in exchange for some of your precious Gems.

title: Crafting Box

# Crafting Box

![](/game-mechanics/crafting.png)

So full of possibilities…

# Crafting Box

“A box for crafting various items.”

Crafting is a game mechanic that will allow you to make certain items with the raw ingredients you collect on your farm, as well as making new ingredients entirely. To begin, collect 100 Wood and 5 Stone, then find the Crafting Box on the Build tab of your Workbench. Find a place to set it down and let's get making!

## Crafting Grid

The 3x3 crafting grid may look familiar, but fortunately you will be able to store everything you make in a recipe, and even earn new recipes from your travels around Sunflorea. To make a recipe for the first time, click on one of the items below, then click on a space in the grid. Assemble your creation and click Craft. If a recipe exists for your arrangement, it will begin crafting right away. Otherwise, it will fail and inform you that you need to rearrange it.

Most crafting recipes take time, though some are instant. You can spend Gems to instantly complete a project, or just go about your day and come back when it's complete. The Crafting Box will animate while it is working, though no timer appears below it like with some other buildings.

Once your project is done and you collect the item, the grid configuration remains and you can immediately craft another item, if you have enough resources. 

If you have an active VIP subscription, you will be able to queue up to 4 recipes and have them craft one after the other, just like with the cooking buildings. Instant recipes like Lumber will still complete instantly if a queue slot is open, so you can craft those while a Doll or other long-running item is still being worked.

## Recipes

Once you successfully craft something, it is stored in your box's memory as a Recipe. You can easily build it again by clicking the hammer icon for the recipe, which automatically populates the grid for you. Recipes are organized in categories, and you can search for a specific item using the search bar at the top of the window.

You may find recipe pages lying around your farm, especially when expanding or upgrading your land, or you may receive them as rewards when making deliveries to NPCs. As of the time of this writing, though, there is no restriction on crafting an item that you do not have a recipe for in-game. If you find the layout on [https://sfl.world/info/crafting](https://sfl.world/info/crafting) and put it in the grid, you can craft it. There are still some recipes that have yet to be discovered, though, so keep experimenting!

## What you can make

### Instant

This category of item is made up of components that go into other crafting recipes. Because of this, they can be crafted instantly with no wait time. 

### Dolls

These decorative crafts are used for several things. They are requested on the [Mega Bounty Board](/en/chapter-race/bounty-board), used for deliveries to a certain NPC, you will need them to be a Contributing Member for your [Faction Pet](/en/factions/pet), and you can also give them to any of your barn animals to wake them up instantly. Or, you can just place them on your farm and admire them!

Every doll starts with a basic Doll, which is just called Doll in the game. It requires Leather and Wool, which will probably require you to do some marketplace trading. After you have one, you can then “decorate” it with other items, making one of a whole host of dolls that are currently available. There are even a few that haven't been discovered yet…

### Beds

Beds are required to hire [Farmhands](/en/mechanics/farmhands), which are additional characters that live on your farm. The purpose of a Farmhand is to allow you to equip more wearable items than normal. If you have two hats, both of which provide a bonus, you can give the other to your Farmhand and enjoy both. Read the linked article for more details.

### Chapter Exclusives

These are special items that can only be crafted during the current chapter, and use resources specific to it. Don't forget to make a few before they disappear!
