title: Animals
markdown:
# Animals ## Animals | ![](https://sfl.world/img/animals/Chicken.png)
[**Chicken**](/en/mechanics/animals/chicken) | ![](https://sfl.world/img/animals/Sheep.png)
[**Sheep**](/en/mechanics/animals/sheep) | ![](https://sfl.world/img/animals/Cow.png)
[**Cow**](/en/mechanics/animals/cow) | | --- | --- | --- | Take a break from farming to do some ranching instead! Although, you'll need products from your farm if you want to get the maximum benefits out of each animal. Sunflower Land as a game is very generous when it comes to allowing new players access to its features. You don't have to wait very long to be able to do many different things in the game, but animal raising is one of those features where most experienced players will recommend you WAIT to begin. All animals require large amounts of food, and unless you have a huge stockpile of feed already, they will eat you out of farmhouse and home island before you know it. You can find all the hard numbers on ranching at [https://sfl.world/info/animals](https://sfl.world/info/animals) ## Animal Basics There are several elements that are common to every animal, so let's begin with those. There are two buildings that house animals, the Hen House contains chickens and the Barn houses both Sheep and Cows together. By default both buildings have 10 slots for animals, so you can have 10 chickens and 10 sheep or cows in any combination. Animals don't age and cannot die from neglect or underfeeding. ### Buying an animal When you first step into your new building, you'll find it empty. To buy your first animal, click on the bag/shop icon in the upper-right corner. Each creature costs Coins initially. You can buy as many as will fit in your building, as shown by the Capacity number at the bottom. ### Feeding an animal Once you have your new level 1 creature, it needs to be fed. Every animal requires an amount of food to gain experience and level up, and when reaching a new level, they will produce a certain resource and then fall asleep from the exertion. An animal that is awake and wanting food will display an icon above its head with the specific food it desires. There are currently five different types: * Kernel Blend- 1x Corn * Hay- 1x Wheat * NutriBarley- 1x Barley * Mixed Grain- 1x Corn, 1x Wheat, 1x Barley (3x Kale with skill Kale Mix) * Omnifeed- 1x Gem All foods are made at the Feeder Machine at the top of your building. Feed is stored in your inventory after you Mix it, and clicking on it in the Machine's window makes it the top item in your active bar, even if you don't Mix any. The feed you want **must** be the top item when you tap on your animal.  You can feed any animal any food at any stage of its life. However, you want to give it the food displayed above its head whenever possible as that will give it the maximum amount of XP. Any other food will give it half the amount of XP per feeding. So, pay attention to your item bar when it's feeding time. Feeding is structured according to “packs." Each animal requires a different amount of feed that must be given to it all at once for the feeding to be successful. At the basic, unboosted level, chickens require 1 unit of food per pack, Sheep 3, and Cows 5. Each level requires a different amount of packs, though, meaning you must feed the animal that many times and use a pack's worth of food each time. By looking at the charts at sfl.world, you can see that feeding gets expensive very quickly. Omnifeed is a special “wildcard” food that will give an animal full satisfaction from a feeding no matter what food it is currently requesting. While feeding your animals ground-up Gems may seem daunting, depending on the price of resources it may actually be cheaper to use Omnifeed instead of Mixed Grain, especially since you can now buy Gems directly with the FLOWER you earn from selling all of that Milk and Leather. ### XP and Levels An animal is awake until its XP bar is full, after which it will produce and fall asleep. Each pack of feed fills up the bar by a certain amount, and overflow is not lost. Meaning if they have 90/100 XP to the next level, and you feed them a pack worth 20 XP, they will have 10/100 XP afterward. Which will be helpful later on. Every animal requires different feed at different levels, but that breakdown is currently the same for all three types.  The highest level an animal can currently attain is 15. They will produce the most resources at this level, but also require the most food, so you must discern when to feed and when to sell. ### Sleep and Petting After an animal falls asleep, you must wait a while for them to regain their strength. But that doesn't mean you should ignore them. Periodically when an animal is asleep, they will request (subconsciously) that you give them some attention. An icon will appear with one of three tools in it: the Petting Hand, Brush, or Music Box. All three of these are available at your Workbench on your home island. The time interval for each affection session is shown if you click on the animal itself, and it is calculated by taking the total sleep (production) time for the animal and dividing it by 3. That timer isn't shown in the game, but it will reset only when you pet the animal. Unlike with feeding, you don't have to select the “right” tool to use on an animal when it's sleeping. If you have the tool it requests, you'll use it when tapping, and if you don't, you won't. Don't worry if you haven't saved up enough Coins for that Music Box, though, since petting can only give bonuses, not penalties. Petting an animal will give it some bonus XP, depending on the tool you used. This means **it will require less feed** when it wakes up again, which is absolutely critical when dealing with high-level animals. It's even possible to level up an animal while it's sleeping, meaning it will produce as soon as it wakes up (and then fall back asleep again). If you can't pet it before it wakes up since you don't have the right tool, it won't gain any XP, but won't lose any, either. If you really need that extra Egg for a recipe right away, you can give your animal a Doll of a specific kind. That will wake it up, allowing you to feed it again and get an extra product. The dolls required for an animal of a certain level are shown at the sfl.world link above, or you can tap on the animal and it will tell you which one it wants. Level 15 animals cannot currently be woken with dolls. ### Spice Boosts After you get your [Aging Shed](/en/mechanics/fermentation) up and running, you can create two different items that will affect your animals. The Salt Lick will increase the amount of your animal's produce by 5%, and the Honey Treat will decrease the amount of feed they require per pack by 25%. Each of these treats will last for 3 harvest cycles, and you can only apply one or the other to a single animal, not both. ### Sickness Periodically your animals will become sick, gaining an icon above their head. Sick animals will drop half the amount of resources when leveled up, and the sickness is contagious: every sick animal increases the chances of another animal becoming sick every day. You must cure them as soon as possible, and fortunately the cure is in the Feeder Machine. Mix up some Lemons and Honey into Barn Delight and give it to the sick animal to have them feeling right as rain. It's possible to sell a sick animal if you can't afford the medicine, but be aware you will only get 75% of the bounty rewards compared to if it was well. Tea with lemon and honey is an effective remedy in the real world, too. Previously, Barn Delight required Iron and Eggs to mix, which was a curious combination for medicine. ### Selling and Bounties When that Cow starts asking for Mixed Grain, you know it's time to let it go. At the same menu where you buy your animals, you can sell them too. Each building has its own Bounty Board, where you can sell up to 10 chickens, or 5 cows and 5 sheep, as long as they are of the required level (the amount of bounties increases with the level of the building). There are three categories of bounties: Coins, Chapter Tickets, and Gems, the last of which only appears on Auction Week or the weeks between Chapters. An animal must be awake to sell it, so check the Board first thing in the morning before you start feeding. If an animal is sick, you can still sell it, though you will only get 75% of the reward listed for the bounty (rounded down). While you may be hesitant to sell that animal you've spent so long caring for, keep in mind that high-level animals require much more food than lower-level ones, so you may end up spending more in feed than it would cost you to just buy the resources it is producing on the marketplace. Check [https://sfl.world/boost/](https://sfl.world/boost/) (enter your farm ID) to see your specific farm's output, and whether you should push that cow to level 11 or let it feed some hungry goblins instead. ## Building Upgrades If you find your Hen House to be too cramped, or if you think it's time to expand your dairy empire, each building can be upgraded to hold additional animals. The requirements and benefits can be seen at the Upgrade button in the upper-left of each building. You can also look ahead at [https://sfl.world/info/animals](https://sfl.world/info/animals) and see that the maximum upgrade is very expensive. Each of the two buildings can hold a maximum of 15 animals when fully upgraded, but if you need even more, find the Barn Blueprint item to maximize your ruminant capacity, or the Chicken Coop for more Chickens than you can handle. ## Mutant Animals Every so often, when obtaining resources after feeding an animal, you may obtain a rare mutant animal. These are randomly determined according to the current Chapter, and while very unlikely, you can find more than one. Obviously the more animals you are handling at once, the more chances you have to find a mutant, and if you really want to get your hands on one, the Rooster item available in the marketplace will double the chances of you finding a mutant Chicken. There are currently no items that boost the chance for a mutant Sheep or Cow. Every mutant animal so far has had a powerful boost, so you can use them to your advantage or sell them on the marketplace when the Chapter ends for top FLOWER.  Don't get frustrated if you don't see any for a while, though, the chance is so small that many players who have been playing since animals were introduced have never encountered a mutant. ## Specialization Skills Or: how to make animals more worthwhile Just by looking at the numbers at [https://sfl.world/info/animals](https://sfl.world/info/animals), you may think that raising animals just isn't worth your time. 60 Barley for 3 Milk and 3 Leather? Without any boosts, you'd be absolutely right. However, there are **many** ways to make your ranching journey more bearable. First of all, just like in the real world, any feed you grow yourself is feed you don't have to buy. All crops are cheaper when grown from seed compared to when bought on the marketplace, so if you can keep up your production of Corn, Wheat, and Barley when they are in season, you will dramatically reduce your feed budget. The Acre Farm crops skill will also be a great boon to you, as each of the feed crops are Advanced and that +1 bonus will go a long way. There are a few NFT items that boost the output of those crops as well, but they are well out of the reach of the beginner player. Unless you have unlimited money at your disposal, but then why would you be worrying about reducing costs? The Kale Mix skill might sound attractive, until you do the math and see that 3 Kale can be more expensive than one each of the other grains (cereals). Since taking the skill permanently changes the requirement for the recipe, you can't pick and choose depending on market conditions. And, Kale can only be grown for two weeks out of the month, while the three grains collectively can be grown all month long. The Chonky Feed skill sounds confusing, but it is worthwhile when you have the skill points. Every pack of feed gives twice the XP, so you need half as many to level up a single animal. But, each pack becomes 50% larger, so you will need more food in each one. The math works out, though, and you will use less feed in the long run, especially at higher levels.  If you're concerned about the cost of Barn Delight, you can choose to boost your Lemon and Honey output through several fruit and flower skills, or reduce its cost through the Alternative Medicine skill, but honestly it's better to take the skill Healthy Livestock, which will make sickness a rare thing. So, with all of that out of the way, the best way to reduce costs and improve yields on animals is to pick one and align your skills toward it. You will have a much easier time compared to raising two or all three types of creature. * Chicken Specialist * Fine Fibers- +0.1 Feather * Double Bale- +0.4 Egg total with Bale * Featherweight- +0.35 Feather, -0.1 Leather & Merino Wool * Abundant Harvest- +0.2 Egg * Clucky Grazing- 25% less feed required per pack, 50% more to other two animals * Sheep Specialist * Fine Fibers- +0.1 Merino Wool * Bale Economy- +0.2 Wool * Double Bale- Additional +0.2 Wool with Bale * Abundant Harvest- +0.2 Wool * Merino Whisperer- +0.35 Merino, -0.1 Leather & Feather * Sheepwise Diet- 25% less feed required per pack, 50% more to other two animals * Cow Specialist * Fine Fibers- +0.1 Leather * Bale Economy- +0.2 Milk * Double Bale- Additional +0.2 Milk with Bale * Abundant Harvest- +0.2 Milk * Leathercraft Mastery- +0.35 Leather, -0.1 Merino & Feather * Cow-Smart Nutrition- 25% less feed required per pack, 50% more to other two animals * Chonky Feed- 2x XP per pack, +50% pack size (recommended for Cows because of high food requirements) With some groups of skills that give bonuses and penalties together, you can take both and get a net gain (Hectare and Acre Farm; No Axe, No Worries and Fruity Woody) but with animals, the numbers just don't work out. **You will use less feed and get more resources out of choosing one animal and focusing your skills on it**, and even more if you can afford the NFT items that boost your animal of choice. So, if you want a steady supply of Eggs for cooking, pick the chicken. If you want to supply Wool to to doll crafters and crabbers, choose the sheep. Or, if you want to take on the challenge and run a dairy farm, providing Milk for the top-tier foods and Leather for dolls and oil drills, take the cow by the horns. ## NFT Items There are many items that will help with animals, and many are extremely expensive. The Gold Cow/Sheep/Egg items let you feed your animals for free, but will be out of the budget range for the vast majority of players. There are some that you can find for more reasonable prices, however. Search for the name of the animal or the resource ("chicken", "egg", etc.) to find the most current list. * Speed Chicken: -10% Egg production time (Chickens wake up faster, can be fed more often) * Fat Chicken: -10% Chicken feed required * Rich Chicken: +0.1 Egg * Summer Chicken: Chickens cannot get sick in summer * Frozen Cow: Cows cannot get sick in winter * Nurse Sheep: Sheep cannot get sick in summer * White Sheep Onesie: +0.25 Wool > **Contributors to this page** > > [iSPANK](/en/user-pages/iSPANK) - init page creation, layout, linking, tagging > > [librophagus](/en/user-pages/librophagus)\- primary content

title: Social Farming
markdown:
# Cooperative (Social) Farming A new addition to the game, cooperative farming lets you visit other players and help them out in ways never before possible. Visit the Plaza to find your friends, or just grab a random Bumpkin and give them the boost they deserve! Click or tap on the top icon in the lower-left corner of the screen to access the social features. Please note this feature is still very new and may be changed at any time in the future. Every effort will be made to correct the information here if and when it does. ## Social Menu This menu is accessible anywhere, whether on your farm or out in the rest of the world. It will show you the feed of recent activity, which includes all of the help and cheers you've received recently, notices about your followers reaching level milestones, and also public notices about players finding valuable items in chests or purchasing extremely expensive things on the marketplace. These last two can't be turned off quite yet, so instead you can filter the feed by Helped (players that visit your farm), Chat (direct messages from other followers), Cheered (players that cheered your farm), and Follows (players that recently followed you).  ## Following While it isn't strictly necessary to Follow another player, it makes helping them regularly much easier. If you already have some friends or Faction comrades that you've talked to on Discord, the SFL.World Telegram group, or another network, you can use "Search players"  in the social menu to find another player by username. If you're new or just shy, many other players have been hanging out in the plaza while waiting for their Kale to finish growing. Tap on anyone you see to access their player menu. If you like what you see, you can Follow them, which will add an entry to the Following tab in your social menu.  That will show you all of the players that you have chosen to follow, ordered by their total social points. It is possible to follow someone without them following you back, but most players are friendly and will return the kindness. If you go looking for some friends and the Plaza is deserted, try changing your Server. You can find that under Game Options → Plaza Settings → Change server. The capacity of each server is shown, so find the most populated one (usually the Bumpkin Bazaar) and watch everyone appear at once! ![](/game-mechanics/social_profile.png) Pleased to meet you! ## Profile Tapping on a player in the Plaza or in your social menu shows their profile, which has a host of important data, including their level, farm ID, social points, Faction, and so on. You can use the Follow button to do that, and the Rocket icon which will appear above their start date to give them a Cheer. There will also be an activity feed on the right side. The feed and cheer button are invisible in the screenshot because I can't cheer myself. You can also see every one of the player's followers, and those they follow too. If you choose to follow the player, you will be able to message them using the right panel. Be polite, otherwise you might get reported. We wouldn't want that. ## Helping Out There are several things you can do to help another player, both of which can be done from their profile. ### Cheering Tap the Rocket icon to Cheer the other player. This is a simple action that grants them +3 Social Points, and if you are a VIP, +3 Love Charms. Social Points don't seem to do much right now, but may in the future. Love Charms are useful in many ways. You can Cheer a player once per game reset. Cheers are limited; you receive 3 for free each day. There is no limit to the amount of Cheers you can hand out in a day, though. You can use them all up at once if you choose. When you need more, visit Goblet at the Goblin's Retreat to exchange some of the resources you find while helping out. ### Helping Tap the magnifying glass icon next to their island to visit. Once there, you will see a counter at the bottom of the screen with their name and the remaining actions you need to complete. In the upper-right corner, under their numbers, is a scroll which calls up a window with every task spelled out for you. Each farm spawns 5 different trash items every day, all of which are on the “mini-island” to the left of the main farm island. ### Projects There are three different kinds of social projects that you can place on your own farm, and will find on the farms of others. Tap on them to further their progress. Nothing is required from you to do this. ### Pets If your friend is lucky enough to have hatched a pet egg, tending to the little critters will also be a task for you to complete on your visit. Just click on them to provide a little XP.  If your friend has built a Pet House for their critters to live in, just tap on it once to pet every creature at the same time.  A complete help session consists of picking up all 5 pieces of trash, boosting every active project, and loving on any pets. Once you've done all of those things, a window will pop up thanking you and announcing the Social Points and Love Charms the farmer has earned through your help. That's right, helping out earns your friend points, not you.  If for some reason you exit the other player's farm before finishing, you will have to do all of the tasks over again before completing the help session.  By default, you can help 5 other farmers per day. After that, you can continue to be helpful by paying a fee of 1 Iron, 3 Wool, and 3 Feathers **per farm**. This boosted limit expires at game reset, though, so you would likely be better off investing in a more permanent solution…  ## Building your own Projects While visiting farmers can always help clean up your trash, you can give them something else to do and benefit greatly in the process. Visit your Workbench to get the project started. There is no limit to the amount of players that can help you in a single day, so make as many friends as you can to reap these benefits quickly. ### Cooking Pots The Basic, Expert, and Advanced Cooking Pots require Gems, and a 2x2 free area on your farm to place. The costs and amount of help needed to be completed are shown on each one. You can only have one Pot of each type on your farm at a time. Once they are completed, you will get 2 Food Boxes of the same tier as the pot (Basic = Bronze, Expert = Silver, Advanced = Gold), **and** every player who helped you complete it will be entered into a mini-raffle and one of them will receive an additional Box. What a deal! | Cooking Pots | Cooking Pots | Cooking Pots | Cooking Pots | Cooking Pots | Cooking Pots | Cooking Pots | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | SN | Name | Type | Unlock Level | Cost (gems) | Helps Required | What you get when completed | | 1 | Basic Cooking Pot | Consumable, 1 time use | 20 | 10 | 10 | 2 Bronze Food Box | | 2 | Expert Cooking Pot | Consumable, 1 time use | 40 | 50 | 50 | 2 Silver Food Box | | 3 | Advanced Cooking Pot | Consumable, 1 time use | 60 | 500 | 100 | 2 Gold Food Box | ### Giant Fruit The Big Orange, Big Apple, and Big Banana cost Coins, and a 2x2 free space. Like Pots, you can only have one of each growing at a time. After completion, you can sell them back to the Farmer's Market for more coins. Or, you can save them for the Mega Bounty Board, where they are worth a high number of Chapter Tickets, and certain NPCs will ask for them in their deliveries. Finally, you can place them in their finished form on your farm to admire. Once you complete a giant fruit and get the item in your inventory, you are given the option to pay coins and restart the project immediately. If you don't think you'll get that Big Orange grown before the bounty expires at the end of the week, you can use some Obsidian to make it ready to harvest right away. The amount needed is proportional to the amount of help still required to complete it, so try and wait as long as you can and rally your friends! | Obsidian Insta-Grow Costs | Obsidian Insta-Grow Costs | Obsidian Insta-Grow Costs | Obsidian Insta-Grow Costs | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Big / Giant Fruit | Big / Giant Fruit | Big / Giant Fruit | Big / Giant Fruit | | SN | Name | Stage | Obsidian Cost | | 1 | Big Orange | 0/25 Helps | 0.5 | | 2 | Big Apple | 0/50 Helps | 1 | | 3 | Big Banana | 0/200 Helps | 4 | | Flowers | Flowers | Flowers | Flowers | | SN | Duration | Stage | Obsidian Cost | | 1 | One Day Flower (24 Hours) | Just Planted | 0.1 | | 2 | Two Day Flower | Just Planted | 0.2 | | 3 | Three Day Flower | Just Planted | 0.3 | | 4 | Five Day Flower | Just Planted | 0.5 | ### Monuments These permanent structures cost a high amount of Gems and take up a 3x3 or 3x2 space each on your farm. Unlike the other two categories, they do not disappear after completion, so you will keep them forever. You are able to build three monuments that boost your daily help limit by +1, and other powerful monuments are frequently offered in auctions or as other rewards. The Lunar Temple is a rare NFT that, when placed on your farm, will decrease the amount of help actions needed to build any of your own monuments. It doesn't affect your actions on other player's farms. The Poseidon's Throne monument has a confusing description, but what it does is give you an additional Dung and Weed item every time you help someone's farm (total of 3 Weed and 4 Dung). Additional trash items don't appear on their mini-island, you just get more in your inventory when you are done.  | List of Monuments | List of Monuments | List of Monuments | List of Monuments | List of Monuments | List of Monuments | List of Monuments | List of Monuments | List of Monuments | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | SN | Name | Type | Unlock Level | Cost | Helps Required | What you get when completed | Effect of Lunar Temple | Comes From | | 1 | Farmer's Monument | Permanent | 10 | 100 gems | 100 | +1 Help Limit | Helps Required = 50 | Landscaping Build Tab | | 2 | Woodcutter's Monument | Permanent | 20 | 200 gems | 1,000 | +1 Help Limit | Helps Required = 500 | Landscaping Build Tab | | 3 | Miner's Monument | Permanent | 50 | 300 gems | 10,000 | +1 Help Limit | Helps Required = 5000 | Landscaping Build Tab | | 4 | Teamwork Monutment | Permanent | NA | 1,000 CH Tickets | 100 | +1 Help Limit | Helps Required = 50 | Stella - Better Together - CH 11 | | 5 | Cornucopia | Permanent | NA | 1,000 CH Tickets | 1,000 | +1 Giant Fruit | Helps Required = 500 | Stella - Paw Prints - CH 12 | | 6 | Poseidon's Throne | Permanent | NA | 3,000 CH Tickets | 2,000 | +1 Weed & Dung | Helps Required = 1000 | Stella - Crabs N Traps - CH 13 | | 7 | Crystal Altar | Permanent | NA | 3000 salt rock | 1000 | \-5% catch time on 
Crab Pot and Marine Pot | Helps Required = 500 | Stella - The Salt Awakening - CH 14 | ## Trash Disposal After clearing out a few farms, you'll find the Weeds and Dung you've been picking up are actually in your inventory. They are items like any other, but they don't have to stay there forever.  ### Deliveries Sometimes, Finn will request trash items for his deliveries, ever searching for new and better chum to give him an edge against his sister. The Jester is also asking for Dung, probably to use it for a new (smelly) prank. Both of these NPCs will reward Chapter Tickets. ### Chum You can also borrow a page from Finn's playbook by using Weeds as fishing chum yourself. Try it out and see what you catch! ### Retreat Head to the goblin's Retreat and speak to Goblet, who will burn your trash and give you extra Cheers in return. Then Cheer the friends you didn't get to today! Or, if you're not in a cheery mood, you can sell them to Garbo for a few Coins. Since there are many other sources of Coins in the game, it's probably better to give them to Goblet unless you are very broke.  > Contributors to this page > > [librophagus](/en/user-pages/librophagus) - primary content > > [iSPANK](/en/user-pages/iSPANK) - initial tables addition and translation, tagging > [Haesoo](/en/user-pages/Haesoo) \- Original table designs > > [Celia A](/en/user-pages/Celia-A) - new item insertion, minor corrections

title: Chests
markdown:
# Chests

## Reward Chests

There are several different treasure chests that can be opened through various means in the game. The possible rewards from every chest are listed at [https://sfl.world/info/chests](https://sfl.world/info/chests)

The contents of the Keyed Chests change every Chapter, while the others do not change very frequently. As with all games of chance, it's important to have an open mindset when opening any chest. Even if you don't get the item you wanted, whatever you receive will likely be useful in some way, even if later.

### Keyed Chests

The Basic, Rare, and Luxury Chests all require keys, which can be obtained through rewards in the game. Each key allows you to open the respective chest once. The rewards are definitely worth it, though, as you can get high-level items.

### Daily Chest

The Daily Chest is automatically opened for you on your first login after the game's daily reset. It contains 3 Cheers used in social farming, 1 of the current Chapter Tickets, and another item that changes every day. You can see what the next few days' rewards will be by clicking on your mailbox and then the Daily Gift tab. If you lose your streak, though, these rewards will change.

Nothing needs to be done to claim these rewards, you simply have to log in. Every 7 days you will receive the Mega Reward chest. Log in every day to build your streak for even greater rewards!

*   Mega Reward- If you are a VIP player, you will get a number of Gems. If not, you will either get some Coins or some Fishing Lures.
*   Tools Reward- Axes, Pickaxes, and Stone Pickaxes. The amount you get is dependent on your level.
*   Power Hour- For one hour after you claim the daily reward, your plot crops have 50% growth time reduction and a +0.2 yield boost. You can see the amount of time remaining on this bonus from the Market on your farm when selecting a seed to buy.
*   Love Box Reward-
    *   Under level 51: [Basic Love Box](https://sfl.world/info/chests#Basic%20Love%20Box)
    *   Level 15 to 100: [Bronze Love Box](https://sfl.world/info/chests#Bronze%20Love%20Box)
    *   Level 101+: [Silver Love Box](https://sfl.world/info/chests#Silver%20Love%20Box)
*   Fishing Reward- Rods, Earthworms, and Grubs. The amount you get is dependent on your level.
*   XP Reward- An amount of XP proportional to your level. Great when all of your food is going to deliveries and pets!
*   Coins Reward- Some coins to keep your farm running smoothly. The amount you get is dependent on your level.

If you don't want to claim the reward as soon as you log in, like if you have a Power Hour and don't have a full hour to play to get the most out of it, you can close the window with the X in the upper-right corner. Then, when you are ready, open the mailbox at your farm house and use the Daily Gift tab to claim it.

In addition to all of the above, if you are a VIP player you will get an additional food item based on your level:

*   Level 1-2: Mushroom Soup
*   Level 3-5: Bumpkin Broth
*   Level 6-9: Kale Stew
*   Level 10-14: Sunflower Cake
*   Level 15-19: Orange Cake
*   Level 20-29: Parsnip Cake
*   Level 30-99: Honey Cake
*   Level 100+: Honey Cheddar

### [Pirate Chest](https://sfl.world/info/chests#Pirate%20Chest)

The Pirate Chest requires you to have a Pirate Potion equipped on your Bumpkin or any of your Farmhands. The potion can be obtained from Old Salty, as a reward for making multiple deliveries.

### [Bud Chest](https://sfl.world/info/chests#Bud%20Box)

There is an additional chest you can unlock by owning a Bud and visiting the Clubhouse in the Plaza. Every day, a specific type of Bud will unlock the chest, so check the schedule to see when you can claim yours!

## How to get keys

The Treasure Key item unlocks the Basic Chest. It can be obtained from the following places:

*   [Digging Shop](/en/mechanics/digging)\- 10x Sand and 3x Hieroglyph (one per day)
*   [Mark Shop](/en/factions/marks)\- 1000x Marks (one per day)
*   [Marketplace](/en/mechanics/marketplace) Rewards Shop- 1200 Trade Points
*   [Betty](/en/npcs/betty)\- Delivery rewards
*   [Pumpkin Pete](/en/npcs/pumpkin-pete)\- Delivery rewards
*   [Blacksmith](/en/npcs/blacksmith)\- Delivery rewards
*   [Jester](/en/npcs/jester)\- Delivery rewards

The Rare Key unlocks the Rare Chest. It can be obtained from the following places:

*   [Digging Shop](/en/mechanics/digging)\- 30x Sand and 10x Hieroglyph (one per day)
*   [Mark Shop](/en/factions/marks)\- 3000x Marks (one per day)
*   [Marketplace](/en/mechanics/marketplace) Rewards Shop- 3600 Trade Points
*   [Bert](/en/npcs/bert)\- Delivery rewards
*   [Raven](/en/npcs/raven)\- Delivery rewards
*   [Finn](/en/npcs/finn)\- Delivery rewards
*   [Cornwell](/en/npcs/cornwell)\- Delivery rewards
*   [Tywin](/en/npcs/tywin)\- Delivery rewards
*   [Victoria](/en/npcs/victoria)\- Delivery rewards
*   [Jester](/en/npcs/jester)\- Delivery rewards

The Luxury Key unlocks the Luxury Chest. It can be obtained from the following places:

*   [Digging Shop](/en/mechanics/digging)\- 100x Sand and 30x Heiroglyph (one per day)
*   [Mark Shop](/en/factions/marks)\- 10000x Marks (one per day)
*   [Marketplace](/en/mechanics/marketplace) Rewards Shop- 6000 Trade Points
*   [Cornwell](/en/npcs/cornwell)\- Delivery rewards
*   [Tywin](/en/npcs/tywin)\- Delivery rewards

The digging shop and Mark shop keys have a limit of one per day, but you can buy both in a single day if you want to.

The marketplace shop doesn't have a limit or wait period since Trade Points are harder to come by. 

 Keys may become available from special events and other sources as well, so keep an eye out!

## Chest locations

The Basic Chest is located at the left side of the Plaza, just below Tywin, and to the left of the new animal shop.

The Rare Chest is located at the Beach, just above the lower exit to the Plaza.

The Luxury Chest is also located at the Plaza, in the far upper-right corner near Bert.

The Pirate Chest is located at the Beach, to the left of the dig site, near Old Salty.

The Bud Chest is in the Bud Clubhouse in the Plaza.

## Reward Boxes

Boxes are an additional way of earning free items, with a completely different set of tiers and requirements. Unlike chests, Boxes are opened as soon as you receive them for no cost. The potential contents of each one is also visible at [https://sfl.world/info/chests](https://sfl.world/info/chests).

### Food Boxes

Primarily earned from the Cooking Pot projects that you build on your farm, you can also get one of these by helping your friend complete one of their own Pots. They contain relatively good food items, from cakes and above. No Mashed Potatoes here, unlike a certain lucky cat…

### Tool Boxes

These valuable bundles contain all kinds of useful tools for mining, fishing, and digging, and even some animal feed and medicine!

### Love Boxes

A grab bag of sorts, these could contain all sorts of items, including Coins, Gems, tools, or food. They are the only reward box that gives Love Charms, which can be used to buy… more Boxes! A Bronze Love Box will be rewarded once daily to all players who help solve the Love Island puzzle.

### Flower Boxes

Like the name suggests, these contain the valuable FLOWER token.

### Love Island Shop

In addition to the various ways of obtaining Boxes shown above, Food, Tool, and Love Boxes of all three tiers will periodically be available for sale at the Love Island Shop. Visit as often as you can to spend those Love Charms for a chance at great rewards.

### Liquidity Rewards

Another way to earn a Reward Box is through the [Wishing Well](/en/beginners/liquidity-pool); a random box (including Flower) will be granted daily to players who hold a certain amount of value. This is a fairly involved process revolving around holding a position in a liquidity pool between USDC and FLOWER on the Base network. If those terms are unfamiliar for you, refer to the linked guide.

## History

### Daily Chest

The Daily Chest was changed in December 2025. Previously, the chest was located on the top of your Farmhouse, and required a blockchain transaction to open. You could also access it from anywhere from the Earn/Rewards button near your Bumpkin's portrait. A small amount of cryptocurrency was required to process the transaction, but was hardly a large expense given the rewards.

There were three tiers to the Daily Chest, depending on the amount of expansions you had unlocked on your current island. There is no indication in the game of which “land level” you are currently on, but you can find out by looking at the "Expansion No" field at [https://sfl.world/land/](https://sfl.world/land/).

The streak bonus was every 5 days rather than every 7. Every fifth day (5, 10,15, etc.) you would get three times the amount of whatever item reward was rolled for the day.

In addition to the randomly determined item, you also received 1 of the current Chapter's Ticket for free. The 3 Cheers were provided automatically in a separate reward window. 

The old daily reward structure can be viewed [here](/game-mechanics/old_daily_rewards.png) if you are curious.

### VIP Chest

The VIP Chest was an extra bonus for active VIP members. It was removed in February 2026. It was available on the first day of a calendar month, unless that month was the beginning of a new Chapter, in which case it was available on the first Monday of that month (the same day as the beginning of the Chapter).

For the first month of a new Chapter, the item given was something that was be beneficial for the Chapter itself, such as a boost to a new resource or game mechanic. The second month reward was tools or resources, and the third was a non-boosting decoration. These rewards have been added to the new Chapter Pass system instead.

title: Goblin Raffle
markdown:
# Goblin Raffle

![](/game-mechanics/raffle.png)

The goblin raffle-eer?

**Heads up! The Goblin Raffle has been discontinued and merged with the** [**weekly chapter raffles**](/en/chapter-race/raffles)**. This article now serves as a list of ways to obtain Prize Tickets.**

# Goblin Raffle

The monthly raffle was a special event where you could win big rewards. 5 players won 1000x FLOWER, while 2 players got a Bud NFT. 

The Goblin Raffle winners were announced on the Friday Twitch Streams in the 1st or 2nd Fridays of the month.

  
Getting a ticket, however, was a feat to itself. Despite the game telling you that you can find a Prize Ticket by doing NPC deliveries, no character will actually give you one just by earning points. What they **will** give you is a treasure chest key, which is the primary source of tickets at this time.

You can see the probability of getting one for each chest type at [https://sfl.world/info/chests](https://sfl.world/info/chests). If you have a Bud already, you could potentially earn one through the Bud Chest.

If you are a master digger, you have a fairly good chance of getting a Prize Ticket if you can keep up your streak for 11 or more days. The chances of that are shown at the above link also.

A Prize Ticket is also one of the available items at the Marketplace Rewards Shop. It's the most expensive thing there, but you can also buy treasure keys, so if you're tired of eating Trade Cakes you can try spending your rewards on those instead. 

In the event you get your hands on one of these coveted items, visit the Prizes chest in the Plaza and see when the next raffle will be that accepts your hard-won Ticket!

title: Garbo
markdown:
# Garbo

![](/npcs/garbo.jpg)

## Garbo

Garbo is a goblin who resides in the far upper-left corner of the Goblin's Retreat. His primary purpose is to recycle old or deprecated items in exchange for Coins or other resources. Garbo does not accept any deliveries or flowers and will not give any rewards for them.

After a Chapter has ended, you can exchange the unused Tickets for Coins. The exchange rate is extremely low, so don't plan on making any money this way.

The Dung and Weeds that you collect from your friend's farms when helping out can be sold for Coins, though it is arguably better to give them to Goblet instead.

If you are a new player, it is unlikely that you will need to visit Garbo for any reason. 

Garbo used to take Earthworms and Grubs, which was useful when you had a large amount of them from repeated composter use, but as of Chapter 11 he does not.

title: Bud NFTs
markdown:
# Bud NFTs

![](/image.jpeg)

Buds are special companions in Sunflower Land that provide global passive buffs to various in-game systems such as crops, animals, resources, and production. Each Bud belongs to a specific Type, may feature a unique Stem, and can possess an Aura that amplifies its effects.

Only 2,621 of the originally planned 5,000 Buds were minted, making them limited-supply collectibles. All Bud effects apply globally (not area-based) and remain active as long as the Bud is owned and placed in the land.

# Lore

Buds are magical beings born from ancient Bud Seedlings, cultivated and harvested by Bumpkins. They’ve been loyal farming companions since the earliest days of Sunflower Land, embodying the deep bond between nature, magic, and the Bumpkin way of life.

Legends describe Buds as keepers of agricultural wisdom, guiding generations of farmers toward prosperity. Their appearance and abilities evolved according to where they were planted, giving rise to ten distinct Types, each reflecting its native environment and subsequent buff.

Over time, experimentation and natural cross-breeding between Buds of different Types led to unexpected mutations. Some Buds began to develop Stems, external growths resembling hats that mirrored either their own Type or traits from other Types. These Stems became sources of visual variation and, in some cases, powerful secondary buffs, marking the first documented evolutionary divergence among Buds.

A long time ago, the mischievous Goblins discovered half of the Bud Seedlings and grew their own versions. These Goblin Buds share the same powers as their Bumpkin counterparts but bear the distinctive Goblin Ears, symbolizing their origin. When Buds were revealed, there was a 50/50 chance it would be a Goblin Bud or a Bumpkin Bud.

When Bumpkins and Goblins first competed over Bud Seedlings, residual magical from both sides infused the sprouts with unstable magical energy. The result: Auras, visible manifestations of that lingering hybrid magic, growing stronger and rarer depending on the balance of Bumpkin and Goblin influence in the soil.

# Types

Each Bud Type determines its picture background environment and grants a fixed buff that affects a specific resource or product.

**Type Buffs**

| Type | Buff |
| --- | --- |
| Plaza | +0.3 Basic Crops |
| Castle | +0.3 Medium Crops |
| Snow | +0.3 Advanced Crops |
| [Saphiro](/en/lore/history#saphiro) | −10% Crop Growth Time |
| Beach | +0.2 Fruit |
| Woodlands | +0.2 Wood |
| Cave | +0.2 Minerals |
| Retreat | +0.2 Animal Produce |
| Sea | 10% chance of +1 Fish |
| Port | +10% Fishing XP |

# Stems

#### Buffed Stems

Several stems grant fixed buffs. If the Stem and Type share the same category (e.g., both affect crops or minerals), their effects stack on the same Bud. Otherwise, only the strongest effect per category applies globally.

**Stem Buffs**

| Basic Leaf | +0.2 Basic Crops |
| --- | --- |
| Sunflower Hat | +0.5 Sunflower |
| Carrot Head | +0.3 Carrot |
| Three-Leaf Clover | +0.5 Crops |
| Apple Head | +0.2 Fruit |
| Banana | +0.2 Fruit |
| Acorn Hat | +0.1 Wood |
| Tree Hat | +0.2 Wood |
| Ruby Gem | +0.2 Stone |
| Miner Hat | +0.2 Iron |
| Gold Gem | +0.2 Gold |
| Diamond Gem | +0.2 Minerals |
| Egg Head | +0.2 Egg |
| Fish Hat | 10% chance of +1 Fish |
| Mushroom | +0.3 Mushroom |
| Magic Mushroom | +0.2 Magic Mushroom |

**Cosmetic Stems**  
No buffs, purely visual. They do not modify bonuses.  
Axe Head  
Hibiscus  
Rainbow Horn  
Red Bow  
Seashell  
Silver Horn  
Sunflower Headband  
Sunshine Foliage  
Tender Coral

# Auras and Rarity

While Buds do not have official rarity tiers, their Aura determines their rarity and power. Some Buds have no aura, offering only their base Type buff. Aura multipliers apply independently and simultaneously to both the Type and Stem buffs on the same Bud.

No Aura = Base type buff only  
Basic Aura (White) 5% boost  
Green Aura (Green) 20% boost  
Rare Aura (Yellow) 100% boost  
Mythical Aura (Light Blue) 400% boost

# Buff Mechanics and Stacking Rules

Every Bud provides its Type buff, even with no Aura.  
Aura multipliers amplify both Type and Stem buffs independently and simultaneously.  
Buffs of the same category (Crops, Minerals, Fruit, etc.) do not stack across different Buds; only the strongest total buff (base + aura) for a resource is applied, however, if a Bud’s Stem buff matches its Type buff, the bonuses stack on that single Bud.  
The Three-Leaf Clover Stem Bud overrides all other crop buff stems if it has equal or higher aura, but can stack with its Type buff if it's a crop category.  
The Diamond Gem Stem Bud overrides all mineral buff stems if it has equal or higher aura, and can stack with the Cave Type when both are on the same Bud.

**Scenario A**: If 2 Buds has the same type or resource/crop boost, the highest buff will be taken into effect.

Bud A: Plaza Bud (+0.3 Basic Crops) with Tree Hat (+0.2 Wood)

Bud B: Woodlands Bud (+0.2 Wood) with Ruby Gem (+0.2 Stone)

Total Buffs:

*   +0.3 Basic Crops
*   +0.2 Wood
*   +0.2 Stone

**Scenario B**: If 1 Bud has buffs that affects multiple resource/crops and another Bud has a buff for one of the resources/crops, the highest buff for that resource/crop will be taken into effect. 

Bud C: Plaza Bud (+0.3 Basic Crops) with Gold Gem (+0.2 Gold)

Bud D: Cave Bud (+0.2 Minerals) with Sunflower Hat (+0.5 Sunflower

Total Buffs:

*   +0.5 Sunflower
*   +0.3 Potato
*   +0.3 Pumpkin
*   +0.2 Stone
*   +0.2 Iron
*   +0.2 Gold

**Scenario C**: If 1 Bud have 2 of the same resource/crop boost, those do stack. 

Bud E: Woodlands Bud (+0.2 Wood) with Tree Hat (+0.2 Wood)

Total Buff:

*   +0.4 Wood

Bud F: Castle Bud (+0.3 Medium Crop) with Carrot Head (+0.3 Carrots)

Total Buffs:

*   +0.6 Carrot
*   +0.3 Cabbage
*   +0.3 Beetroot
*   +0.3 Cauliflower
*   +0.3 Parsnip

Additional buds will still be seen on the farm.

A bud's buff is additive to other existing farming buffs you have (e.g. Scarecrows)

# Visual Traits

All Buds share a fixed body design but has variations which include:  
Color Palettes: Silver, Gold, Green, Blue, Red, Purple, Stone, Brown, Beige, Orange, Diamond, Rainbow  
Ears: Can appear with or without  
Stems: Cosmetic or buff-based as listed previously  
Auras: Visible glow indicating rarity and power level  
Each Bud’s Type determines the environment in its image background (e.g., Sea Buds have oceanic scenery, Cave Buds have rocky caverns).

# Strategic Notes

Buds with matching Type and Stem buffs are the most efficient.  
Aura rarity often determines economic and strategic value; Mythical Aura Buds vastly outperform lower tiers.  
Clover and Diamond Gem stems act as override archetypes, ensuring only one of each resource or crop category is dominant per land.  
Players often optimize Bud collections by maintaining unique Type coverage to maximize buff variety instead of duplicates.

All values, categories, and stacking rules verified as of 2025-10.

# Farm Pets _Not to be confused with the_ [_Faction Pet_](/en/factions/pet) # Farm Pets Add a furry (or feathery, or scaly) companion to your farm and enjoy the many benefits of your new friend. Pets are a collectible and progression system designed to create hype, excitement, and a burn mechanic for FLOWER and Chapter progression. They feature an iterative proposal with proof of concept designs. ![444250847-a5516bdc-691a-4589-bfee-5a7474ca1614.gif](/game-mechanics/pets/444250847-a5516bdc-691a-4589-bfee-5a7474ca1614.gif) Every Pet hatches out of an egg, even those that normally don't in real life! There are several ways for you to get your first egg: * Purchase one at the Pet Shop in the Plaza for 150,000 Coins (once ever) * Purchase one at the Love Shop on the Floating Island for 10,000 Love Charms (once ever) * Complete chores and deliveries to earn one from the Chapter Rewards Pass Pet Eggs are opened as soon as you purchase or claim them, like Reward Boxes, and the Pet itself will be put in your inventory. Place them somewhere on your farm or in your farmhouse to start feeding and caring for them! **All of this information is now viewable in the game via the Guide button on a Pet's UI.** Information provided in-game takes precedence over this community-run wiki. ## Pet Types You can only get one egg from the Pet Shop and Love Shop each, so that will give you two Pets if you can get them both. There are 20 different Pet types, and you will always get a new one every Egg that you buy. So you can't get duplicates! Common pets cannot be traded. Each Pet has a Category, which determines what kind of items they can fetch for you. There are 20 different Common Pets across 7 categories: ![480440174-8e5f24e6-6b0f-451c-8a8e-b85c0d73dbd9.png](/game-mechanics/pets/480440174-8e5f24e6-6b0f-451c-8a8e-b85c0d73dbd9.png) * Guardians fetch Chewed Bones * Hunters fetch Ribbons * Voyagers fetch Ruffroot * Beasts fetch Wild Grass * Moonkin fetch Heart Leaf * Snowkins fetch Frost Pebble * Foragers fetch Dewberry Every pet has 2 or 3 Categories, so they will be able to get you multiple items. It takes approximately 4.5 years to collect all 20 common pets, provided you can obtain one in each 3-month Chapter. ## Requests Every day at game reset, your pet will request different foods. When you feed it to them, they will earn Energy and XP. Requests start with 2 per day and increase with pet level. Currently only one unit of each food is required to fulfill the request (unlike the Faction Pet, which usually requires multiples of each food). New requests are generated every day at game reset, **whether you have completed them or not**. So, make sure you can finish that Fancy Fries before your pet's fancy moves on to something else. You can also reset all the requests with new ones by paying Gems (generates 3 new ones; cost increases with use). ![2025-10-31\_02-48-31.png](/game-mechanics/pets/2025-10-31_02-48-31.png) The order of the three slots is important; the top slot will be for "Easy" foods, the middle for "Medium" and the lower for "Hard." You can see which foods may appear in a given slot at [https://sfl.world/info/pets](https://sfl.world/info/pets), and plan accordingly. If you have the resources, keeping one of each food on hand will help with whatever requests may come up. Pets will never request anything that requires a fish product or a mushroom as one of its ingredients. It will only ask for things that can be made with resources bought on the Marketplace. If you can't feed your pet for 3 consecutive days, it will lose 500 XP. This will only happen once, though, so if you need to take an extended leave from the game you will only incur the penalty one time, not every 3 days during your absence. Any of the three slots will fulfill this requirement, it does not need to eat every requested food. Your pets will sleep periodically, and can be tapped on to gain a small amount of XP (+10 XP every 2 hours during 'nap' mode). In addition, visitors to your farm will pet your creature to give it some bonus XP (+1 to +5 XP, capped at 50 XP per pet per day from social help). ### Foods Not Requested by Pets | Rapid Roast | Beetroot Blaze | Mushroom Soup | | --- | --- | --- | | Mushroom Jacket Potatoes | Kale & Mushroom Pie | Shroom Syrup | | Furikake Sprinkle | Creamy Crab Bite | Crimstone Infused Fish Oil | | Surimi Rice Bowl | | | ## Fetching Once your pet has some Energy, you can send it out on quests to find items for you. The Acorn is a standard item that every pet can find, and has multiple different uses. The other items it can find are dependent on its Category, and its level. Sending it to fetch consumes the displayed amount of Energy, and awards the resource instantly, there is no timer or cooldown. The only limit is the amount of energy the Pet has accumulated. Energy does not expire, you can store up as much as you like per pet and have them fetch all at once. Once your pet reaches a certain level, you will see the amount of resource increase by a decimal amount. This replaces the old mechanic where your pet had a chance to fetch double the resource, which proved to be problematic. This increased amount does not apply to the Fossil Shell, as it is essentially a reward box and not a tradeable resource. The Fossil Shell will always give whole amounts of resources. Once your pets have gathered some resources, you can use them to craft [Shrines](/en/mechanics/pets#shrines), put them in water traps to bait [Crustaceans](/en/mechanics/fishing#crustaceans), or sell them on the Marketplace to other players who need what their Pets can't fetch yet. Currently the only Pet resource that's used for deliveries are Acorns, but that may change in the future. Acorns can also be used as chum when fishing, though it doesn't seem to differ much from other, easier to get resources. ![2025-10-31\_02-50-21.png](/game-mechanics/pets/2025-10-31_02-50-21.png) ## Experience Leveling up your pet will grant it different perks, such as more items available to fetch, more foods available for requests, and other bonuses. There is currently no level cap for a pet, so feed it and watch it grow! XP progression is quadratic (e.g., Level 2: 120 XP, Level 3: 300 XP, Level 4: 600 XP). | Level | Perk | | --- | --- | | 3 | Unlock Category (fetch first non-Acorn resource) | | 5 | +5 energy per pet food | | 7 | Unlock 2nd Fetched Item Category | | 10 | 3 Food Requests per day | | 12 | Unlock Moonfur (**NFT ONLY**) | | 15 | +0.1 extra fetched resource (including Acorn) | | 18 | +1 Acorn yield | | 20 | Unlock Fossil Shell | | 25 | Unlock 3rd Fetched Item Category (**NFT ONLY**) | | 27 | Pet Experience +10% | | 30 | 4th request per day (**NFT ONLY**) | | 35 | +5 energy per pet food (+10 total) | | 40 | Pet Experience +15% (25% total **NFT ONLY**) | | 50 | +0.05 extra fetched resource (+0.15 total) | | 60 | +1 non-acorn/moonfur resource yield (**NFT ONLY**) | | 75 | +5 energy per pet food (+15 total) | | 85 | Pet Experience +25% (50% Total **NFT ONLY**) | | 100 | +0.1 extra fetched resource (+0.25 total) | | 150 | +0.25 extra Moonfur yield (+0.5 total) (**NFT ONLY**) | | 200 | 5th food request (**NFT ONLY**) | There is currently no sickness mechanic for pets. ## Shrines Shrines are special buildings that are placed on your farm, and take Pet resources to craft. Resources other than Acorns are tradeable, so you can get them from farmers who have pets of different categories than you. Shrines are crafted in the plaza using the Pet/Shrine Shop and are limited by Acorn input (depends on number of pets fetching Acorns). Like with all other boosts and items, the effects of a Shrine are only applied when a resource is harvested or processed. For example, the Stag Shrine reduces the Oil well recovery time by 25%. If you currently have an Oil well that has been drilled and is recovering, placing the Shrine will not change the amount of time before the well is ready. For this reason, you should wait until the resources are refreshed and ready (such as first thing in the morning) before placing and activating it. Otherwise, you will spend some of its limited time when it cannot be beneficial to you. Once a Shrine's timer has expired and its effect has ended, you can choose to remove it from your farm and put it in your inventory, or renew it, paying the resource cost again and restarting the timer. You cannot buy another of the same Shrine at the Pet Shop, so if you want to use it again you must renew the one you already have. All the costs and benefits of the shrines are shown here: [https://sfl.world/info/pets](https://sfl.world/info/pets) ## Pet House If you keep advancing, you'll find yourself with more than one of these critters running around your farm. To help with their management, you can ask your Blacksmith to construct a Pet House for you. This is a 3x3 structure that can hold 3 Common Pets and 1 NFT pet. It can be upgraded to hold more if you need that. After placing your pets inside, you can access the house menu with the upper-right icon. From there you can feed all the pets at once, and fetch with only a few taps. You currently cannot place any other items or decorations inside the house, only pets. You also cannot remove the Pet House from your farm without first removing all Pets within it. There is no bonus or boost given to your pets from being inside, it is purely a convenience feature. This convenience could turn into a drawback, however, as the Pet House is considered a building just like the Barn and Hen House, and therefore it will be disabled if your farm is struck by a Tornado or Tsunami.  ## NFT Pets Special collectible and tradeable Pets will also be available to those resourceful players who can obtain them. These NFT Pets function just like the commonly-available ones, eating food and taking requests and so on, but have special properties that boost their XP and Energy gains. Their XP and levels will persist even if they are traded to another player, so their value will only grow as you raise them! NFT Pets are also twice as large as their common counterparts, and take up a 2x2 space on your farm rather than a 1x1 square. * **Total Supply**: 3000 NFT Eggs. * **Initial Drop**: 1000 Eggs in FLOWER Auction (November 3rd-10th), 50 per auction; players can win multiple (up to 7). * **Remaining**: Available each Chapter with tickets (250 total, including Pet Chapter). | SN | Pet Type | NFT Supply | No. of Pets | Basic Resource

title: Chapter Race Overview
markdown:
# Chapter Race

The ‘chapter race' is a term that refers to the competition that takes place over every 3-month period in the game. During this time farmers collect Chapter Tickets and Chapter Points, and use them to earn fabulous prizes.

## How do I get tickets and points?

The methods of getting chapter tickets include:

*   Daily Reward- 1 Ticket per player per day
*   Animal Bounties- Ticket amounts vary based on animal level, plus 5 track points per ticket
*   Mega Bounty Board- Ticket amounts vary based on item rarity, plus 5 track points per ticket
*   Deliveries- Ticket amounts vary based on delivery value, plus 5 track points per ticket. Coin and FLOWER deliveries also award 10 track points per delivery.
*   Weekly Chores- Ticket amounts vary based on chore complexity, plus 3 track points per ticket

There are several different items and wearables that can boost your ticket-earning potential, some are rewarded in the Chapter Track, and some are available at Stella's Megastore. Getting as many of these as you can afford, and making the most of Double Delivery Day, is the key to maximizing your earnings.

## Why should I collect chapter tickets?

Chapter Tickets are used to buy entries into the weekly raffles; 100 prizes are handed out every week, and you can potentially get something for only a single entry!

You can also save up your tickets to buy powerful items at Stella's Megastore.

Finally, tickets are used to bid on valuable items in the Auctions that take place during a special week near the end of each Chapter.

While earning tickets, you will also get chapter (track) points, which are used to unlock unique rewards more reliably. Even if you gamble all your tickets on a raffle and lose, you'll still have your points.

## USE IT OR LOSE IT!!!

The tickets in every chapter are only good during the chapter they are obtained from. At the end of the chapter tickets become ‘nearly worthless’. The only place the can be used/removed from inventory is by giving them to [Garbo](/en/npcs/garbo); who will purchase them from you for a very cheap coin price (usually 0.1 coins each).

So in conclusion; use your tickets before the end of the chapter or you will lose the value.

title: Weekly Chores
markdown:
# Weekly Chores

![](/game-mechanics/chores.png)

_Not to be confused with_ [_Faction Chores_](/en/factions/chores)_, an inactive and possibly obsolete mechanic_

## Weekly Chores

“Complete chores for Bumpkins to earn Chapter Tickets.” (Or other resources)

Chores are another way for you to earn those all-important Chapter Tickets and Chapter Points, especially for new players. Unlike deliveries, Chores can be completed without leaving your farm, and involve more than just giving up resources or food. You will also earn one Chapter Point per Ticket earned. 

Every chore is tied to an NPC, but this is primarily cosmetic as completing a chore does not earn delivery points with that character. The progress bar underneath shows you how close you are to completion for it, and when done you can just click the Complete button to earn your Tickets immediately. Items that boost Tickets also work for chores.

Many chores, especially those near the bottom of the menu, are extremely expensive and only suitable for high-level players. The amount of Tickets is usually not worth the effort, unless you are doing a lot of that action anyway and can get some extra value from it.

Chores are tied to the weekly schedule, and will reset on Monday with the new season. For Auction Week and the weeks between chapters when Ticket NPCs are unavailable for deliveries, chores will reward another resource such as Coins or Gems. Gem chores are highly recommended to pursue.

There is no notification or indicator in the game of when you have completed a chore, so make sure to check the tab from time to time, especially at the end of the week, to make sure you collect any that you've already completed.

## Harvest/Pick/Grow

These chores require you to obtain a certain crop, fruit, flower, or other plant resource. Note that the requirement is for a certain number of harvest actions, not the amount of resource that's actually obtained. For example, if the chore is “Harvest Beetroot 40 times," then you must pull up 40 plots worth of Beetroot. Even if you have 20 plots that are boosted to output 2 Beetroot per harvest, you will only complete the chore halfway. Similarly, if you get +1 flower when harvesting a bed, it will not count toward the total for the chore.

For advanced players who use the Crop Machine, note that every seed you add to a pack will count toward a harvest chore when you harvest the completed pack.

## Chop/Mine

These are for trees and mineral nodes, including Crimstone. Again, you must harvest that node type so many times, no matter how much resource you get out of it.

## Fish/Dig

Simply use the required amount of fishing rods or digging tools. A Sand Drill counts as one dig. What you find doesn't matter, as long as you attempt it. Some of these chores, especially digging, may require you to do more actions than you are capable of doing every day, so do the math before you attempt them. (e.g. Dig 225 times, meaning your daily dig limit must be at least 33, meaning you cannot complete this unless you own the Heart of Davy Jones)

## Collect

Similar to the harvest actions, these are for animal products like eggs, milk, and wool. Regardless of how much you obtain on each feeding, you must do it that number of times.

**Honey is an exception**, as the chore does count the amount of honey you actually collect, not the number of times you collect it. That means if it asks you to “Collect 11 Honey” and you collect it 10 times at 1.1 Honey per collection, you will complete the chore.

## Cook/Prepare

These chores require you to cook a certain food a specific number of times. You can then do whatever you like with the food, whether you eat it, deliver it, or anything else. Food obtained from chests or other rewards do **not** count for these chores, only those you collect from your own cooking stations.

## Eat/Drink

These chores require you to feed the requested food to your Bumpkin. It does not matter how you got it, whether from your buildings or as a reward, as long as it is eaten before the week is over.

## Craft

Make the required amount of tool at your workbench. Then use them to fulfill other chores!

## Spend

Every so often Tywin or another royal appears to tax your hard-earned money. You must spend the required amount of Coins, whether at your market, workbench, or another store. All fees for crafting weather items and digging tools also count as spent Coins.

title: Mega Bounty Board
markdown:
# Mega Bounty Board

![](/game-mechanics/bounty_board.png)

Example screenshot, content changes every week

# Mega Bounty Board

“Gather the resources & exchange them for rewards before time runs out!”

The Mega Bounty Board is one of the various ways for players to earn Chapter Tickets and Chapter Points. It is also one of the most available, catering to multiple different types of players. Whether you choose to fish, craft, or grow flowers, you will likely find something here that you can tackle.

Each bounty is worth the stated amount of Chapter Tickets, as well as three times as many points toward the Chapter Pass.

The items requested on the board change every week on Monday, at the same time as a new season begins. You can view the current lineup from anywhere in your Codex, including the value of the reward and whether or not you have any of that item in your inventory, but you must travel to the lower-right side of the Plaza and speak with Poppy to actually turn items in for the reward.

## Flower Bounties

Five different [flowers](/en/mechanics/flowers) will be requested among all of those currently available. There may be some you have never grown before, so use this as an opportunity to experiment with new combinations. Also do the math to ensure you will actually be able to grow a particular flower before the week ends altogether, unless you are willing to use some of that valuable Obsidian…

## Fish Bounties

Any five of the various aquatic treasures will be up for rewards. Fish that are not in season are possible candidates, so make sure you have some fish products on hand to get the one you need through a guaranteed catch.

## Crustacean Bounties

Craft some water traps to get these valuable creatures. These are usually worth quite a bit more than fish.

## Exotic Bounties

This category currently consists of the exotic crops that can be purchased with Potion Tickets. You can also get them from the Magic Bean, also for sale in the potion minigame store.

## Giant Fruit Bounties

Round up your friends to help grow these special exotic fruits. Each fruit can be turned in once per week. Extras can be sold for coins or given to certain NPCs for their own deliveries.

## Doll Bounties

Five of those new-fangled dolls will be up for redemption, too. Pick which ones you can afford to make and turn them in for quite a few rewards!

## Obsidian Bounties

Each of the three bounties in this category require one Obsidian. Since they each have differing reward amounts and all only require one, it is easy to see which should be redeemed first…

## Bounty Bonus

In the event that you are an extremely capable player and can complete all of the possible bounties, you can claim an additional large reward. This is a tall order for even the most experienced players, but it is a good goal to work toward! 

## History

The bounty board used to include items that you could get from digging or fishing like Old Bottles, Sand, and Sea Cucumbers. These were removed in the Paw Prints chapter, along with the Moon Berries, and Marks earned from the Kingdom. Previously multiple copies of each Giant Fruit could be turned in for rewards in a single week.

### Limited Marketplace

Previously to the Craps & Traps chapter, it was possible to buy and sell a large selection of items requested on the bounty board each week. Now that flowers can be grown instantly with Obsidian and guaranteed catch fishing has been expanded, the limited section has been removed.

title: Auctions
description: Brief description of auctions, how they work, and where to find them
markdown:
# Auctions

Just like any auction in the ‘real world’, auctions inside of Sunflower-Land work just about the same.

## When?

Generally auctions happen ‘once’ per currency per [Chapter](/en/chapter-race).  
But the number of auctions for each item depends on the effect of the item in question; and the number of that item available.  
When an auction is ‘live’ (able to be bid on), you will see a pop-up on the bottom of your screen saying as such.

## Where?

At the auction house. Which is located just to the right as you land inside the Plaza. (on your game map, inside of the globe icon)

To participate, talk to the Auctioneer when one of the auctions is live.

![](/chapter-mechanics/auctions/auctionhouse.jpg)

## Method

There is generally only 1 type of Auction; the “Blind Auction".

*   Every player is allowed 1 bid, you DO NOT get to see what other players bid.
*   Top X bids win the prize.
*   Player's who DO NOT win the auction receive back their full bid when the auction is over.

## Token Types

There are 3 tokens that are used in the auctions; [Flower](/en/home/tokens#flower), [Gems](/en/home/tokens#gems), and [Chapter Tickets](/en/home/tokens#chapter-tickets).

Each of which happens (generally) at a different time period from one another. But the team has used many different scheduling methods over the chapters. And at the time of my writing this, there is no clear defined pattern as of yet.

## Final Notes

*   Player's can only win ONE of each item regardless of the token type. So winning an item with $FLOWER means you cannot win that item again, with any token type (gems, chapter tickets, flower) from an auction during the same chapter.

title: Megastore
markdown:
# Megastore

![](/chapter-mechanics/megastore-new.png)

Reference screenshot, items will change every Chapter

# Stella's Megastore

If you don't feel like trying your luck in a raffle, you can always save up your Chapter Tickets and trade them to Stella for some powerful prizes. She also carries some items that will boost your overall ticket-earning potential, and will accept Digging artifacts too. Simply gather the required amount of resource and visit her in the Plaza to purchase your desired item. 

If an item has a boost, a lightning bolt icon will indicate that in the menu. Most items are limited to one per player. Items that cost FLOWER are discounted by 50% for VIP players (yes, that means the items in the screenshot above cost 100 and 200 FLOWER respectively for free players).

Some items cannot be traded on the Marketplace even after the chapter ends, these are clearly marked in their description. These items are usually also monuments, meaning they must be placed on your farm and your friends help you build them, just like with Giant Fruits and other special items.

You can also view the current Chapter Pass rewards from her window. You can view the items available from your Chapter Dashboard anywhere in the game, but must travel to the Plaza to buy something.

## History

With the advent of the Chapter Pass rewards system, Stella's Megastore became a lot less mega. Her offerings used to be divided up into the four-tier layout that is currently used for the Event Shop during holiday events; Basic, Rare, Epic, and Mega items. In order to buy items from the higher tiers, you needed to have have bought at least four items in the tier below it. After unlocking a tier, you could buy any item in it.

The lineup of items changed every Chapter, but there were some recurring types of items. The basic tier contained decorations and ticket-boosting items, while the rare tier had more useful items for general gameplay. The last two tiers had expensive, powerful items that were highly sought after once the Chapter ended. 

Most items required Tickets to redeem, but a few cost FLOWER, and others required the current Artifact from the Beach Dig Site. Some items had additional costs on top just tickets. For example, the Double Bed offered during Chapter 11 not only required 1250 Bracelets, but also 5000 Wool and 2500 Gems. 

The three treasure Keys were available for purchase, one in each of the first three tiers. As with the other ways to obtain these items, you could only get one per day, but instead of another one being available at game reset, you actually had to wait 24 hours for the item to "cool down".

Bronze, Silver, and Gold Flower Boxes were also available. The cooldown for those items was 7 days (168 hours), down to the minute, so planning was needed if players wanted to buy multiples.

You can view a screenshot of the previous store layout [here](/game-mechanics/megastore.png), if you are curious.

title: Chapter Pass
markdown:
# Chapter Pass

![chapterdashboard.png](/chapter-mechanics/chapterdashboard.png)

### AKA Chapter Track, Battle Pass, Chapter Rewards

The newest way to earn rewards in the game, the Chapter Pass is open to all players, and is the primary form of progression and rewards in the new system. Earn points for doing things that you already do, and benefit greatly!

### Reward Tracks

The two tracks are accessible in the middle of the new Chapter Dashboard, accessed by the green journal icon near your bumpkin's portrait.

As you earn chapter points, you will unlock rewards on the tracks you have access to. There are two, one for VIP players and one for all players. If you unlock a rank as a free player, then decide to purchase a VIP membership, you will get the reward from every VIP rank you have already unlocked..

Chapter Points are earned from several different sources:

*   Ticket Deliveries- In addition to Chapter Tickets, your favorite NPCs will give you **5 points per ticket** in their reward.
*   Coin Deliveries- A flat **10 points** will be added to every delivery for Coins, no matter the reward amount.
*   Bounty Board- Earn **3 points per ticket** you earn on each bounty.
*   Animal Bounties- Each animal is worth **3 points per ticket** when sold.
*   Weekly Chores- Chores grant **3 points per ticket** also.

Since point amounts are tied to ticket amounts, Double Delivery Day will only increase the point rewards from Ticket Deliveries, not Coin Deliveries.

### Claiming Rewards

The game does not notify you when you have earned enough points to unlock a new rank and reward. Check the dashboard periodically to see what you're eligible for. The rank icon in the upper-right of the window shows your progress to the next rank, while clicking on a reward that you haven't earned yet will show the amount of points overall for the entire chapter.

### Social Rewards

Twitter rewards, referral links, Discord and Telegram links have all been moved to the Earn window accessed in the lower-right of this screen.

### Megastore, Auctions, Raffles

You can view the items available in Stella's pared-down [Megastore](/en/chapter-race/megastore) at the button in the upper-right, though you still need to visit her in the Plaza to actually buy something with Chapter Tickets.  
Similarly, you can view upcoming [auctions](/en/chapter-race/auctions), but must travel to the Plaza to place your bids once they begin.  
But, you can enter the [weekly raffles](/en/chapter-race/raffles) from home or anywhere, and add additional entries if you want.

# Faction Kitchen

![](/faction_kitchen.png)

The Faction kitchen is one of the best sources of Marks because of its reliability. Each week, you will be presented with three different resources, which can be anything from crops to fruits to wood and stone. You will receive Marks for every set of resources that you deliver, and the reward will decrease with every set. The amount will reset to the maximum at the next game reset, so it is up to you if you want to dump all of your stock at once or wait and give a little each day.

The Faction kitchen reward amounts are affected by Mark multipliers such as Emblem bonuses and Faction equipment. The current requirements for your faction can be viewed here: [https://sfl.world/util/factions](https://sfl.world/util/factions)

There is also a section on [https://sfl.world/land](https://sfl.world/land) (Enter your Farm ID) that will show the P2P cost of each item set, and how many Marks you've earned each day of the current week. Use these tools to best plan your strategy.

title: Faction Pet
markdown:
# Faction Pet

_Not to be confused with personal_ [_Pets_](/en/mechanics/pets)

![](/faction_pet_window.png)

# Faction Pet

The Faction Pet is one of the primary mechanics of joining a faction, and feeding it will benefit not only you but every participating member of the group. Located centrally in the middle of the faction house, the Pet requires different foods every week. Contribute one of each request to unlock the XP streak bonus!

## Requests & XP

Each week there will be three foods requested, along with one doll. You must have all of the food requested on hand to successfully make the delivery (i.e. if the request is for 2 Roast Veggies, you must have both). Every time you make a delivery, you will gain the Marks shown below the food, and contribute XP to the Weekly Goal. Like the Faction Kitchen, the amount of the reward will decrease after each delivery, but will reset at the beginning of the next day. Rewards are affected by multipliers from Emblems, equipment, and other sources.

The reward amount is much lower than for the Kitchen, so it is difficult to earn a large amount of Marks unless you have a lot of the food on hand. The primary purpose of each delivery is to give the Pet XP, and to make you a Contributing Member for the week. Only the food deliveries will earn XP; the doll is only required for your contribution status. It is assumed that the Pet does not actually eat the doll, only plays with it while waiting for more food to be delivered. 

By making at least one delivery for every food and doll shown, you will be recognized as a Contributing Member for the current week. You will not actually get the XP bonus, however, until the following week. 

If the Weekly Goal is not reached, the Pet will fall asleep the following week and cannot be fed, meaning no Marks can be earned.

You can see the current requests for your Faction's Pet, along with the progress toward the goal, at [https://sfl.world/util/factions](https://sfl.world/util/factions), or by visiting your Faction House in-game

## Streak

During the first week that the Pet is successfully fed, nothing will happen, no bonuses will be given. Technically, you can skip being a Contributor for this week if you are running low on resources. During Week 2, you must be a Contributor if you want to get the bonus that will start on Week 3.

If the Pet is fed by the end of the week **and** you are a Contributing Member, you will get a bonus to XP according to the following layout:

*   Week 2 streak = 10% XP bonus for weeks 3 & 4
*   Week 4 streak = 20% XP bonus for weeks 5 & 6
*   Week 6 streak = 30% XP bonus for weeks 7 & 8
*   Week 8 streak = 50% XP bonus for weeks 9 & 10+

The Weekly Goal is 25% higher than it was the previous week, so eventually the Pet will become too expensive to feed. When it falls asleep, the XP bonus of the prior week will **still be in effect** until the next week begins (assuming you were a Contributing Member for the failed week, of course). The developers have acknowledged that this is not what they had intended when implementing the Faction Pet, so it may change in the future. For now, however, you can safely eat all of your foods during an off week and still get the bonus.

You can always check if you have an active Pet Streak bonus by tapping on the XP amount for any food when you go to eat it.

## Request Rotations

If you play for a while you may see some patterns in the foods requested by the pet. Read more about the 12-week rotation cycle at this article: [https://wiki.sfl.world/en/factions/request-rotation](/en/factions/request-rotation\)

title: Faction Chores
