# Faction Chores

_Not to be confused with_ [_Weekly Chores_](/en/mechanics/Chores)

Faction chores are an old system that have not been fully removed from the game. There is an NPC in your faction house that will claim to be preparing chores, but not have any available. Unfortunately, they have been working on them for many months now. There is also a section for these visible at the bottom of the faction tab in your Codex. 

**It is unknown at this time if Faction Chores will be available again, or completely removed.**

### History

Faction Chores were another way to earn Marks in addition to the Pet and Kitchen. Three chores would be displayed at a time in a menu, and you could complete any of them that you liked. They followed the mechanics present in Weekly Chores, with cooking, eating, harvesting, and so on. Once a chore was complete and you collected the Marks for it, the next one in the queue would take its place. Emblems and equipment bonuses did increase Marks earned from Faction chores.

An interesting situation would occur when the same chore would appear in two different slots, allowing you to get double the amount of Marks for the same effort. For example, “Chop 20 Trees” in two slots, meaning when you completed the task you could claim both chores at the same time.

Faction Chores could be skipped like deliveries, but only if they had been available to you for at least 24 hours. The complexity of the chores increased as you completed them, but so did the rewards.

# Marks

## Marks

Marks are the primary currency of the Kingdom, and all four Factions as a result. You will earn Marks for contributing to your [Faction Pet](/en/factions/pet), making deliveries to the [Faction Kitchen](/en/factions/kitchen), and playing [minigames](/en/mechanics/minigames) at the portal outside the Bumpkin House.

Marks can be traded in for powerful items at Eldric's shop.

The “best” or fastest way to earn Marks is generally considered to be the Kitchen, followed by the Pet, and lastly minigames. You will also earn bonus marks for placing in the top 100 members of your faction every week, or if your Faction wins the Weekly War (no matter your rank).

## Emblems

Emblems are a resource that have no direct use, but are still valuable for any Faction member. There are four different Emblems, one for each Faction, and can be bought and sold on the Marketplace under the Resources tab. **You can only trade the Emblems of the faction that you are currently in.** Some players may still have emblems from multiple factions, from before this restriction was put in place.

Once you obtain a certain number of Emblems, the amount of Marks you earn from the Pet and Kitchen will be increased. This is called earning a Rank in the Faction. The amount of Emblems needed for each Rank, and the Mark multiplier for each, can be seen here: [https://sfl.world/util/factions](https://sfl.world/util/factions)

It is not strictly necessary to obtain Emblems to participate in a Faction, but as the Rank 5/+150% bonus only requires an average of 335 Emblems, and at the average price at the time of this writing is 0.06 FLOWER per emblem, you only need roughly 20 FLOWER to obtain a substantial boost to the amount of Marks you earn.

## Faction Shop

Eldric sells a large amount of items in the Faction Shop, and it can seem overwhelming until you realize that you can only purchase ¼ of them; items not meant for your Faction are visible but not purchaseable. The items available there can be broken down into several categories:

### Decorations & Cosmetics

There are several decorative items and wearables which provide no boosts, but will demonstrate your Faction's aesthetic to any visitors to your farm.

### Food

There are three food items which can be purchased with Marks, though their cost to XP value is lower compared to [cooked](/en/mechanics/cooking) food.

### Treasure Keys

You can obtain keys for the Basic, Rare, and Luxury [Chests](/en/mechanics/chests) with Marks, though you can only get one of each per day.

### Hourglasses

You can buy hourglasses that will: 

*   **Gourmet Hourglass**\- Decrease cooking time for all kitchens by 50% (for 4 hours)- 1500 Marks
    *   Place when all cooking buildings are idle, then start new recipes
    *   The Fish Market and the Aging Shed do not count as cooking buildings for purposes of this boost
*   **Fisher's Hourglass**\- Increase your chances of catching an extra fish by 50% (for 4 hours)- 2000 Marks
*   **Blossom Hourglass**\- Reduce flower growth time by 25% (for 4 hours)- 2000 Marks
    *   Place when all flowerbeds are empty, then plant seeds
*   **Timber Hourglass**\- Reduce tree recovery time by 25% (for 4 hours)- 4000 Marks
    *   Place when all trees are ready to be chopped, then chop them
*   **Orchard Hourglass**\- Reduce fruit patch growth time by 25% (for 6 hours)- 4000 Marks
    *   Place when all fruit patches are empty, then plant new seeds. This boost will NOT affect fruits already in progress.
*   **Harvest Hourglass**\- Reduce crop growth time by 25% (for 6 hours)- 5000 Marks
    *   Place when all plots are empty, then plant seeds
*   **Ore Hourglass**\- Reduce mineral recovery time by 50% (for 3 hours)- 8000 Marks
    *   Minerals include stone, iron, gold, crimstone, and sunstone. Unless you have another boost that reduces mineral recovery time, it's unlikely you'll get more than one use out of this item.

For the time-reducing items, it is important to note that the bonuses will only take effect when a resource or product timer is initiated. For example, the Gourmet Hourglass instructs you to ensure all of your cooking buildings are idle before placing it, because any foods that are currently cooking will not have their times adjusted when the hourglass is placed. This is especially important for fruits, as time bonuses are only applied when a new fruit seed is planted, not when you harvest a grown plant and it begins replenishing.

### Faction Equipment

The real power of the Faction shop comes in the equipment pieces that you can buy, which can provide **large** bonuses if invested in properly. Each Faction's equipment have the same benefits, only the styles are different. 

*   Faction Pants (37.5K Marks)- Provides 5% bonus Marks
*   Faction Boots (37.5K Marks)- Provides 5% bonus Marks
*   Faction Helmet (56.2K Marks)- Provides 10% bonus Marks
*   Faction Sword (56.2K Marks)- Provides 10% bonus Marks
*   Faction Armor (112K Marks)- Provides 20% bonus Marks
*   Faction Crown (210K Marks)- FLOWER and Coin delivery amounts increased by 25%, and 10% bonus Marks
    *   Note: The Faction Helmet must be bought before the Crown, as it is taken from you when you make this purchase. The 10% bonus remains on the new item.
*   Faction Shield (240K Marks)- +0.25 yield to Trees and Mineral nodes
*   Faction Quiver (240K Marks)- +0.25 yield to Crops and Fruit plots
*   Faction Medallion (240K Marks)- 25% faster cooking

As you can see, these items are designed for players who put in the time and effort to contribute to their Faction. The costs may be high, but the benefits are even higher. The only item that has a prerequisite is the crown, you can buy the others in any order. However, a solid strategy is to buy them in the order listed here, each purchase increasing the speed at which you can obtain the next one.

If for some reason you decide to [leave your Faction](/en/factions/leaving) after purchasing one of these items, it will cease to function.

title: Faction Wars
markdown:
# Faction Wars

## Weekly War

Every week, the amount of Marks earned by the top 100 players of each Faction is totaled up, and becomes the score by which each group is ranked. All members of the first place faction will earn 10% of the Marks they individually earned during the winning week. If your faction claims the victory, visit the Faction House the following week to find this bonus payment.

Those top 100 players also earn additional rewards, regardless of their Faction's ranking. All of the possible ranks and rewards can be viewed in the Factions tab of your Codex, or farther down this page. These rewards are quite substantial, so if you have the resources to help your faction, it is recommended that you do.

As for the question of which faction is “the best,” each Faction is functionally the same; they all have the same potential bonuses and rewards available for every member. The ranking also fluctuates every week, and each have roughly the same amount of members, so it is not really possible to say that one Faction is consistently superior to another. Each has its own unique aesthetic and style, so pick the one that suits you best!

### Bonus Week

Periodically you may see a “Bonus Week” reward in the Factions tab of your Codex. But what are these bonus rewards? In addition to all of the usual amounts of Coins, FLOWER, and Marks for each of the top performers, a number of keys will be given to each tier.

title: Leaving a Faction
markdown:
# Leaving a Faction

## Leaving a Faction

It is possible to leave a Faction, if you believe that you will benefit somehow from being in a different one. The costs of doing this are steep, however.

*   You must sell all of your Emblems, which is a short-term benefit as you will get some FLOWER in exchange.
*   You will lose all of your Marks, so you will want to spend as many of them as you can at Eldric's shop first (but NOT on the equipment pieces).
*   You will be unable to get a Faction Pet Streak XP bonus for **six weeks** after leaving the Faction, even if you are a contributing member for the week in your new Faction.
*   All of your Faction equipment pieces that you bought with Marks will cease to function.
*   You must pay the entry fee for the new Faction.

If you still feel strongly about changing your Faction, sell all of your Emblems, then speak to the NPC in your Faction House who shows you the bonuses for owning Emblems. Your Marks will be removed automatically, so best to spend them beforehand.

title: Chicken Rescue
markdown:
# Chicken Rescue

![](/game-mechanics/mini-games/chickenrescue.png)

# Chicken Rescue

“Help rescue the chickens while avoiding tricky obstacles in this survival challenge!”

Chicken Rescue is one of the minigames accessible through the Kingdom Portal. Completing it gives you a fixed number of Marks, which changes every day along with the goal score. Emblems and items that boost Mark earnings do not affect the payout of this or any other minigame.

## Rules

The point of the game is to rescue at least as many chickens as is specified in the goal for the day. The goal amount is the same for every player, and it will not change in between attempts. You're given 5 attempts to start, and can unlock unlimited attempts for the remainder of the day for 3 FLOWER.

The game is a simple snake-style challenge where every chicken that you “rescue” follows along behind you, creating a trail of increasing length. You lose the round if you touch anything other than a free chicken, including obstacles, the fence bordering the game board, or the chickens that are following you. 

The board is an 18x18 grid, which is divided up into squares. Your character moves forward automatically, you can only change their direction in any of the four cardinal directions. You aren't restricted to the squares for movement, you can move across any pixel in each square. The squares mainly exist to help you align your direction with your target and make sure you won't run into something on the way. That said, your character's hitbox is slightly larger than one square exactly, so you must be careful not to run into anything as you move around obstacles.

Rocks and planter boxes will appear periodically around the map to obstruct you, they will never disappear. Goblins appear as moving obstacles, they will pick a random direction and move for a random number of squares before stopping. Fortunately, they warn you with a “!” above their head before they are about to move. 

Once you reach the target number of chickens, you are free to run into an obstacle to end the game. You can end the game anytime with the icon in the lower-left corner of the screen, and it will not use an attempt unless you made your initial move.  

## Tips/Strategy

*   Play with sound on. The chickens make a clucking noise when you successfully rescue them, letting you know when to change direction.
*   Use a keyboard for precise control, WASD and arrow keys are valid. Swiping is possible on mobile or touchscreen devices, but a keyboard will give you much better results. 
*   Play for as long as you can, even if you have a low goal. Shoot for 50 chickens, the maximum that has been seen so far, so when that day arrives you will be ready.
*   On your first attempt, the board is empty and you will have to wait for chickens to spawn. On subsequent attempts, the board will be randomized and include obstacles and chickens already. Use this to your advantage to plan your route.
*   Some of your Bumpkin's wearables will not display while you are playing this game, most commonly hats. This will not affect your gameplay.

title: Crops & Chickens
markdown:
# Crops & Chickens

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/9a47743e-347d-4dc3-88d6-cd9d5e75a64c/image.png?t=1740657193)

## Introduction

![](/game-mechanics/mini-games/crop-chickens-npc.jpg)

Crops and Chickens is a portal minigame, created by [**Polysemouse**](/en/user-pages/Polysemouse), that will earn the player Marks upon completion. The total number of points required for completion and the reward amount change daily. Marks earned are not affected by Emblem bonuses or equipment, they are the same for all players.

## Rules

The point of the game is to obtain as many crops as you can before the time runs out, while avoiding any of the chickens that roam around the game board. 

In the center of the board is a rug with a chest atop it. This is considered the home base, and where you must return to after picking up any crops. They will not count toward your point total unless you do this.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/7a39538c-dd4f-428d-b31d-41052909048f/image.png?t=1740657156)

The black Ayam Cemani chicken will follow you around wherever you go, though you move faster and can easily outrun it. The white chickens will march forward and not deviate, allowing you to dodge around them. Touching any chicken will cause your Bumpkin to drop all of their crops and return to the rug.

You have until the 2 minute time limit expires to obtain the target score. You will not lose from touching a chicken a certain number of times, only from running out of time. Time running out counts as an attempt, of which you have 5 daily. You can pay FLOWER to get more attempts in a day.

### Points Guide

*   Sunflower: 1
*   Potato: 2
*   Pumpkin: 5
*   Carrot: 10
*   Cabbage: 20
*   Beetroot: 50
*   Cauliflower: 100
*   Parsnip: 250
*   Radish: 1,000
*   Wheat: 2,500
*   Kale: 10,000

## Strategy

A good strategy is to ignore all of the other crops below Cauliflower, and focus on picking up as many of those as you can. There  are at least twenty of them around the sides of the map, which can get you 2000 points if you can get them all. Start in one corner and pick up all of them left to right, then move down to the second row and pick up those too. Then run back to the rug and deposit them as soon as possible. Remember to run forward instead of backtracking, and follow the arrow back to the rug if you get lost. If you see an opening around the Radish or Parsnip, grab it.

### Tips

*   All chickens will kill your Bumpkin. Don’t touch any of them.
*   Your Bumpkin can run faster than the chickens. You can move ahead and cut them off if needed.
*   The map wraps around in all four directions. Don’t move backwards to get to the rug, only move forwards.
*   You have 2 minutes per attempt, but unlimited “lives.” You can get hit by a chicken as many times as you need in one attempt.
*   Use a keyboard! Play on a PC or use a Bluetooth keyboard for your phone, as it gives you much greater control.
*   Keep playing after you reach the goal to practice up for days with high requirements. See how high of a score you can get!

title: Fruit Dash
markdown:
# Fruit Dash

![](/game-mechanics/mini-games/fruit-dash.png)

# Fruit Dash

“Survive as long as you can collecting fruits while dodging obstacles in this endless challenge!”

Fruit Dash is one of the minigames in the Kingdom Portal, created by Felga. Completing it gives you a fixed number of Marks, which changes every day along with the goal score. Emblems and items that boost Mark earnings do not affect the payout of this or any other minigame.

## Rules

This is an endless runner game, where your character moves forward constantly, and you can only move them left and right to avoid obstacles. Anything that is not a fruit or powerup will end your attempt immediately, so avoid them as best you can. You have 5 attempts to reach the goal score per day, after which you can pay 1 FLOWER to unlock 3 more attempts, or 3 FLOWER to get unlimited attempts for the remainder of the day.

The speed at which you run increases as the game progresses, making it harder to dodge obstacles, but the value of each fruit also increases the faster you go. The first two powerups you will find will be the Magic Mushroom, which elevates your consciousness to the point that you can pass through obstacles completely, while still picking up fruits as you run. The other is the Golden Pickaxe, which can be thrown at an obstacle to remove it from your path.

After earning 500 points, the Hourglass may appear, which slows the game down by 20%. It will then continue to speed up as normal. You may also find the Pirate Bounty, which is worth a huge amount of points.

You also earn points by passing obstacles, meaning you earn points constantly without needing to collect fruit. You still want to get as many as you can, though!

## Tips/Strategy

*   Use a keyboard! Your precision control with the A/D or left/right keys will be much greater than the tappable buttons on a touchscreen.
*   Don't fret if you miss fruits. More will come, and you are earning points for every obstacle you dodge.
*   If a fruit is right in front of a large obstacle, let it pass by rather than trying to move out of the way at the last second. Unless you have a pickaxe and can clear it out of your way, of course!
*   When you get a mushroom, continue to dodge obstacles to keep your reflexes up for when the effect ends. The mushroom is essentially insurance to make sure you don't hit something. 
*   Prioritize the hourglasses. They are critical to reaching the highest score goals.
*   There is a tab to donate POL to Felga in appreciation of the hard work that went into this game.

title: Mine Wack
markdown:
# Mine Wack

![](/game-mechanics/mini-games/mine-wack.png)

# Mine Wack

“Tap the moles, dodge the rabbits, and race against time in this reflex challenge!"

Mine Wack is the newest minigame in the Kingdom Portal, created by Felga and Asterion. Completing it gives you a fixed number of Marks, which changes every day along with the goal score. Emblems and items that boost Mark earnings do not affect the payout of this or any other minigame.

## Rules

The rules of this game are very simple, and are summarized well in the description on the button you use to access it. Tap or click on the moles when they appear, and don't tap on rabbits or empty holes. Each time you miss (meaning tapping a hole, a rabbit, or letting a mole escape), you lose one of your 3 lives. In testing the game for this article, I was able to tap on about 5 rabbits and empty holes before losing 1 life, but just focus on hitting all the moles and you will be fine.

The speed at which the moles and rabbits appear and disappear will increase as the game progresses. Different moles worth more points will also start to appear more frequently. There are two varieties of rabbits, one will penalize you more than the other.

There is a bonus meter that will fill up as you hit moles, going from 1x to 5x inclusive. Each level will multiply the score from hitting a mole by that amount. If you lose a life, the meter will reset at 1x.

## Tips/Strategy

*   Use a touchscreen! Unlike every other game where I recommend a keyboard, for this game you will do much better with a touchscreen. If you don't have that kind of a device, a mouse will do fairly well instead.
*   Play with the sound on, you will hear a tone when you reach the target score and can relax. 
*   Keep playing for as long as you can and build up your high score for days that have higher targets.
*   There isn't much other strategy other than to only hit the moles!

title: Potion Room
markdown:
# Potion Room

![](/game-mechanics/mini-games/potion-house.png)

# Potion Room

“Select your potions and unveil the secrets of the plants!”

The Potion Room minigame is accessible by speaking to the NPC Eins in the lower-right corner of the Plaza, near the pair of goblins. Unlike the Kingdom minigames, the Potion Room can be played as long as you have coins to pay for it. The rewards are also completely different, but definitely worth it. It resembles the board game [Mastermind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mastermind_\(board_game\)), and follows the same basic rules.

## Rules

You can begin playing the game with at least 320 Coins. There is a multiplier setting that will increase the amount of Potion Tickets you receive when you win, but will increase the cost proportionally. Choose your level, then begin the game.

There are seven potions for you to choose from, and four slots to put them in. The first potion you select will go into the first slot, then the second, and so on. Once you finish a row of four potions, tap the Mix potion button to submit your guess. An icon for each potion will show you whether the potion belongs in that slot (Green happy face), belongs in a different slot (Yellow neutral face), doesn't belong in any slot (Orange sad face), or is the "chaos potion" (Red scared face). Rearrange your choices, and try again.

It is possible for the same potion to appear more than once in the pattern.

You have three attempts to get the combination correct, and the more correct potions you have in the final row, the more points you will earn, up to the maximum determined by your multiplier. If the chaos potion is in the final row, you will score no Tickets no matter if every other slot is Green. 

## Tips/Strategy

*   Playing the game itself is very straightforward and doesn't require much in the way of strategy, just follow the rules. Use the green book icon in the corner of the screen if you need to review them.
*   The more important strategy to consider is how often to play the game. Unlike the Kingdom games, which cost nothing to play, this game requires you to pay coins, and not a small amount either. New players may be tempted by the Exotic Crops available in the Rewards Shop and try to win some to sell for Coins, but will likely burn through all of their funds first. This game is designed for mid to late-game players who have a steady income of Coins and can afford to spend them.

## Rewards Shop

Each successful completion of the game earns Potion Tickets, which can be turned in for various rewards. There are three cosmetic giant vegetables, which should only be bought after every other item has been claimed.

The Lab Grown Carrot, Radish, and Pumpkin are valuable items to boost your output of those crops. They can be expensive, but will help you in the long run.

The various Exotic Crops are worth high amounts of Coins, and may be eligible for Chapter Tickets at the [Mega Bounty Board](/en/chapter-race/bounty-board). Because of the changing nature of the Board, it's not recommended to buy one until it is up for sale. Even then, the low amount of Chapter Tickets compared to the high amount of Potion Tickets needed makes it hard to justify playing enough to earn one unless you have a lot of Coins and nothing to do with them.

The Magic Bean is a special item that is placed on your farm like a decoration, but after several days will reward you with a random item. It will most likely be one of the Exotics, but has a small chance of providing a special item that will provide a unique boost to your Potato, Radish, or Sunflowers. Specifically, each harvest has a 3% chance of +10 output. The “Mutant” crops are available on the Marketplace if you would rather get them through commerce than luck.

If you are set on trying to collect the Mutants, consider buying the Carrot Sword decoration first, which increases the chances of finding one by 4x.

| Name | Type | Weight | % |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Potent Potato | Mutant | 1 | 0.88% |
| Radical Radish | Mutant | 1 | 0.88% |
| Stellar Sunflower | Mutant | 1 | 0.88% |
| Black Magic | Exotic | 2 | 1.75% |
| Golden Helios | Exotic | 4 | 3.51% |
| Chioggia | Exotic | 4 | 3.51% |
| Purple Cauliflower | Exotic | 25 | 21.93% |
| Adirondack Potato | Exotic | 20 | 17.54% |
| Warty Goblin Pumpkin | Exotic | 20 | 17.54% |
| White Carrot | Exotic | 10 | 8.77% |

## History

Eins used to reside in the Woodlands zone, as one of its only residents. Once inside his house you could talk to him to play the game, or to his assistant to access the Rewards shop. According to Bert, “strange things are happening in the woodlands,” and they are not safe, so Eins moved to the Plaza to continue work on perfecting his plant potions.

title: Love Island
markdown:
# **Love Island (AKA Mystery Island, AKA Floating Island)**

Catch the heart balloon to the mysterious **Love Island** to trade in your [Love Charms](/en/mechanics/love-charms) for [$Flower](/en/home/tokens) or shop rewards. Don’t forget to solve the **Flower Puzzle** to win a bronze love box once a day!

![](/user-pages/potatofather/loveisland_1intro.png)

dreaming of that free daily love box…

## **Where to find it?**

When it’s time, go to Plaza and click the notification at bottom-left, or walk up to the balloon and click to get whisked away to Love Island!

![](/user-pages/potatofather/loveisland_1_notification.png)

(Clicking this notification will teleport you to Love Island!)

## **Flower Puzzle**

Work with other players to solve the flower puzzle and win a bronze love box once a day! The goal is to get all petals to turn Orange.

Dull color = Not enough players on the petal

Orange = Perfect amount of players on the petal

Red = Too many players on the petal

Don't worry if it takes a while to solve it. The point is to get players to work together, which can sometimes take a while. Players may be brand new and not know what to do, or experience lag or connection loss that makes it seem like they're standing on that red petal for no reason. If you can't get the reward, don't fret, as it is relatively small and you'll get another chance later.

![](/user-pages/potatofather/loveisland_2_puzzle.png)

Reward List sourced from sfl world

### **Bonus Tip!** 

Are there players idling on one petal forcing it to be stuck on red? Try **changing servers** and try your luck elsewhere. Go to Settings -> Plaza Settings -> Change Server

![](/user-pages/potatofather/loveisland_3_changeserver.png)

## **Exchange Love Charms for Flower...**

VIP players can go to the well and exchange your hard-earned Love Charms for Flower at a rate of 80 Love Charms = 1 Flower! There is a daily limit of 10,000 Love Charms (125 Flower)

**The screenshot is incorrect, the ratio was changed to 1:80 on April 8, 2026.**

![](/user-pages/potatofather/loveisland_4_well.png)

## **...Or Buy Items in the Shop!**

Save up and spend those love charms on some neat items! Boosts like the hour glass, decor like the statue and rugs, cosmetic wearables like the dino onesie and love aura. Shop items change out daily so check back often! 

![](/user-pages/potatofather/loveisland_5_shop.png)

Reward list sourced from sfl world

## **Can I check Shop Items ahead of time?**

You can use [sfl.world](https://sfl.world/) to check that day’s rewards, just enter your farm id and see the Checklist section on your Info Page.

![](/user-pages/potatofather/loveisland_checklist.png)

## _**When**_ **Does it Fly?**

In-game you can check two ways: Going directly to the Balloon itself, or your Codex. The Balloon flies three times a day for 30 minutes, and the displayed times are conveniently in your time zone.

![](/user-pages/potatofather/loveisland_when_fly.png)

## **Additional Links**

Link to rewards lists!

[Bronze Love Box contents, via Chests page of SFL world](https://sfl.world/info/chests)

[Love Shop Items list, via Constants page of SFL world](https://sfl.world/info/const)

title: Guardian Tribute
markdown:
# Guardian Tribute

**This feature has been disabled and the information provided here is for historical reference.**

**⚔️ Guardian Tribute**

A **Guardian Tribute** lasts for **24 hours** and occurs **daily**.

Its mechanic functions as a tribute event involving a **random resource** such as _Kale_, _Gold_, or _Crimstone_. A total of **90%** of the contributed resources are **redistributed among the top 30%** of contributors, while the remaining **10% is permanently burned 🔥**.

This feature introduces an element of **risk and strategy 📊**. Players must analyze previous contributions to secure a position within the top 30%. Overcontributing can result in losses — for example, contributing **500 Gold** when the average distribution is **300 Gold** may lead to a **net loss** of resources 💎.

* * *

**📍Where to find it ?**

Visit Kingdom > go near the bridge and visit the guardian. There is also a guardian on the left-most side of the [Love Island](/en/events/love-island), though they will offer the same deal as the one in the Kingdom. The appearance of the Guardian will change depending on the current in-game [season](/en/mechanics/seasons).

title: History
description: a detailed accounting of the Bumpkin's history
markdown:
# Timeline

0 AB - Bumpkin Beginnings

500 AB - Sunflorians

760 AB - Sunflower Land

780 AB - Goblins

960 AB - Moon seekers

## Bumpkin Beginnings

Timeline: 0 AB - 500 AB

###### **Saphiro**

![](/saphiro_bumpkin.png)

A Saphiro Bumpkin

  The earliest known recordings of Bumpkin blood traces back to the ancient Saphiro tribe, a group of brilliant Bumpkins that inhabited the Southern Sunflower Isles.

 For centuries these Bumpkins mastered the arts of farming, crafting and gathering. Through trial and error they uncovered the secrets of advanced cultivating,  discovered exotic minerals and danced with the dangers of alchemy. 

 Unfortunately there are few known records kept from this historic time as all tradition and advanced techniques were passed down only through storytelling. Saphiron  Bumpkins were not boastful, which meant only rumors and folklore of the origins of these people remain today. 

###### Broadminded Bumpkins

For a long time, life was blissful in Saphiro - Bumpkins blossomed and innovations were discovered daily.

However, it wasn’t long before a new generation of curious Bumpkins emerged who were willing to push the boundaries. They grew discontent living in small communities and upholding the traditions of their people.

These bored Bumpkins began to build buoyant boats that could travel distances previously unheard of. They honed their sailing skills and over the years they spread throughout the Sunflower Isles, discovering warmer regions, foreign resources and eventually building the initial Kingdoms of the islands.

The most notorious of these Kingdoms was the Sunflorians.

## Sunflorians

500 AB - 760 AB

###### **The Sunflorian Dynasty**

The Sunflorians were a brave race that bred bold Bumpkins, constantly looking to conquer and expand their reach throughout the Sunflower Isles. Over the centuries, these Bumpkins wrote their name into the history books with discoveries of Stone Haven, Treasure Island, The Retreat and even the far reaching Snow Kingdom.

These initial explorers eventually became the royal families that ruled the Sunflower Isles and the Sunflorian Dynasty was born. It was a prosperous time for all Bumpkins and the future looked bright. Technology was rapidly advancing and they were discovering new land & innovations daily. It was a symbol of pride to be a Sunflorian.

The centre of the Sunflorian sphere was discovery and expansion. As the royal family grew, so did mass mining and deforestation across the islands. The Sunflorians wanted to extract every resource and build as much as they could.

However, as the Sunflorian empire grew, grave rumours spread. It became clear that the discovery of new islands was slowing down. Bold Bumpkins would voyage vast distances on expeditions in search of bountiful land. For the Bumpkins that returned, all they brought was bad news and stories of endless seas and treacherous creatures.

Sunflorians were losing Bumpkins and ships everyday and were facing an existential crisis. If there was no more land to explore, what is a Bumpkin good for?

###### **Bumpkin Bans - 720 AB**

To avoid more death and disappointment, Queen Bella (_702 AB-758AB_) of the Sunflorians instated an exploration ban on all Bumpkins. Bumpkins were always a peaceful community and begrudgingly accepted this decision.

With a ban on travel, the islands were becoming overcrowded and land was rapidly turning sterile. With no other choice, new measures were brought in to preserve resources and space that restricted Bumpkins from building new structures. As the population grew, the Sunflorians clamped down further on these restrictions to keep the peace in the Kingdom. No more crafting, no more planting and no unlicensed trading.

The Bumpkin Boomers who grew up in the bustling exploration period carried fond memories of their voyages and could find peace knowing that they lived a fulfilled life. However, the Bumpkin babies were being brought up in a backward kingdom and were quickly becoming bored and restless.

It wasn’t long before the new generation began experimenting with illegal home-grown parsnips, sneaking out at night to chop down trees, crafting boats and going on joy rides to the retreat.

![](/bored_bumpkin.png)

A Bored Bumpkin - 756 AB

 The Sunflorians were not blind to the rising restlessness of their society. They were losing grip of control. To retain power, more bans were implemented and  young Bumpkins were rounded up and jailed. It was evident that conditions were worsening everyday. Riots broke out and  prisons overflowed. At risk of a  revolution, the Sunflorians made a grave announcement.

 All Bumpkins who opposed the Sunflorian Kingdom would be banished from the Sunflower Isles, in search of their own land.

 The young buzzing Bumpkins thought their dreams had come true. However, the Bumpkin elders knew this was a death wish. There was nothing to discover but  death and disappointment across the seas.

## Sunflower Land

760 AB

###### The Banished Boat

A fleet of boats were arranged for the banished Bumpkins and convicts of the Sunflorian Kingdom. With rumours of treacherous winds to the East, endless water to the South, and dangerous monsters to the West, there was only one direction to go. North. The banished Bumpkins were given a barrel of local Sunflorian Parsnips, a handful of seeds and a wave goodbye.

![](/brainy_blake.png)

Blake the Brainy - 762 AB

 The travelling Bumpkins faced perilous conditions, starvation and were on the brink of mutiny. Dark days, cold nights and endless Parsnip soup were beating the  Bumpkin’s spirit. Luckily, amongst these banished Bumpkins, was Blake the Brainy. Blake had learnt ancient sailing skills passed down through his Saphiron  heritage. Through his brilliance and perseverance, the fleet survived the toughest of conditions and held together.

 On the 9th week of the journey a miracle appeared on the horizon - Land! As they grew closer they saw vibrant beaches and green pastures filled with Sunflowers.  The Bumpkins were breath-taken, they had just discovered **Sunflower Land** 🌻

###### **The Pioneering Settlers**

![](/buzzing_bumpkin.png)

Pioneering Buzzing Bumpkin - 778 AB

 The Bumpkin pioneers were buzzing with excitement as they landed on the shores of Sunflower Land. The settlers cultivated Sunflowers, built houses and  explored the surrounding fields. Villages were flourishing, farming was booming and the Bumpkins were blissful. They thought they had found paradise.

 However, they soon discovered they were not alone.

###### **First Encounters**

![](/brooke.png)

Brooke the Bumpkin - 780 AB

 During a daily seed gathering routine, Brooke the Bumpkin decided to venture further into the forest to search for exotic seeds. The forest was foreign, puzzling  and she quickly became lost. With no bearings, she wandered endlessly for days through the forest trying to find her way home.

 One morning she heard strange noises coming from a nearby Blueberry bush. She was curious about the unusual noises but delighted to find breakfast. As she  grew closer and reached out her hand to grab a blueberry she heard a loud noise - ACKK!!!

 A small green creature popped out of the bush, timid and on high alert. The creature was roughly the same size as Brooke but had rough green skin, long pointy  ears and was built like a buffalo.

 The creature’s mouth was smeared in bright blue blueberries and Brooke realised she had interrupted a feast. It was not trying to attack Brooke, it was only trying  to _gobble_ as many Blueberries as possible.

![](/goblin-export.png)

The Gobbling Goblin - 780 AB

 In an act of peace, Brooke pulled out a Parsnip brought from the Sunflorian Kingdoms and offered it to the creature. The creature came forward slowly with eyes  wide open. The smell of parsnip filled the creatures nostrils and in an instant it snatched the parsnip and swiftly _gobbled_ it down, followed by a loud belch.

 Brooke giggled and the tension between the two eased. She decided to call it Goblin.

# Yakkamon

![1\_-4nlhawwn9yiqu2ea0xbrw.gif](/side-projects/1_-4nlhawwn9yiqu2ea0xbrw.gif)

## Yakkamon

**Yakkamon** (known as Project II during development) is a monster-collecting tactical battler game set in the FLOWER ecosystem. It is a standalone project, not a mini-game, and is being developed alongside _Sunflower Land_. The game is confirmed to be a **creature collector** with roguelike elements, real-time speed-based combat, farming mechanics, and a shared economy with _Sunflower Land_ via the FLOWER token.

Official website: [https://yakkamon.com](https://yakkamon.com)

> **Original announcement (August 2021–2025 context):**  
> _Project II is confirmed to be a monster-collecting tactical battler game. Other than using the FLOWER token to buy and sell resources, no other connections to Sunflower Land have been confirmed yet._  
> — Medium: _Sunflower Report – The Road to 2026_

* * *

### 🔧 Development Timeline (2026)

#### January 2026

*   **2026-01-06** – Core combat prototype begins internal testing. The team is satisfied with the combat model and begins prototyping meta-game systems around it. A future stream or GIF showing progress is possible.
*   **2026-01-20** – Beta is scheduled for **Q3 2026**. The game is described as a “rethink of web3 gaming”: a creature catcher/trading game with a shared economy with _Sunflower Land_. It is not a farming game and aims to attract new audiences (e.g., no Bumpkin battles in SFL).

#### February 2026

*   **2026-02-10** – GitHub development progresses. After core mechanics are locked, beta is expected in **July/August 2026**.
*   **2026-02-13** – Spencer moves to full-time P2 development. Genre confirmed as **creature collector**. Influences include _Temtem_ and _Slay the Spire_. The game will be web-based, mobile-friendly, with menu-oriented combat (not MMO-style). FLOWER token will be incorporated with its own economy. Possible tournament systems with entry fees are discussed.
*   **2026-02-19** – Vertical slice spec document completed. Combat is **not turn-based** but **real-time speed-based** (similar to _Final Fantasy VII_). Key features:
    *   Runs (roguelike style)
    *   Taming creatures
    *   Farming with creatures
    *   PvP
    *   Economic design: creatures require resources for healing, feeding, training
    *   Resources burned in P2 will also burn FLOWER from _Sunflower Land_
    *   Breeding mini-game planned with stat genetics
    *   Player-vs-player combat will help counteract inflation
*   **2026-02-27** – First sneak peek. The game features monster battling, exploration, and farming elements. Roguelike exploration approach with runs, battles, resource gathering. Same FLOWER token across both games. A **centralized marketplace** is shared between games. Beta target remains Q3 2026. A public prototype may be released early for feedback.

#### March 2026

*   **2026-03-05** – Spencer works exclusively on P2. A breakthrough in game look and UI is achieved with Adam. A tutorial run is shown with nodes for battles and other activities. The game is built with **Unity** (different from _Sunflower Land_’s React). A “vertical slice” (full run of the game) is being built for feedback.
*   **2026-03-13** – Core mechanics detailed:
    *   **Roguelike exploring and taming**
    *   **3 core aspects**: farming, battling, roguelike adventure
    *   **3v3 battles** with type advantages (e.g., water cancels electricity)
    *   Farm with monsters – catch monsters and put them to work on fields
    *   Gather resources to feed monsters and prepare for battle
    *   Monsters have types affecting both battles and farming (e.g., desert monsters for certain plots)
    *   **Launch plan**:
        *   Beta launch: closed – top _Sunflower Land_ players first
        *   Next round: competition inside _Sunflower Land_
        *   Then restricted to ~10,000 players for load testing
        *   Will use FLOWER and have a marketplace for trading creatures/resources

#### April 2026

*   **2026-04-02** – **Public prototype demo released** at [project-ii.sunflower-land.com](https://project-ii.sunflower-land.com/).
    *   Only one creature (**Grassling**) is initially available.
    *   Players can capture creatures and attempt to reach **Firebug Level 2** (boss).
    *   Not playable on mobile at this time.
    *   Feedback button is available on the farm screen under the shop icon.
    *   **No plans** to use pets or buds from _Sunflower Land_ – the game will have its own original creatures.

* * *

### 🎮 Confirmed Game Features (as of April 2026)

| Category | Details |
| --- | --- |
| **Genre** | Monster collector, roguelike, tactical battler |
| **Combat** | Real-time speed-based (like Final Fantasy VII), 3v3, type advantages |
| **Exploration** | Node-based roguelike runs (battles, resource gathering, events) |
| **Farming** | Monsters can work on fields; types affect farming efficiency |
| **Economy** | FLOWER token shared with Sunflower Land; resources burned in P2 also burn FLOWER; centralized marketplace |
| **Monster Systems** | Taming, feeding, healing, training, breeding mini-game with stat genetics |
| **PvP** | Yes – helps counteract inflation; possible tournament system with entry fees |
| **Platform** | Web-based, browser-friendly; mobile-friendly (but demo not mobile-ready as of Apr 2, 2026) |
| **Engine** | Unity (different from Sunflower Land’s React) |
| **Beta Window** | Q3 2026 (July/August) |
| **Early Access** | Closed beta for top SFL players first, then competition, then ~10,000 players |

* * *

### 🌸 FLOWER Token Usage in Project II

As originally announced, FLOWER remains the native token for:

*   NFT drops
*   Gameplay perks
*   Exclusive content

Additionally, based on 2026 updates:

*   FLOWER will be used for healing, feeding, training creatures
*   Burning resources in P2 also burns FLOWER from _Sunflower Land_, linking the economies
*   A shared marketplace will allow trading creatures and resources using FLOWER

* * *

### 🔗 Relationship to Sunflower Land

*   **Sunflower Land remains the primary focus** of the team and the primary FLOWER generation method.
*   Project II is a **separate game** with its own creatures, systems, and economy, but shares the FLOWER token.
*   There is **no cross-use** of Sunflower Land pets or buds in Project II.
*   Top Sunflower Land players will receive priority access to the closed beta.

* * *

### 🛡️ Development Philosophy

*   No ICO, no direct sale of FLOWER.
*   Built in public from scratch, with community feedback from day one.
*   Open-source principles, sustainable economies, community-first design.

* * *

*   **April–June 2026** – Vertical slice testing, feedback collection, UI polish.
*   **July–August 2026** – Beta launch (closed → limited → ~10k players).
*   **Q3 2026** – Public beta target.

title: Mayor
markdown:
# Mayor

![](/npcs/mayor.jpg)

## The Mayor

The Mayor resides in the middle of the Pumpkin Plaza, directly above the pier where you initially arrive. His closest neighbor is the [Blacksmith](/en/npcs/blacksmith). 

He will initially greet new players when they arrive in the Plaza for the first time, prompting them to choose a username. Provided it is available, the player will be known by that name henceforth. He also provides them with the game's [Code of Conduct](https://docs.sunflower-land.com/support/terms-of-service/code-of-conduct). 

Like many other characters, the Mayor's actual name isn't known, he only goes by his title.

## Name Change

If you decide that you really don't like your username, you can pick a different one. The Mayor explains that this process requires paperwork, and the administrative cost is 250 Gems. If you are really dissatisfied with your handle, visit him to change it.

## Quotes

"Hmmm, don't you just love the smell of coffee?"

"I hope you enjoy your stay in Sunflower Land! If you ever need me again, just come back to me!"

## History

The ability to change usernames is very new, being added in an update in March of 2025, nearly three years after the game was launched. Prior to that, new players were assigned a string of random numbers as their username, and had to visit the Mayor to get a name of their choosing. At the time this was an easy way to identify bots, as their operators only focused on extracting resources from the game.

title: Bailey

# Bailey

## Bailey

Bailey resides in the right side of the Plaza, between the Auction House and Poppy. He offers the four weather protection items, and nothing else. Each one will protect your farm from the negative effects of the weather events that can occur each season. He will also explain the various events in another tab.

He seems to be making quite the profit from his trade, as he is holding the Autumn's Embrace shield, which as of this writing is worth thousands of FLOWER.

Bailey's name is a pun on “bailing out," or giving relief or aid in response to a disaster.

## Weather Items

*   Tornado Pinwheel (prevents the Tornados that damage your crops and buildings in summer or autumn)
*   Mangrove (prevents the Tsunami that also does damage to your farm in spring)
*   Thermal Stone (prevents the Great Freeze that slows your crops down in winter)
*   Protective Pesticide (prevents the Insect Plague that reduces your yields in spring or summer)

title: Pumpkin' Pete
markdown:
# Pumpkin' Pete

![](/npcs/pumpkin_pete.jpg)

## Pumpkin' Pete

Pete is an NPC residing in the Pumpkin Plaza, perhaps deriving his name from the place, or perhaps the other way around. He is the easiest NPC to reach, being immediately to the left of the initial arrival location in the Plaza. Pete requests very simple foods and products for his deliveries, making him the easiest NPC to satisfy. He is a Ticket delivery NPC, meaning he will reward you with the current Chapter Ticket, and will be unavailable for the first week of each Chapter. 

Pete is the main guide for Sunflower Land, teaching new players the ropes of farming and the various things you can do around the islands. He also appears on your Home Farm, paddling his coracle up to your shores to provide tips and tricks for your farming journey.

He prefers Yellow Cosmos above all other flowers.

## Rewards

*   5 points
    *   160x Coins
*   12 points
    *   Treasure Key
*   50 points
    *   Pumpkin Hat (wearable hat)
*   100 points
    *   640x Coins
*   200 points and every 100 points after
    *   640 coins

## Quotes

"Hey there, newbie! How 'bout some fresh produce?"

"Fresh and delightful, that's my motto. What do you have?"

## Trivia

Pete used to be the means by which players were informed of the schedule for Double Delivery Day. After making a successful delivery, he would whisper the information in his success window. Now that the Calendar has been established, he no longer does this.

Pete's full title is Pumpkin' Pete, which is linguistically odd. The gerund form in English denotes a present action, such as “jumping” or “walking." The ‘g’ is dropped and replaced with an apostrophe to denote a rural or colloquial way of speaking: “been farmin' all day.” Therefore, the more proper form of his title would be “Pumpking,” and the root verb form “Pumpk.” Perhaps he truly is the Pumpkin King of Sunflorea, biding his time before he can take back his throne from Tywin and the other pretenders…

# Tywin

Tywin is a royal NPC who resides in the Plaza, just below the entrance to the Kingdom. He requests very expensive items such as Gold, Golden Pickaxes, Crimstone, and high sums of Coins. He is a Ticket delivery NPC, meaning he will reward you with the current Chapter Ticket, and will be unavailable for the final week of each Chapter. 

He is the favored prince of the realm, though his relationship to the reigning monarch Victoria is not clear. He would be in the Kingdom, away from the common folk, if it weren't for the treasure chest just below him. He's unable to resist the lure of the gold that might be lurking inside.

Common flowers are not fit for a prince, and Tywin won't settle for anything less than a Primula Enigma or a Celestial Frostbloom.

Tywin's impertinence has led to a [recurring joke](https://discord.com/channels/880987707214544966/1264714770817224724/1343376846074413108) at his expense where the developers of the game blame any downtime or bugs on him.

## Timmy

A strange young fellow in a bear suit, Timmy resides in the upper-right corner of the Plaza, between Bert and Betty. Timmy used to only request fruits and sometimes drinks made from the Smoothie Shack, but now has taken to playing with dolls and wants them for his collection. This makes him one of the most expensive NPCs to cater to, and without delivery point rewards, it is hard to justify the cost of his requests outside of Double Delivery Day.

# Bert

![](/npcs/bert.jpg)

Bert is an NPC residing in the upper-right corner of the Pumpkin Plaza, near the old entrance to the Woodlands zone. He frequently requests Wood, Stone, Axes, Honey, and Mushrooms for his deliveries. He is a Ticket delivery NPC, meaning he will reward you with the current Chapter Ticket, and will be unavailable for the final week of each Chapter. 

Bert is the town's crazy old man, wearing tattered clothing and ranting about visions he's seen when consuming the Magic Mushrooms that grow on Bumpkin's farms. He may also have been a pirate at some point. As of Chapter 9: Winds of Change, he has taken to wearing a Crab Hat, making him somewhat easier to identify in the Codex.

He prefers all of the Lotus flowers in any color.

## Rewards

*   60 points
    *   Tattered Jacket (wearable shirt)
    *   Recipe- Wooly Doll
*   100 points
    *   20x Gems
    *   Recipe- Cluck Doll
*   210 points
    *   3x Pirate Cake
    *   Recipe- Cow Bed
*   330 points
    *   Greyed Glory (wearable hair)
    *   Recipe- Moo Doll

## Quotes

“Mushroom madness, that's me. Magic Mushrooms, anyone?”

“The mushrooms tell me secrets about the missing animals!”

## Bert's Obsessions

Prior to Chapter 9, Bert had a unique mechanic known as his Obsession. Every 3 days, he would request a random item and ask to see it, but not take it from you, in exchange for Tickets. Most often these items were already available in the Marketplace from previous chapters, but some were from the current Chapter and weren't sellable yet, or could not be traded under normal circumstances. 

An item being chosen for an Obsession would inevitably raise the price on the Marketplace dramatically, but by getting tickets for it, you would be unable to sell it until the next Obsession was chosen. This system was removed in May of 2025 in favor of the current Bounty Board.

title: Digby
markdown:
# Digby

![](/npcs/digby.jpg)

Digby resides in the upper portion of the Beach, to the right of the Dig Site. He surveys the shifting sands of the site daily, and has a rough idea of how treasures are grouped together. Speaking to him will show you clues that will help you find the treasures you seek. He also gives an overview of digging itself.

Digby must have traded some of his excavated relics to the [Jester](/en/npcs/jester) for some confetti, as he will throw a handful of it every time you excavate a tile, no matter what you uncover.

To prevent damage from over-excavation, each Bumpkin is only allowed to dig a certain amount of times each day. Digby enforces this rule with his ever-watchful gaze, but may be persuaded to allow a little more work in exchange for some precious Gems…

If you discover all three of the Chapter artifacts in a single day, Digby will reward you with a fourth artifact, and a bonus item. If you prove yourself a competent digger for multiple days in a row, Digby will reward you with better items. You can see the breakdown of streaks and rewards at [https://sfl.world/info/chests](https://sfl.world/info/chests)

Digby is not a delivery NPC, and will not accept any items or flowers. You can access Digby's menu by tapping the “New dig site!” button at the bottom of the screen. He will also give you your streak reward automatically, meaning it is unnecessary to be near him at all.

## Quotes

“Hey, you need a sand shovel to dig here! Talk to [Jafar](/en/npcs/jafar).”

“Howdy explorer, today the following items have been spotted in the desert puzzle.”

# Finn

## Finn

![](/npcs/finn.jpg)

Finn resides in the central area of the Beach, on a pier above [Corale](/en/npcs/corale). He requests various fish, the trash you find on other players farms, and Leather, all in exchange for Chapter Tickets. As a Ticket NPC, he will not accept deliveries during the final weeks of the Chapter.

He is the brother of [Finley](/en/npcs/finley), engaged in an ongoing fishing competition with her. He appears to use the items he requests as chum for fishing, though he requests fish directly, and may be passing those off to his sister as specimens he has caught himself…

He prefers the White and Blue Cosmos over other kinds of flowers.

## Fishing Lure

Finn is the primary source of Fishing Lures available to players, the others being chests and rewards. He will sell the player any amount of lures for 10 Gems or 100 Feathers each. Check the prices on the Marketplace and the FLOWER/Gem exchange rate to determine which is the best deal at the time.

During the period between chapters when Ticket NPCs refuse deliveries, Finn will still sell Fishing Lures.

*   Every 130 points after- Rare Key

title: Farmhands
markdown:
# Farmhands

As you explore more of the game, you may find yourself with multiple pieces of wearable equipment that provide useful boosts, but only one slot to put them in. While you can wear two shirts in real life, your Bumpkin can't, so you'll have to invite some friends to help you maximize your potential!

## Farmhand Usage

Farmhands are extra characters that you can assign to your farm and have them wear additional pieces of equipment. If you have two hats that both provide a benefit, you can't equip them both to your primary Bumpkin. With an extra Farmhand, you can use them, and even more. You can have as many Farmhands as there are Beds available in the game. Enter your Farmhouse and tap on the Add Farm Hand button to see the current lineup. More are added frequently, so check back each Chapter.

Farmhands come with their own random (cosmetic-only) equipment when hired, so don't worry if you don't have enough shirts and pants to clothe them all.

If you decide you really like the style of one of your Farmhands and want to show it off in the plaza, tap the Set as Bumpkin button. This will set your active character to be the Farmhand instead, meaning you control them when making deliveries and visiting areas outside your farm. If you change your mind, just find your last character and promote them back again.

The primary Bumpkin is the one you feed to gain XP, so either tap on them wherever they are on your farm, or tap the portrait button in the upper-left and select Feed Bumpkin.

## Beds

Bumpkins won't stick around your farm without a place to sleep, so you'll have to build them a bed if you want them to help out. If you started playing the game recently, you should already have a Basic Bed in your house. If you don't, you will need to make one before you can build the others. Get a Crafting Box if you haven't already, and follow the recipes to build a Basic Bed. Place it in your farm, then your primary Bumpkin will claim it. Then, start work on the next one. The recipes for all of the beds can be found at [https://sfl.world/info/crafting](https://sfl.world/info/crafting)

You do not have to build them in any specific order, but the order shown in the Farmhouse menu is the recommended one, due to the price and complexity of the components needed for each one.

Beds are also rewarded through participation in the current Chapter Race, so keep an eye out for where they might be available every few months.

## Placement on the Farm

Farmhands may get tired of just hanging out on the porch of your house, so let them roam about! Farmhands can be picked up and moved anywhere on your farm just like a decoration or resource node. If you remove them, they will return to standing in front of your farmhouse and not go into the Chest.

Currently, the location of a Farmhand doesn't affect the boosts provided by their equipment.

title: Ascension
markdown:
# Ascension

**This feature is new as of Chapter 15, and may change at any time. Please refer to the game for the most accurate info.**

Source**:** [https://github.com/sunflower-land/sunflower-land/discussions/7343](https://github.com/sunflower-land/sunflower-land/discussions/7343) 

Volcano Island is not the end! After expanding your island as far as it will go, you will be prompted by a helpful Goblin to Upgrade your island to a new type (Basic→Spring→Desert→Volcano). Now you can keep on going, and gain some powerful enhancements along the way!

Upon reaching Bumpkin Level 150 and expanding the Volcano Island to its maximum, you will be presented with the option to Ascend. This will have several immediate effects, including lowering your level back to 50, raising your Ascension Level (A) and changing your island to a new type. Despite your level being lowered, your total skill points will not go down, in fact it will continue to go up as you keep leveling. This will let you unlock even more skills and bonuses, and use the Ascension Shard items you find to push your boosts even further.

## **Basic Ascension Flow**

*   Reach Level 150 and max out Volcano Island
*   Upgrade to reach Swamp Island (A1)
*   Expand Swamp Island 12 times and earn 50 XP levels
*   Upgrade to Spooky Island (A2)
*   Repeat (50 levels, 12 expansions):
    *   Crystal Island (A3)
    *   Galaxy Island (A4)
    *   Marble Island (A5+)

You will continue to earn skill points for each of the 50 levels needed to reach the next Ascension, and you will continue to gain new resource nodes, crop plots, and all the things you usually find when expanding your island. This makes [node forging](/en/mechanics/sunstone) more useful than ever.

New biomes are available in the Landscaping Shop for each of the island types if you decide you really like the look of one and don't want to leave it behind as you continue your rise to glory.

## Ascension Shards

Gained from Ascension Crystals, these special nodes will appear on your island after certain expansion levels. When mined with a Gold Pickaxe, they give you 3 Ascension Shards, then disappear completely, with no replenishment. Shards are used to upgrade learned [skills](/en/mechanics/skills) to higher tiers. Higher-tier skills have greater bonuses, but also more severe penalties…

After moving from the Basic (Tutorial) island to Petal Paradise, you will find one Ascension Crystal node as you expand your land. After upgrading to Desert Island, you will uncover another one in the sands, and a third one is buried under the ashes of the Volcano Island.

After Ascending beyond Volcano Island, you will get more Crystals as you continue to expand, so don't worry. It is totally possible to unlock every rank of every skill! 

If you were an existing player before the Ascension Age Chapter started, you will get some Ascension Crystal nodes as soon as you complete your next expansion, and will gain more as you continue to expand your island.

title: Chapter Raffle
markdown:
# Chapter Raffle

![](/chapter-mechanics/raffles.png)

### Chapter Raffles

Wondering what to do with all those Chapter Tickets? Try your luck in a little game! Every week during a chapter, a certain set of items will be put up for raffle. You can buy entries using Chapter Tickets, or other resources specified in the raffle details. Unlike auctions, where the richest players always win, raffles allow for newer players to participate as well. Even though you may only have 10 entries and that top-level player has 1,000, you still stand a chance to win something!

To enter a raffle, visit the Auctioneer's house in the Plaza and tap on the chest labeled Prizes. Or, you can just access the current raffle in your Chapter Dashboard from anywhere in the game.

You can also view the results of past raffles from the Plaza, including the amount of entries the winners had submitted. Don't think that your single entry isn't worth anything.

Remember that you can only win **one prize per raffle**, no matter how many entries you submit.

### Earning Entries

Most raffles will accept two forms of entry: Chapter Tickets and Chapter _Raffle_ Tickets. Standard tickets are earned from deliveries and bounties, while Raffle Tickets are currently earned only from the Chapter Pass rewards.

*   Chapter Tickets are worth **10 entries**
*   Raffle Tickets are worth **1 entry**

The reason for two different forms of entry is to allow players to keep their standard tickets and try for the high-level Megastore items while also being able to participate in the raffles. You cannot remove entries from a raffle once you have submitted them, but you can add more up until the end date.

### Prize Tickets

While the Goblin Raffle may have officially ended, its spirit lives on with the Chapter Raffles. Every month of the chapter will have a special raffle for a Bud NFT and other fantastic prizes, which will accept Prize Tickets as forms of entry.

*   Prize Tickets are worth **200 entries** in the Bud raffle only
*   Chapter Tickets and Raffle Tickets are worth their normal amount of entries (if they are accepted)

### Chances of Winning

While the raffle mechanic is still brand new and no statistics are available, the list of prizes for each raffle is encouraging. Unlike an auction, 100 prizes will be handed out per week, all of which are useful in some way. Even if you don't get the headliner prize, you could still win some Gems or a high-tier Food Box.

If you don't win anything in the previous week's auction, you will receive 100 coins as a consolation prize.

title: Fermentation & Aging
markdown:
# Fermentation & Aging

![](/game-mechanics/aging_shed.png)

Smells delicious….

Welcome to the long game! Salt deposits have been discovered around home islands, and every farmer is racing to rake it up and make use of its properties of preservation. 

## Salt Harvesting

Salt nodes must be unlocked in order to begin harvesting. Salt works a little differently than other minerals. Each node will accumulate one charge every 7 hours, and can hold three charges at once. The number of charges on each node is shown visually (0- empty, 1- sprinkling of salt, 2- mound of salt, 3- pile of salt) and the time for the next one to be added is shown numerically.

To obtain salt, craft a Salt Rake for 3 Wood and 20 Coins. Salt Rakes will be stock limited and require restocks to replenish. No Salt Rakes will be included in the free daily shipment restock. Then, use one Rake per charge on every node, for **10** Salt at the base level. Harvesting does not reset the timer for a node, it will still replenish at the same time whether you harvest with 4 hours or 4 minutes remaining.

Salt is tradable on the marketplace, but there is much more you can do with it.

*   Initial Unlock- 1 Node
    *   30x Wood, 20x Stone, 200x Coins
*   Level 2- 2 Nodes
    *   1000x Coins, 15x Stone, 5x Iron, 100x Salt
*   Level 3- 4 Nodes
    *   4000x Coins, 500x Wood, 40x Gold, 200x Salt
*   Level 4- 6 Nodes
    *   12000x Coins, 100x Gold, 1000x Salt

## Aging Shed

After harvesting some of the sea's salty goodness, you can further unlock its power by building the Aging Shed, at an affordable cost of 200 Coins and 30 Wood. Once it is placed, you will have access to several new features: the Aging Rack, the Fermentation Rack, and the Spice Rack.

Each of these function like their own individual buildings, and have multiple slots where you can run different products simultaneously. Unlike the VIP queue for cooking buildings, all recipes will run concurrently as soon as they are added, and this does not require VIP. You must collect all finished products at the same time. More slots can be obtained by upgrading the building itself, up to 6 per rack. Each upgrade level adds a slot to all racks.

Upgrade Costs- (Number of slots is equal to level)

*   Level 2: 100x Stone, 20x Gold, 3000x Coins
*   Level 3: 500x Wood, 500x Stone, 4000x Coins
*   Level 4: 100x Gold, 10,000x Coins
*   Level 5: 10x Crimstone, 20,000x Coins
*   Level 6: 100,000x Coins

### (Fish) Aging Rack

This process will take fish and age them, which will increase their XP value and allow them to be used in other processes. The amount of Salt and the time needed are directly proportional to the amount of XP that the fish is worth, and can be affected by skills and other factors. Aged Fish (silver) has a chance of being upgraded automatically to a Prime Aged Fish (gold) upon collection. Prime Aged fish are worth 30% more XP when eaten (compared to non-prime aged), and when used to make Fermented Baits, yield double what a normal Aged Fish would provide.

As you can see from the table, the XP/Salt ratio goes down rapidly, with the highest-XP fish requiring huge amounts of salt, not to mention very long processing times. When first starting out, the recommended path to level via Aged Fish is to stick with Anchovy, Red Snapper, or Tuna, as each have a guaranteed bait+chum combination that make them very reliable to harvest in large amounts. Once you start producing fish products, it is better to catch multiple sharks per cast and age those.

All bonuses that affect XP affect Aged Fish, so it is still worth waiting for your Faction Pet bonus to peak at 50% before eating them. 

#### Aged Fish Table

| Aged Fish | Tier | Salt | Base XP | Aged XP | XP/Salt | Time (min) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Anchovy | Basic | 5 | 80 | 240 | 48.0 | 32 |
| Red Snapper | Advanced | 6 | 100 | 300 | 50.0 | 40 |

| White Shark | Expert | 200 | 2000 | 10000 | 50.0 | 480 |

### Fermentation Rack

The most useful job in the building, this allows you to take many resources and create many others. The slot system allows you to process multiple kinds of products at one time.

**Pickled Vegetables**\- Each recipe takes 1 hour. These are only used as ingredients in other recipes, they cannot be eaten directly.

*   Pickled Zucchini- 75x Zucchini + 5x Salt
*   Pickled Tomato- 15x Tomato + 5x Salt
*   Pickled Pepper- 30x Pepper + 5x Salt
*   Pickled Broccoli- 20x Broccoli + 5x Salt
*   Pickled Radish- 10x Radish + 5x Salt
*   Pickled Onion- 10x Onion + 5x Salt

**Greenhouse Fertilizers**\- Each recipe takes 2 hours.

*   Greenhouse Glow- 1x Pickled Tomato, Zucchini, or Broccoli + 1x Refined Salt
    *   Reduces Greenhouse plot growth time by 20%
    *   Like with Rapid Root, this fertilizer will affect the remaining time on a plot, so use it before you plant to get the maximum benefit.
*   Greenhouse Goodie - 1x Pickled Radish, Pepper, or Onion + 1x Refined Salt
    *   Increases Greenhouse plot yield by 0.2

**Combination Fertilizers**\- Each recipe takes 2 minutes.

*   Sproutroot Surprise- 5x Sprout Mix + 5x Rapid Root + 2x Refined Salt
    *   Yields 5 units. Combines the effects of Rapid Root & Sprout Mix (50% growth time and +0.2 yield)
    *   The Knowledge Crab NFT affects this fertilizer also, increasing its bonus to +0.4 yield.
*   Turbofruit Mix- 5x Rapid Root + 5x Fruitful Blend + 2x Refined Salt
    *   Yields 5 units. Reduces fruit patch growth time by 20% and adds 0.1 to yield. The Fruitful Bounty skill **will** increase the yield bonus just like the normal fertilizer.
    *   Like with Rapid Root, applying this fertilizer will affect the **remaining** time before a fruit patch is ready to harvest, so you will want to apply it before you plant a new seed. It will also affect all subsequent harvests, so you can use it right before picking and get the next harvests more quickly.

**Salt Extraction**\- Instant recipe. These can be produced while other recipes are running, even if all slots are full.

*   4x Seaweed for 15x Salt
*   8x Old Bottle for 9x Salt
*   4x Crab for 3x Salt
*   2x Camel Bone for 1x Salt

**Fermented Bait**\- Each recipe takes 5 minutes. Using an Aged Fish (silver) yields 5 units of bait, while a Prime Aged Fish (gold) yields 10. Baits can be used for fishing in place of their listed composter bait, or traded on the Marketplace.

*   Capsule Bait- 1x Pickled Tomato or Zucchini + 1x Basic Aged Fish
    *   Fermented bait that “behaves like an Earthworm”
*   Umbrella Bait- 1x Pickled Broccoli or Pepper + 1x Advanced Aged Fish
    *   Fermented bait that “behaves like a Grub”
*   Crimson Baitfish- 1x Pickled Onion or Radish + 1x Expert Aged Fish
    *   Fermented bait that “behaves like a Red Wiggler”

**IMPORTANT:** All Aged Fish of the same quality are considered equal for purposes of making fermented bait, so there is absolutely no reason to use anything other than an Anchovy, Red Snapper, or Tuna, as they require the least Salt for making in the first place, and will give you the best value for your resources. If you have an Aged Fish of a higher XP value, eat it instead of making it into bait.

### Spice Rack

This process will use Salt and other resources to create some special items.

*   Refined Salt- 10x Salt
    *   Used in other recipes, and to upgrade the Salt Sculpture
*   Salt Lick- 5x Refined Salt
    *   Yields 5 units. Increase Animal produce by 5% over the next 3 harvests
*   Honey Treat- 5x Refined Salt + 5x Honey
    *   Yields 5 units. Reduces Animal feed requirements by 25% over the next 3 harvests

The Salt Lick and Honey Treat are fed to animals like normal feed, except you can use them while they are asleep or awake. You can only apply one or the other to a single animal, not both.

## Salt Skills

Fermentation and aging are so important that they get their own set of skills! Salt nodes are available on all island types except for the Tutorial Island, so these skills will be accessible to most players.

*   Tier 1
    *   Cheap Rakes- Reduces Coin cost of Salt Rakes by 20%
    *   Speedy Aging- Reduces fish aging time by 10%
    *   Salty Seas- Reduces time for Salt nodes to accumulate one charge by 10%
    *   Wide Rakes- +2 Salt per harvest
    *   Bacalhau- +1 Fermented Bait yield (bacalhau is the Portugese word for dried and salted codfish)
*   Tier 2
    *   Fish Smoking- Chance for a Prime Aged Fish increases from 10% to 20%. With a Level 2 Salt Sculpture, the total chance will be 24%, not 28%.
    *   Refiner- 15% chance to get +1 Refined Salt per recipe
    *   Sea Blessed- After harvesting Salt, 5% chance to add 1 charge to up to 4 non-full nodes
*   Tier 3
    *   Ager- All recipes in the Aging Shed take 2x the ingredients and output 2x the products
    *   Salt Surge- Power skill that adds maximum charges to all Salt nodes at once. (72 hour cooldown)

## Salt Sculpture

A new item crafted from the Boosts tab in the landscaping menu, the Salt Sculpture will provide passive boosts related to fermentation and aging. It will be the first upgradeable crafted item, requiring large amounts of resources to fully unlock its power.

It will cost 2000x Coins and 30x Refined Salt to craft initially, which grants the level 1 boost. The boosts are cumulative, meaning a level 6 sculpture will provide every boost listed.

*   Level 1: -5% salt charge replenishment time
    *   Upgrade Cost- 45x Refined Salt, 10x Capsule Bait
*   Level 2: +4% Prime Aging chance
    *   Upgrade Cost- 60x Refined Salt, 10x Capsule Bait, 10x Umbrella Bait, 500x Coins
*   Level 3: +1 max salt harvest cap (4 total)
    *   Upgrade Cost- 70x Refined Salt, 5x Greenhouse Glow, 5x Greenhouse Goodie, 1000x Coins
*   Level 4: -10% Salt Rake coin cost
    *   Upgrade Cost- 85x Refined Salt, 10x Sproutroot Surprise, 10x Turbofruit Mix, 1500x Coins
*   Level 5: “+5% Aging Rack speed” (This boost reduces the time of fish aging recipes by 5%)
    *   Upgrade Cost- 100x Refined Salt, 10x Crimson Baitfish, 2000x Salt, 2000x Coins
*   Level 6: +1 max salt harvest cap (5 total)
